title: Was Jordon Hudson at UNC game? Updates on Bill Belichick's girlfriend in Dublin for Week 0
description: Here's updates on whether Hudson made the trip overseas.
fullText:
Was Jordon Hudson at UNC game? Updates on Bill Belichick's girlfriend in Dublin for Week 0 originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

As North Carolina traveled to Dublin to play TCU in Week 0, Bill Belichick was hoping this season started better than his first.

The Tar Heels went just 4-8 in 2025 as Belichick led the team as head coach for the first time, proving that jumping from the NFL to college is not so easy. In the process, Belichick's personal life was a huge talking point throughout the season, largely focused on his girlfriend, Jordon Hudson.

The 25-year-old immediately made her mark as Belichick relied on her to help run many areas of his career, both within the program and on the public relations side. While she has taken a step out of the spotlight more this season, the upcoming college football year could thrust her back into national news.

While the Tar Heels started their season on a high note, claiming a 15-10 win overseas, it remained unclear whether Hudson made the trip. Here's what's known about her status at UNC's Week 0 win on Saturday.

MORE: Why Bill Belichick is on the hot seat entering 2026

3:30 p.m. - While UNC was able to hold on for a 15-10 win, opening 2026 with a win, Hudson was never spotted in Ireland by fans or broadcast cameras.

Regardless, the Tar Heels will return to the United States with some momentum as they open their new season under Belichick.

2:12 p.m. - All remains quiet still on the Hudson front. The ESPN broadcast has not focused on her at all today, and some viewers have noticed.

Any Jordon Hudson in Ireland sightings yet? pic.twitter.com/zVS1NpCTbS

12:25 p.m. - Still no screentime yet for Hudson. Fans on X, formerly Twitter, have begun asking about her status.

12:05 p.m. - The 2026 FBS season is underway! Belichick's squad will start today's game with possession. Still no news on whether Hudson made the trip to Dublin.

11:19 a.m. - With under an hour until kickoff, the college football world is still awaiting the news of whether or not Hudson made the trip to Ireland to watch her boyfriend try and coach the Tar Heels to a surprising win over the Horned Frogs.

Kickoff will commence at around 12 p.m. ET. Stay tuned for further updates on Hudson.

MORE: Ranking the 138 FBS coaches ahead of 2026

Bill Belichick has been dating Jordon Hudson for several years, and the 25-year-old has become a huge part of his life. The two were first publicly together in 2024, but some reports detailed that she may have been part of his life a few years prior to that.

When Belichick was first hired by North Carolina, Hudson frequently got into hot water for seemingly being too involved in the program and Belichick's life despite not initially being on the school's payroll. Several reports from the 2025 offseason detailed how Hudson took control of Belichick's public relations appearances and was looped into many of Belichick's decisions as a head coach.

As a result, she has become a central figure in North Carolina football as long as Belichick is leading the team. Therefore, during Tar Heels' games, Hudson's appearance on the North Carolina sidelines would surely draw eyeballs.

title: Final Colts 53-man roster projection before cutdown day

fullText:

Given what we've seen over the last month of practices and preseason action, here is one last projection of what the Colts' final roster will look like.

Daniel Jones, Riley Leonard, Anthony RichardsonQuarterbacks (3)

Daniel Jones, Riley Leonard, Anthony Richardson

As more time has gone by during training camp, it's seemed less and less likely that Richardson will be traded. He very well may have won the backup job.

Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan, DJ Giddens

I do like Bentley's ability to impact the passing game, but early in the preseason finale, it was Giddens on the field, perhaps giving us a glimpse into what the running back depth chart looks like for the RB3 role.

Alec Pierce, Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Ashton Dulin, Deion Burks, Laquon Treadwell

Treadwell has often been operating with the starters this summer, while Nick Westbrook-Ikhine was with the twos. Burks has also come on strong over the last week-plus of practices and games.

Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox, Drew Ogletree, Will Mallory

Mallory's surge in the passing game this summer secured his roster spot.

Bernhard Raimann, Quenton Nelson, Tanor Bortolini, Matt Goncalves, Jalen Travis, Jalen Farmer, Dalton Tucker, Luke Tenuta, Blake Freeland

This is very much a position that the Colts could make a waiver claim, with there being shaky play from the depth of this position group in camp. But for now, this appears to be the top nine players on the roster.

Laiatu Latu, Arden Key, Jaylahn Tuimoloau, Micheal Clemons, George Gumbs, Caden Curry, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, Colby Wooden, Adetomiwa Adebawore

Curry and Gumbs each earned their roster spots this summer, while I didn't see enough from Jerry Tillery or Derrick Nnadi at defensive tackle.

CJ Allen, Bryce Boettcher, Akeem Davis-Gaither, Jaylon Carlies, Austin Ajiake

There was a lot of rotating this summer to determine who would start and fill the backup roles, but it's been pretty clear all along that this group of five would make up the linebacker room on the initial roster.

Charvarius Ward, Sauce Gardner, Justin Walley, Johnathan Edwards, Cam Taylor-Britt

Ideally, the Colts keep a sixth cornerback, but the depth of this unit isn't strong enough to justify that. Rob Carter Jr. and Jaylon Jones both struggled.

Cam Bynum, AJ Haulcy, Hunter Wohler, Jonathan Owens, Juanyeh Thomas

Rigoberto Sanchez, Luke Rhodes, Spencer Shrader

Shrader won this job with his terrific performance in the preseason games.

title: Giants acquire defensive lineman CJ Okoye from the Ravens for a 2028 seventh-round pick
description: Taking another step to improve their defensive-line situation, the New York Giants acquired CJ Okoye in a trade with the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday.  Coach John Harbaugh confirmed the Giants sent a 2028 seventh-round pick to his old team for the 24-year-old from Nigeria.  “We see him as an inside defender, defensive tackle, A-gap, B-gap player, run stopper, pocket pusher, in terms of the pass game, and just a real big, physical player,” Harbaugh said on a video call with reporters.
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Taking another step to improve their defensive-line situation, the New York Giants acquired CJ Okoye in a trade with the Baltimore Ravens on Saturday.

Coach John Harbaugh confirmed the Giants sent a 2028 seventh-round pick to his old team for the 24-year-old from Nigeria.

"We see him as an inside defender, defensive tackle, A-gap, B-gap player, run stopper, pocket pusher, in terms of the pass game, and just a real big, physical player," Harbaugh said on a video call with reporters. "A type of guy we've been looking for, and we're really excited to get him up here."

Okoye is the team's latest addition in an offseason of change at the position since trading Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati for the 10th pick in the draft. New York, which ranked second-worst against the run last season, also signed veteran defensive tackles D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris.

After spending time with brother Jim Harbaugh's Los Angeles Chargers out of the NFL's International Pathway Program, Okoye joined John and the Ravens and made 15 tackles in 13 games last season in his first action in the league.

"A guy who had been a developmental type guy learning the game," John Harbaugh said. "Tremendous physical skills, hard worker, has really dedicated himself over the last few years to learning the game, really, because he didn't play it growing up and made great strides."

It is the third trade by the Giants over the past two weeks. They got a sixth-rounder next year from Jacksonville for guard Daniel Faalele and a '28 seventh from Kansas City for fellow offensive lineman Josh Ezeudu.

In the aftermath of saying Odell Beckham Jr. had done enough to make a roster following the preseason finale against the Jets on Friday night, Harbaugh was not yet willing to confirm that the 33-year-old receiver is making the Giants' initial 53-man group. All teams need to be down to that number by 6 p.m. ET Sunday.

"We'll have to see throughout the weekend if he does make the roster," Harbaugh said. "We're working through that right now. We have a pretty good idea in all honesty, but we're not ready to make that announcement or any other announcement as far as who's making the team at this point."

Beckham made seven catches for 76 yards over three exhibition games and got better as training camp progressed. Beckham looked to be on the bubble, though Calvin Austin's season-ending knee injury opened up a spot.

title: Notre Dame QB commit goes off Friday night, scores 6 total touchdowns
description: Notre Dame football’s 2027 quarterback commit, Wonderful ‘Champ’ Monds had a monster game on Friday night, accounting for six touchdowns.
fullText:
Notre Dame football didn't get its first choice at quarterback in the 2027 recruiting cycle, but it found one that is starting to look like he'll be the guy.

After missing out on a few higher ranked prospects, the Irish ultimately landed Florida's Wonderful 'Champ' Monds in early May. The 6-foot, 2-inch and 224-pounder is currently ranked as the No. 255 overall prospect in the 247Sport composite, but if he continues to have games like he did on Friday night, his ranking will surely rise.

Monds was an absolute menace with his arm and legs, completing 80% of his passes for 396-yards and 4 touchdowns, while accounting for another two scores on the ground. Through two games, he's completed 82.5% of his attempts with seven touchdowns while rushing for another four.

If Monds continues to show this kind of improvement, it's looking like another great Notre Dame recruiting find from a player who isn't as highly ranked as others. It will be fun to watch his progression over the remainder of the season.

title: Olympic Sprinter Marvin Bracy-Williams Arrested on DUI Charge Months After 12-Year USADA Ban
description: Former Olympic sprinter Marvin Bracy-Williams was arrested on a DUI charge in Orlando, Florida, on Aug. 3, adding a new legal issue to a year ... Read More
fullText:
Former Olympic sprinter Marvin Bracy-Williams was arrested on a DUI charge in Orlando, Florida, on Aug. 3, adding a new legal issue to a year already marked by a lengthy anti-doping sanction and his notice of retirement.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ Sports, the arrest followed a roadside encounter after Bracy-Williams' vehicle ended up in a ditch and a tow truck driver requested law enforcement at the scene.

TMZ reported the arrest on Aug. 28. The outlet's report did not identify a blood-alcohol result or a final disposition in the case, and an arrest does not establish guilt.

The case surfaced less than three months after the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency imposed a 12-year period of ineligibility on Bracy-Williams for his third anti-doping rule violation. He notified USADA of his intent to retire on the same day that sanction was announced.

The tow truck driver told officers that he came upon Bracy-Williams' vehicle and found the athlete apparently passed out in the driver's seat while the engine was running and the vehicle was still in gear, according to TMZ's account of the court documents. By the time police arrived, the tow truck was pulling the vehicle from the ditch.

The driver told police that he contacted his employer and requested law enforcement because he believed Bracy-Williams was intoxicated. An officer reported smelling alcohol and said Bracy-Williams performed poorly during field sobriety testing before he was taken into custody on the DUI charge.

Bracy-Williams was already serving a 45-month anti-doping sanction when USADA announced another 12-year period of ineligibility on June 5. The latest violation stemmed from three whereabouts failures recorded on July 1, 2025, Feb. 24, 2026, and April 1, 2026.

Three whereabouts failures within a 12-month period constitute an anti-doping rule violation. USADA said a first whereabouts violation ordinarily carries a one- to two-year period of ineligibility, but because this was Bracy-Williams' third anti-doping rule violation, he faced an increased range of eight years to a lifetime ban. The agency determined that 12 years was appropriate under the circumstances.

His earlier 45-month sanction was announced in November 2025 after a USADA investigation involving testosterone use, attempted tampering and a separate whereabouts violation. USADA said Bracy-Williams admitted his violations and provided substantial assistance, resulting in significant reductions to part of the sanction he otherwise faced. A 24-month penalty for the earlier whereabouts violation was then added to the reduced 21-month sanction for the testosterone and tampering violations, bringing the total to 45 months.

The newer 12-year sanction is required to run consecutively after his previous period of ineligibility. Because Bracy-Williams notified USADA of his intent to retire on June 5, the agency said his remaining period of ineligibility will continue indefinitely until he returns from retirement and serves the remainder of his sanctions.

Bracy-Williams returned to competition outside the traditional World Athletics system shortly before the latest sanction. Enhanced announced in January that he would join its sprint field while he was still serving his previous USADA suspension, and he went on to finish third in the men's 100 meters at the inaugural Enhanced Games in Las Vegas in May, a result also noted by the New York Post.

The Enhanced Games permits athletes to use performance-enhancing substances that are prohibited in traditional sanctioned competition under its own competition framework. The event has positioned that policy as a defining difference from organizations operating under the World Anti-Doping Code.

USADA's June ruling also disqualified Bracy-Williams from competitive results on and after April 1, 2026, with the agency stating that applicable medals, points and prizes are subject to forfeiture.

Four years before the latest legal and anti-doping developments, Bracy-Williams entered the 2022 World Athletics Championships in Eugene as one of the leading American sprinters. He won his opening 100-meter heat in 10.05 seconds and advanced through the rounds to the final.

Bracy-Williams crossed the line in 9.88 seconds in the final, taking silver behind Fred Kerley's 9.86 as the United States swept all three medals. Trayvon Bromell also ran 9.88 and took bronze.

Bracy-Williams earned another silver as part of the U.S. men's 4x100-meter relay team at those championships. He had previously represented the United States at the 2016 Rio Olympics, advancing to the 100-meter semifinals.

title: Josh Dobbs rolls as Lions backup QB in preseason win over Colts
description: Detroit Lions preseason score: Backup QB Josh Dobbs passed for two TDs and moved the offense efficiently in the first half in Indianapolis.
fullText:
INDIANAPOLIS – The Detroit Lions' backup quarterback situation might not be as dire as it appeared.

Josh Dobbs had a strong showing in the Lions' preseason finale Saturday, Aug. 29, completing 15 of 19 passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in a 25-16 win over the Indianapolis Colts to stake claim to the backup job behind Jared Goff.

Dobbs signed with the Lions in early August and worked mostly as the third quarterback behind Goff and undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer this summer. He lost a fumble and threw an interception on back-to-back possessions to start last week's win over the Washington Commanders, but was sharp and in command of the offense Saturday.

RELIVE THE ACTION: What happened in Indy?

Altmyer started and threw an interception on his third pass attempt while playing against the Colts' first-team defense, while Dobbs led two touchdown drives – he converted three third downs and a fourth down on the first and ran a flawless two-minute drive on the second – in the second quarter against Indianapolis' backups.

A veteran in his 10th NFL season and playing for his ninth team, Dobbs has previous experience with the Lions (2-1) – he was on the practice squad briefly in 2022 – and with Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing (who he played for in stops with the Cleveland Browns and Arizona Cardinals).

The Lions have long employed veteran backups behind Goff, and Lions coach Dan Campbell admitted this week that was still his preference.

Altmyer, though, played well enough in moments this summer that he still was in the mix for a roster spot, and there was some thought the Lions could look outside the organization for a backup.

Altmyer played the first and most of the third quarters and finished 7 of 11 passing for 55 yards with two turnovers against the Colts (0-2-1). Along with his first-quarter interception, he lost a fumble on a sack on the opening drive of the third quarter. He led one touchdown drive on his second possession, when running back Trayveon Williams scored on a 1-yard run.

Dobbs also led a touchdown drive in the fourth quarter.

Dobbs could easily be the player of the game, but I'm going with Saylors, who accomplished the rare feat of rushing for 100 yards in a preseason game.

Like Dobbs, Saylors seemed pretty secure in his roster spot entering Saturday and likely cemented his role with his play. He had three runs of 16-plus yards, was solid in pass protection and averaged 5.9 yards on his 17 carries.

If Isiah Pacheco misses time with his back injury to star the season, Saylors should be Jahmyr Gibbs' top backup.

Gill-Howard put a cherry atop his nice summer as a sixth-round pick with a sack, two quarterback hits and a couple hustle plays Saturday. He split two blockers for his sack on a third-and-5 play in the first quarter and made one tackle when he got cut block on a screen pass popped to his feet and chased the receiver down from behind. He should be a roster lock.

Bates has had an odd summer, meanwhile. He changed how he sets up for field goals this offseason and had some stretches where he missed several makeable kicks in camp. On Saturday, he missed two extra points wide right and also left a kickoff short of the landing zone. He'll be the Lions' kicker this fall, but I wouldn't feel too comfortable sending him out there for a game-winner right now.

A wide reciever-turned-tight end, Meeks wasn't bad Saturday. He caught two passes, including a touchdown with a linebacker bearing down on him on the goal line. But his limitations as a blocker were apparent as he missed a block on run plays by Saylors and Williams and appeared to miss a blitz pickup on a screen. Meeks has had a nice camp overall. He forced a fumble last week and had a team-high five catches entering the game. But as the clear No. 4 tight end, there might not be room for him on the 53.

I'll wait for some clarification from Campbell on why he divvied up the snaps the way he did, but I found it interesting that I did not see backup center Seth McLaughlin or Tom Kennedy, who's fighting for the No. 5 receiver job, play Saturday, while presumed starting defensive end Tyler Lacy played into the fourth quarter. Lacy is more of a situational big end than your typical every-down starter, but on a day when every other projected starter and several top backups did not play, it was odd to see him on the field. Levi Onwuzurike, who also is in the mix for a backup job on the defensive line, also played into the second half.

The next time you see the Lions on the field it will be for the regular-season opener against the New Orleans Saints on Sept. 13 (1 p.m., Fox). There's work to do before then, though, as the Lions have to cut their roster to the 53-man limit by 6 p.m. Sunday, Aug. 30.

Lions general manager Brad Holmes has traditionally cut to fewer than 53 players with plans on filling the open spot(s) on the waiver wire. The Lions have enough good roster candidates they might not want to do that this year, but they also could be looking outside the organization for backups at running back, on the interior offensive line and in the defensive secondary.

Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com. Follow him on Bluesky, X and Instagram at @davebirkett.

title: Warrington retain top-two hopes with win at Hull FC
description: Warrington hold off a spirited late Hull FC fightback to secure their sixth successive win and keep a top-two finish in Super League in sight.
fullText:
Tries: O'Neill, Briscoe Goals: Sezer 3

Tries: Hayes, Ashton, Thewlis Goals: Williams 2

Warrington Wolves held off a spirited late Hull FC fightback to secure their sixth successive win and retain their hopes of a top-two finish in Super League.

With the scores tied at 2-2 heading into the final five minutes of the first half, errors in defence allowed the away side to score back-to-back tries through Leon Hayes and Matty Ashton.

Josh Thewlis extended Wire's lead with the home side down to 12 men after Ligi Sao was sin-binned for a high shot on Ashton.

Ethan O'Neill crossed for the home side's first try and Tom Briscoe, making his final home appearance for Hull before retiring, quickly got a second to cut Warrington's lead to just two points, but the third-placed visitors held out to move two points behind Leeds Rhinos and Wigan Warriors.

The tone for what was at times an attritional encounter played in wet conditions in East Yorkshire was set in the opening minute when the home side had James Batchelor sin-binned for a tackle on Arron Lindop, who subsequently failed a head injury assessment.

Warrington captain George Williams kicked the away side into the lead after 18 minutes before Aidan Sezer made it 2-2 from a Hull penalty shortly afterwards.

It looked like that was how the half would end but the home side, who have now lost 18 of their 25 Super League matches this year, then produced two errors under high kicks in three minutes that were both punished by Sam Burgess' men as Hayes and Ashton went over.

Thewlis' score ten minutes into the second half seemed to have put the game out of reach of Hull before the home side surprisingly rallied with 15 minutes to go.

O'Neill went over on Hull's left before the retiring Briscoe scored the 233rd try of his illustrious career.

The Black and Whites pushed for another score but Warrington held out, while the home side were perhaps lucky to end the game with 13 men on the field with Sao involved in further incidents after his sin-binning.

The Wolves head to fourth-placed Wakefield next Saturday, with Hull travelling to Toulouse Olympique on Friday.

Interchanges: Kemp, Lisone, Romano, Sao.

Sin-bin: Batchelor (1), Sao (45).

Warrington: Thewlis, Hopoate, Lindop, King, Ashton, Williams, Hayes, Byrne, Walker, Harrison, Bentley, Stone, Currie.

Interchanges: Powell, Wood, Philbin, Thomas, Crowther.

fullText:
A 2025 draft pick is among the Ravens' cuts as they move toward a 53-man roster.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the Ravens have waived cornerback Robert Longerbeam. The Ravens selected Longerbeam in the sixth round last year.

Longerbeam did not appear in any games during his rookie season and spent the year on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury in the summer. He had 11 tackles in three preseason games this summer.

title: “I will never forget this day” – Demichelis delighted after winning Bundesliga debut as RB Leipzig coach
description: Martin Demichelis could hardly have wished for a better start to the Bundesliga season, as he led RB Leipzig to a 3-0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach in his first league game in charge on Saturday....
fullText:
Martin Demichelis could hardly have wished for a better start to the Bundesliga season, as he led RB Leipzig to a 3-0 win over Borussia Mönchengladbach in his first league game in charge on Saturday.

"I will never forget this day. The fans' choreography, such a performance, three points, three goals – everything went really well. Compliments to the boys and to all the staff," Demichelis said in a post-match interview, according to RBLive.de.

Ridle Baku's first-half goal gave Leipzig a one-goal lead at the break, before Antonio Nusa and Rocco Reitz wrapped up a convincing victory in the second half.

"Except for the final 15 minutes, we consistently played forward and had the game under control. The first half was difficult; the opponent made it hard for us and, in certain phases, we lacked control without the ball," Demichelis said.

"We created a lot of chances and scored the first goal. After that, we dominated the game and had better structure both in possession and without the ball.

"We came out aggressively in the second half and played forward. There were a lot of good things in our performance."

title: JJ McCarthy, Vikings rumors start: Should Browns be interested if waived or cheap trade?
description: The Cleveland Browns QB room is pretty full, but would former 1st round pick J.J. McCarthy be worth the addition?
fullText:
If you have four quarterbacks, you probably have none, or are the luckiest/best team in the NFL. The Cleveland Browns head into their initial 53-man roster decisions not knowing how many quarterbacks they will keep after starter Deshaun Watson. At this point, it feels as likely that all three of Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and Taylen Green are on that roster as not.

Few believe the Browns long-term answer is currently on the roster.

The Minnesota Vikings had hoped they had solved their quarterback need when they drafted JJ McCarthy with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. The team was so confident that they let QB Sam Darnold leave in free agency to hand the keys over to McCarthy.

So far, that has gone so poorly that the Vikings signed Kyler Murray and gave him the starting job early and camp, and now reports are that McCarthy may not even make the initial 53-man roster in Minnesota:

O'Connell gave him the day off Wednesday so that he could rest up enough to start Friday's final preseason matchup with the Broncos. But McCarthy did not play. Wentz started and appears to be in line to be the team's backup. McCarthy's comfort (or lack thereof) with being QB3 could dictate his future in Minnesota.

That report from The Athletic fits what we heard from Vikings fans over at The Daily Norseman, who were talking about a McCarthy-for-Sanders trade earlier this week:

McCarthy played 10 games last season, after missing his entire rookie year due to a knee injury. With the former Michigan Wolverine as a starter, Minnesota was 6-4, but McCarthy only completed 58% of his passes for 1,632 yards with 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

More than one in the Vikings media believes that McCarthy will not have a chance to add to those numbers:

Tomorrow likely ends JJ McCarthy’s time in Minnesota. Worse than getting nothing from the 2023 1.10, the team doubled down on him when they chose to let Sam Darnold walk. A brutal series of decisions with franchise-changing ramifications. https://t.co/GQocKJ42uO

The NFL has seen some resurgence of first-round picks in recent years, including Darnold, Baker Mayfield, and even Mac Jones, to a lesser extent. Could McCarthy, who most feel was overdrafted by a couple of rounds, be the next to join that list after getting a fresh start somewhere? Should Cleveland have interest in being the spot where he gets that fresh start?

Do you think the Browns should make a cheap trade of McCarthy, claim him if he's waived, or stay far away from the former 1st-round pick?

title: Report:MRavens release rookie center Nick Dawkins during roster cuts
description: The Ravens released undrafted rookie Nick Dawkins as Baltimore continued settling its center competition and offensive-line depth chart.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens have released undrafted rookie center Nick Dawkins while trimming their roster, according to Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun.

Dawkins signed with Baltimore after going undrafted out of Penn State in April. The 6-foot-4, 305-pound lineman entered training camp with an opportunity to compete at center after Tyler Linderbaum departed for the Las Vegas Raiders in free agency.

The Ravens eventually added veteran Ethan Pocic to the competition, while Danny Pinter and Jovaughn Gwyn also received opportunities. Pinter's season-ending patellar tendon injury appeared to improve Dawkins' chances of remaining with the organization, but Baltimore still had several interior offensive linemen capable of playing center.

Dawkins brought extensive experience and leadership credentials from Penn State. He was a two-time team captain and won the 2024 Wuerffel Trophy, which recognizes community service and leadership. He also arrived in Baltimore with familiarity alongside first-round guard Vega Ioane, his former college teammate.

His release suggests the Ravens are comfortable moving forward with Pocic and Gwyn as their primary center options, or that they believe other interior linemen can provide emergency flexibility. It also removes another player from a crowded offensive-line roster competition.

Dawkins must pass through waivers before becoming a free agent. If he goes unclaimed, he would make sense as a practice-squad candidate because of his experience, leadership and familiarity with Baltimore's blocking system. The Ravens could continue to develop him without using one of their initial 53-man roster spots.

title: Yankees sign former Mets top prospect Jarred Kelenic to minor-league deal
description: Kelenic played for the White Sox and Rangers earlier this season before being designated for assignment.
fullText:
The New York Yankees need outfield help with Aaron Judge's return still uncertain. They're looking to a former top major-league prospect for a possible contribution, one who also hopes he can revive his career with a postseason contender.

The Yankees have signed outfielder Jarred Kelenic to a minor-league deal, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reports. He will report to the team's Triple-A affiliate in Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, the team announced on Saturday.

Kelenic, 27, was designated for assignment by the Texas Rangers last week. He compiled a .373/.447/.655 with their Triple-A affiliate and slashed .200/.333/.200 in 17 games with the major-league team.

Additionally, Kelenic spent time with the Chicago White Sox this season. He had a .202/.346/.464 slash line with their Triple-A club and hit .226 with a .626 OPS in 19 big-league games.

JARRED KELENIC CALLS BALLGAME! pic.twitter.com/oh6tjno0n1

Kelenic was originally the 2018 first-round pick (No. 6 overall) by the New York Mets out of Waukesha West High School in Wisconsin. He was traded to the Seattle Mariners later that year with four other players in exchange for Robinson Canó and Edwin Díaz.

After three disappointing seasons with a .204 average and .656 OPS, the Mariners traded Kelenic to the Atlanta Braves. But the former top prospect still didn't fulfill his potential with the Braves (.222, .660 OPS) and opted for free agency rather than go to the minors after the 2025 campaign.

A left-handed hitter who can play all three outfield positions, Kelenic could possibly provide depth on the Yankees roster behind Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham and Spencer Jones. (And Judge, if he's able to return.) Jasson Domínguez and Yanquiel Fernández will likely be in the outfield mix as well.

Judge is "closer" to returning from his right rib stress fracture and could soon begin hitting off a high-velocity machine. If that goes well, the reigning American League MVP doesn't want to go on a minor-league rehab assignment, but be activated to the major-league roster right away.

"Why waste at-bats?" Judge said to reporters on Thursday. Yankees manager Aaron Boone said that decision will be made by the organization.

Without Judge, the Yankees have hit a collective .219 with a .674 OPS and scored 292 runs since June 1. During the first two months of the season, they scored 305 runs.

title: Interview: Why versatility is the key to Polish forward Lila Banaszak’s basketball career
description: Swish Appeal interviews Polish national team member and pro Lila Banaszak about her basketball career and more.
fullText:
Lila Banaszak is a 26-year-old and 6-foot-1 forward who plays for the Polish national team and Flammes Carolo Basket in France. She's also played professionally in Egypt and Spain.

Naturally strong, Lila is capable of playing multiple positions, demonstrating a willingness to do whatever is necessary for her team to win.

Banaszak recently spoke to Swish Appeal about being a pro, traveling and switching teams while having a dog, playing against adults while still in high school and maybe one day joining the WNBA. Here are a few highlight from our conversation:

I think the school is not that popular now. People have had their own ways to be successful and build careers, but in my day that was the only basketball school we had. It was ran by the national federation and had good coaches, who could spend time with you on individual skills.

For me, being from a small city, there was no other way to get better than going to this kind of school and, to be honest, I never expected that I'd be going there because I didn't even know about it. Basketball was never a thing for me until they invited me. When they sent a [recruitment] letter to my family, I was on the national under-15 team.

We woke up before 7 a.m., had breakfast and at 7:15 a.m. we already had some classes. Then we had practice, then lunch, then classes and then practice. From 7 a.m. till 8, sometimes 9 p.m., we were working, [constantly] doing stuff. In some evenings you had maybe one, two hours to study or take care of yourself, and that was it.

There were not a lot of fans in attendance, but our games were on public TV and I know that a lot of people were watching our games. It was thousands of people. I think it's about the culture. They don't have much money to attend games, so people don't come to the arenas but they watch them on TV.

This allows [women's basketball] to be everywhere. The level of basketball is hard to describe because when you go there. There's no organization, there's nothing. But at the same time, those girls know how to play basketball.

A special thank you to Tomasz Matyskiewicz of SPORTFORUM Agency for arranging the interview.

title: UFC Fighters React To Song Yadong’s Improbable Shanghai Win

Yadong’s knockout surprise was stunning in more than one way. First, the actual knockout itself was incredible. Song timed a perfectly-placed right […]
fullText:
Some of the most skilled UFC fighters in the world were left in shock by Song Yadong's incredible upset knockout over Umar Nurmagomedov earlier today in UFC Shanghai's main event (full results HERE).

Yadong's knockout surprise was stunning in more than one way. First, the actual knockout itself was incredible. Song timed a perfectly-placed right uppercut as Nurmagomedov dipped his head to the left during a level change. Nurmagomedov has shown a tendency to do this throughout his UFC tenure and Yadong (alongside coach Urijah Faber) took full advantage of it. The fact that Nurmagomedov dropped like a sack of potatoes made the finish even more spectacular.

Adding to the fight itself were the betting odds associated with the UFC Shanghai main event. Yadong was not expected to win this weekend against a fighter in Nurmagomedov who many consider to be championship level. Fans haven't seen Song take that step up in his career yet so there was some hesitation to trust he could get it done. Needless to say, Yadong spoiled a lot of betting slips early Saturday as he flipped the script on Nurmagomedov's anticipated victory.

On top of that, Yadong was fighting on his home soil in China. Yadong fought in Macau this past May as well, but before that he hadn't competed at home since all the way back in 2018. Chinese fight fans had another chance to see Song perform and they made sure it counted. The atmosphere was absolutely electric, which created an unforgettable scene after Yadong finished Nurmagomedov.

The MMA community was left in shock and awe as they had witnessed one of the biggest upsets of the year and one of the biggest upsets in recent UFC bantamweight history. Some of the biggest names in the sport, including former UFC champions Sean O'Malley, Aljamain Sterling, Belal Muhammad, Merab Dvalishvili and Daniel Cormier, took to social media to share their reactions. Not to mention Nurmagomedov's friend, long-time teammate, and current UFC welterweight champion, Islam Makhachev.

Check it out below and let us know your final thoughts!

Although competition for places remains strong, Lewis-Skelly has already shown that he can perform for the team and will have opportunities to establish himself further.

His performances this season have strengthened his case to remain part of the squad, despite the number of experienced players Arsenal have available in the positions he can play.

The Gunners therefore appear determined to keep him rather than allow him to leave at this late stage of the transfer window.

Lewis-Skelly can now focus on continuing his performances and taking advantage of the opportunities that come his way as Arsenal look to achieve their targets this season.

title: Red Sox Answer Offensive Drought With Statement Shutout Win Over Yankees
description: The Red Sox ended their offensive drought early before their pitching staff completely silenced the Yankees in a much-needed bounce-back victory.
fullText:
Red Sox Answer Offensive Drought With Statement Shutout Win Over Yankees originally appeared on NESN. 

The Boston Red Sox finally broke through at the plate Saturday afternoon. Once they did, their pitching staff made certain the New York Yankees never had an opportunity to respond.

Boston bounced back from consecutive shutout losses with a 6-0 win over New York in the first game of Saturday's doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. Wilyer Abreu ended the Red Sox's scoreless drought in the opening inning, launching a two-out solo home run off Yankees starter Carlos Rodón. It was Abreu's 23rd homer of the season and gave Boston its first run since Wednesday.

That one swing ultimately provided more than enough support for Hunter Bennett and the Red Sox bullpen.

Bennett delivered six scoreless innings, allowing only three hits without issuing a walk. He struck out seven and threw 59 of his 83 pitches for strikes, producing a game score of 73. New York never sent more than four batters to the plate in any inning against Bennett. Its best opportunity came in the fourth when Heliot Ramos doubled, but Ceddanne Rafaela threw out Amed Rosario at home plate to preserve the shutout.

It was exactly the type of response Boston needed after its offense disappeared in consecutive losses.

The Red Sox entered Saturday looking for something positive after suffering back-to-back shutouts, including a 1-0 loss to the Yankees in Friday's series opener.

Shut ‘em out.

FINAL: #RedSox 6, Yankees 0#DirtyWater￼ pic.twitter.com/6GivFTAXpu

Abreu immediately removed the possibility of another scoreless afternoon, but Boston's pitching staff remained the biggest story. Bennett retired the final six batters he faced before handing the game to the bullpen. Tayron Guerrero worked around a seventh-inning single, Garrett Whitlock pitched a perfect eighth and Jovani Morán closed the game.

The four Boston pitchers combined to allow four hits and no walks while striking out nine.

Boston added its second run in the fifth when Adley Rutschman scored on a passed ball. The Red Sox then turned a close game into a comfortable victory with four runs in the ninth.

Andruw Monasterio drove home Caleb Durbin and Rutschman with a single. Nick Sogard followed with an RBI double before Rafaela completed the scoring with a run-producing single. Rutschman finished 3-for-4 with two runs, while Sogard went 2-for-4 with a double, an RBI and a run scored. Boston collected nine hits and went 3-for-8 with runners in scoring position.

The victory improved the Red Sox to 74-61 and pulled them within two games of the Yankees, who dropped to 76-59. It also evened the four-game series at one win apiece.

MORE:  Red Sox Get Major Bullpen Boost Before Doubleheader Against Yankees

Boston will not have much time to celebrate. The Red Sox and Yankees return to the field Saturday night for the second half of their doubleheader. First pitch is scheduled for 6:15 p.m. ET at Yankee Stadium, with the game airing nationally on FOX.

After being shut out twice, Boston now has a chance to leave Saturday with two wins and make the American League East race significantly more interesting.

title: ‘That’s Special’ — Ben Roethlisberger Predicts Germie Bernard Will Bring Big-Time Excitement to Steelers
description: Germie Bernard did not need a huge workload to make a huge impression. fullText:
Germie Bernard did not need a huge workload to make a huge impression. One play in the Pittsburgh Steelers' preseason finale was enough to show the exact traits Ben Roethlisberger believes that can make the rookie a problem for defenses this season.

Bernard turned a short-field opportunity into his first preseason touchdown on Thursday, Aug. 27, and Roethlisberger took notice. The Steelers legend pointed to Bernard's quickness, tackle-breaking ability and explosiveness as reasons the Steelers fans should be excited.

Roethlisberger's prediction comes after Bernard made his biggest preseason splash yet. Following the Buffalo Bills muffed punt, the Steelers took possession at the Bills' 13-yard line. Will Howard immediately found Bernard on the right side, and the rookie broke a tackle before racing into the end zone for a 13-yard touchdown.

The play itself was simple. That burst is exactly what Roethlisberger sees translating to the regular season. The former Steelers quarterback believes Bernard has the combination of shiftiness, speed and contact balance to turn relatively modest opportunities into explosive plays.

"Let's talk about Germie Bernard. That's special. That's what I think you're gonna see from him this year, and I think that should excite a lot of people, because of what he has and that potential for the shifty, break a tackle, fast enough, quick enough, get in the end zone. There's gonna be a lot of excitement there."

Ben Roethlisberger believes Germie Bernard will bring a lot of excitement to the Steelers this year: “Let’s talk about Germie Bernard. That’s special. That’s what I think you’re gonna see from him this year, and I think that should excite a lot of people, because of what he has…

— Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) August 29, 2026

That endorsement carries some weight because Bernard is not entering the Steelers receiver room as a finished product. He is a rookie who still has to carve out his role; however, the second-round pick has already shown enough flashes to make the Steelers curious about how much they can put on his plate.

And that touchdown highlighted a particularly useful skill set. Bernard did not need a perfectly designed deep shot to make an impact. He caught the ball underneath, created separation, absorbed contact, and finished the play. That kind of juice can give an offense another dimension.

The timing also matters. The Steelers' preseason finale was Bernard's final opportunity to make an impression before the regular-season roster takes shape. One reception may not tell the entire story, but the way he created the touchdown gave the coaching staff another reason to trust his playmaking ability.

Roethlisberger also believes Bernard has enough physical talent to become a genuine source of excitement rather than merely a rotational rookie. If that prediction hits, Pittsburgh could have another young weapon capable of changing a drive with one touch.

For now, Bernard still has to earn those opportunities; however, after one explosive touchdown and a strong endorsement from one of the franchise's biggest names, the rookie has given Steelers fans plenty to watch for when the real games begin.

title: Steelers Make Swift Decision on 11 Players as 53-Man Deadline Nears
description: Pittsburgh’s preseason ended in heartbreak Thursday night, as the Buffalo Bills scored late to beat the Steelers 28-27 at Highmark Stadium. fullText:
Pittsburgh's preseason ended in heartbreak Thursday night, as the Buffalo Bills scored late to beat the Steelers 28-27 at Highmark Stadium. Head coach Mike McCarthy watched his roster compete one final time before decision day arrived.

The Pittsburgh Steelers released 11 players Friday, their first move in what will be a busy weekend of roster decisions. The team must reach the 53-man limit, and multiple reports indicate the front office has until Sunday at 8 p.m. ET to finish the job.

The August 28 list included tight end Jaheim Bell, offensive linemen Greg Crippen and Jaylon Guilbeau, and defensive backs Jack Henderson, Brandon Hill and Daryl Porter. Wide receivers Jakobie Keeney-James, Tamon Lynum, Cornell Powell and Isaiah Winstead were also let go, along with running back Alex Tecza.

Several of the released players were recent additions, some signed only days earlier as undrafted free agents or free-agent pickups brought in to fill out camp bodies. McCarthy noted the preseason gave his staff useful evaluation chances and said the coaching staff would use the next day or two to finalize the roster before turning attention to the season opener.

This marks only the first round of cuts. More decisions are still needed before Pittsburgh reaches the required 53-man limit, and the next moves could touch far more prominent names on the depth chart.

The next question facing McCarthy might be the trickiest one of the offseason.

Pittsburgh's roster crunch is complicated by an unusual situation at quarterback. McCarthy has indicated the team plans to carry four passers into the season: starter Aaron Rodgers, veteran backup Mason Rudolph, and two younger arms in Drew Allar and Will Howard, who could shuffle between the active roster and the practice squad.

Preseason numbers slightly favored Allar, who posted a better rating and avoided interceptions, though Howard was viewed as the more accurate passer overall. Carrying four quarterbacks is rare across the league and would likely force Pittsburgh to make cuts elsewhere to fit everyone on the roster.

Rodgers has said there is "zero debate" about playing beyond this season, framing 2026 as his farewell tour after agreeing to a one-year extension back in May. How the Steelers balance that quarterback competition with roster limits will be one of the more interesting subplots of cutdown weekend.

Pittsburgh now sits at 80 players with one more round of cuts required before Sunday's deadline. The Steelers open their regular season against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1, and how this weekend's decisions shake out will go a long way toward shaping that matchup.
