title: Haidt's Moment
description: Plus: The scourge of scromiting, blaming air traffic control, and more...
fullText:
Was Jonathan Haidt right all along? Readers of this newsletter—and writers at Reason—are surely divided on this one. On Wednesday of this week, news broke that Meta had reached a humongous $17.1 billion settlement with 47 states and the District of Columbia, forced to pay damages due to child-endangerment claims stemming from its social media algorithms and platforms.

"The owner of Facebook and Instagram agreed to the financial penalties for violating federal child privacy and states' consumer protection laws, the states announced," reports The New York Times. "Meta also agreed to limit how long teenagers can spend on its platforms and to bans on features that stoke mental health issues, striking at the heart of the company's business of engagement for advertising."

"The settlement effectively ends a bellwether federal trial in the U.S. Northern District of California in Oakland, where California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey were seeking roughly $200 billion over accusations that Meta harmed children," adds the Times. Meta, the owner of Instagram and Facebook, at times invoked a Section 230 defense, the "First Amendment of the internet" that makes it so companies don't bear liability for the posts of their users—which Reason has repeatedly defended amid a media landscape that doesn't seem to understand the value of Section 230.

"After years of being barred from suing social platforms, state prosecutors have gotten creative," wrote Reason's Elizabeth Nolan Brown earlier this month about the California/Colorado/Kentucky/New Jersey suit. "They're now claiming that this isn't about user-generated speech but about tech companies' product design. In this case, the states claim that providing photo filters is contributing to teens' body dysmorphia and that 'psychologically manipulative' features like displaying post 'like' counts, sending notifications, and using algorithms to curate content around a user's particular interests are what's keeping kids hooked, not the actual content on Facebook and Instagram. It's a silly claim, since clearly there could be no 'addiction' to social media if not for the content or communications contained on these platforms."

"The attorneys general and plaintiffs say that Meta's algorithms trap its users in the infinite scroll, hours of time spent staring at half-naked influencers or malnourished celebrities, images that breed body dysmorphia, anxiety and depression," reads a different Times article. This case was very explicitly built off of arguments and research found in Jonathan Haidt's book The Anxious Generation, which has enjoyed mainstream appeal. "Mr. Haidt met with some of the attorneys general on Zoom, briefing them on his research," the Times continues.

"We're now seeing the dark side of digital technologies in a way that makes it possible for a cultural rejection, a cultural awakening that we can't live this way," Haidt told the Times.

Brown smartly noted earlier this month that "no one can actually say whether social media use causes teen problems or whether excessive reliance on social media is simply a symptom of struggling socially or already suffering from mental distress."

Regardless of where you come down on child-harm arguments, the real thing that should unite libertarians is the fact that Meta's predictably interested in using the levers of the law to screw over its competitors:

after the initial shock of the settlement headlines yesterday, it took me a bit to see just how much Meta is putting the screws to its competitors https://t.co/yyxaxIMSig pic.twitter.com/rwHnjmGeRy

"In the sunlight of the next day, Meta's settlement looks less like a child safety 'win' and more like a prosecutorial gun aimed at TikTok, Snap, and YouTube," writes Adam Kovacevich, who works in tech messaging for Democrats, on X. "Meta's contingent settlement payment is essentially a bounty: billions more for states if its rivals are brought into the settlement regime. Meta even admitted that teens restricted on Instagram will migrate elsewhere, so its goal is to make its competitors less engaging for teens too."

In an ideal world, the mechanisms through which we would curb teen's social media use—which I feel awfully Haidt-aligned on, personally—would be smaller-scale and not enforced by the government: Parents would refuse to give children and teenagers phones until they have already developed both attention spans and a modicum of self-regulation; schools would aggressively crackdown on smartphone use during instructional hours; social-media time would be limited by families. There's still such a thing as parenting, you know, and it's kind of wild how (to borrow from Haidt), we're dealing with "overprotection in the real world and underprotection in the virtual world" en masse, when this is a choice made by today's parents. The companies aren't forcing their hands.

That said, it's a very difficult collective action problem: When schools and other parents aren't adopting common-sense restrictions, it becomes more fraught for one single family to do so, thus relegating their teenager to years of pariahdom. Haidt understands this, and even cites research on how young adults say "they would PREFER to live in a world with no TikTok or Instagram," that "they feel trapped" and feel like "they have to use these platforms because….everyone else is using them, and they would pay money to have everyone stop, which would allow them to stop."

Scenes from New York: Former Reasoner Emma Camp is on fire right now:

Since everyone liked my rent control video so much, I thought you might enjoy another video I made about some maddening NYC housing policy.pic.twitter.com/mxVcWjmcfk

— Emma Camp (@emmma_camp_) August 27, 2026

Another one bites the dust: "Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb general whose actions during the Balkan wars of the 1990s led to him being called the 'Butcher of Bosnia' and who was held responsible for Europe's deadliest massacre since World War II, the killing of some 8,000 Muslim men and boys at Srebrenica in 1995, has died in custody in The Hague. He was 83," reports The New York Times.

Look, if you're "scromiting" then I think you have bigger problems than pot.

"Federal aviation officials have found that two air-traffic controllers left work early before an Air Canada regional jet crashed into a firetruck at LaGuardia Airport in March," reports The Wall Street Journal. "The Federal Aviation Administration is moving to fire the two controllers, who officials determined had left about an hour before their shifts ended on March 22, people familiar with the matter said. As a result, two controllers remaining at the LaGuardia tower didn't have backup to assist with high workloads."

"The Trump administration acted illegally when it labeled the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic a security risk and barred the company from working with the U.S. government, a federal judge ruled on Thursday," reports The New York Times. "Judge Rita Lin of the U.S. District Court in the Northern District of California wrote in her 59-page ruling that the government had unlawfully retaliated against Anthropic 'for constitutionally protected expressive activities' after the A.I. company spoke out about how its technology should be used. 'The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,' she wrote."

The post Haidt's Moment appeared first on Reason.com.

title: Star student rejected by 16 colleges, hired by Google, gets legal win in racial discrimination suit
description: A Palo Alto, California, father declares victory after a judge denied the University of Washington's motion to dismiss their anti-Asian bias suit.
fullText:
A father in Palo Alto, California is declaring a victory in court after a federal judge allowed a civil rights lawsuit alleging anti-Asian bias in college admissions to move forward.

Nan Zhong and his son, Stanley Zhong, filed federal lawsuits against several elite institutions — including the University of California system, the University of Washington, the University of Michigan, and Cornell University. The complaints allege the universities engaged in "racially discriminatory admissions practices that disadvantage highly qualified Asian-American applicants."

One of their cases will now proceed in part against the University of Washington after a federal judge granted the university defendants' motion to dismiss in part and denied it in part.

"We got an exciting ruling from the judge," Nan Zhong told Fox News Digital. "Effectively, the judge ruled in our favor by denying the university's motion to dismiss. So this is a major development in the lawsuit. That means the judge found enough factual allegations to support our allegation."

Duke Law's Alleged Race-based Admissions Accused Of Defying Supreme Court Ruling: Doj

The ruling centered in part on sovereign immunity. Judge James L. Robart denied the defendants' motion to dismiss Stanley's Title VI claims against the university while dismissing several other claims.

The University of Washington Board of Regents sent Fox News Digital a statement in response to the ruling.

"We're pleased that the court dismissed many of the claims and two of the three plaintiffs. Admission to the Allen School is highly competitive and the vast majority of out-of-state applicants are not admitted because, as Washington's flagship university, we prioritize Washington residents for admission," a spokesperson said.

"With that ruling, we can now proceed into discovery, request internal documents, internal communication, and most importantly, admissions data," Nan said.

Stanley Zhong, now 21, made headlines after he was rejected by 16 of the 18 colleges he applied to — including top-tier public and private institutions — despite boasting an elite academic record. A 2023 graduate of Gunn High School in Palo Alto, Stanley scored a 1590 out of 1600 on the SAT (99th percentile), held a 4.42 weighted GPA, ranked in the top 9% of his graduating class, and had launched a free e-signing startup featured by Amazon Web Services.

Shortly after the college rejections, Google hired Stanley as a full-time software engineer in a position that his family's court filing says typically requires a Ph.D. or equivalent practical experience. Stanley was first scouted by the tech giant in coding competitions when he was just 13 years old.

California Sociology Professor Cited 'Irony' In Removing Act/sat, Not Fixing Racial Disparities As Intended

The family spent over a year researching admissions trends before filing the lawsuits, concluding that anti-Asian bias remains a systemic issue despite recent court precedents.

"The story is much bigger than myself, than my son, Stanley, or our family," Zhong told Fox News Digital. "First of all, I have a younger son, so I don't want him to face the same problem that his older brother faced. I think this is something important we should correct so my future grandkids won't have the same problem again."

Zhong added that since taking their battle public, dozens of families across the country have reached out to share similar experiences.

"After the story came out, we received a lot of communication from other Asian-American families telling us about their story, telling about how highly qualified Asian-American students were rejected left and right," Zhong said. "So this is a large-scale issue and I think of it as an issue that's been around for a long time."

California Board Of Regents To Review Sat/act Testing Ban After 1,400 Professors Warn Of 'Severe' Math Gaps

Spokespersons for the University of California system have previously denied the allegations, maintaining that their admissions policies strictly comply with state and federal laws prohibiting race-conscious decisions.

Stanley Zhong was accepted at the University of Maryland and the University of Texas-Austin but decided to take a job offer as a software development engineer at Google in the fall of 2023 instead.

title: One question about the Constitution puts liberals’ appetite for sweeping change to the test
description: March on Washington activists called to abolish the Senate and rewrite the Constitution while pushing Zohran Mamdani-style socialist policies.
fullText:
Fox News Digital spoke with attendees and activists at Friday's March on Washington who voiced support for systemic political change, from sweeping reforms to bringing socialist policies to their hometowns as DSA-backed candidates notch primary victories ahead of the midterms.

"I would definitely advocate for that from (the) ground up, like abolishing [the Constitution], rewriting it, including people's voices that haven't been included on there as well," Sravya, of Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital. "I would probably also rewrite all the oppressive amendments that are in there targeting marginalized individuals."

March on Washington 2026: Defend the Vote was held Friday at the Lincoln Memorial on the 63rd anniversary of the 1963 March on Washington. It was organized by Rev. Al Sharpton's National Action Network.

Fox News Digital spoke with a handful of attendees, asking whether they would support abolishing and rewriting the Constitution and whether DSA policies are good for the direction of America, questions that drew support from some of those interviewed.

Socialists Launch Radical Platform To Abolish The Us Senate In Bid To Fundamentally Transform America

Democratic leaders, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Independent Sen. Bernie Sanders took the stage to rally attendees around voting rights and civil rights protections.

"I think so," Sravya added when asked if the Senate should be abolished. "Or reconstructing it from (the) ground up. I think that would be important because we have a lot of older leaders there currently that have been there for years. I think it needs a whole systemic reform."

Sen Deb Fischer: The Left's War On The Senate And Supreme Court Puts Our Republic At Risk

"I'm in full support of abolition of the colonial structures that cause terror to all marginalized and oppressed people," Darius from Maryland said when asked the same question.

Abolishing the Senate is one of the goals of the DSA platform, and several march attendees echoed the broader push for systemic change while also backing policies associated with democratic socialist New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

DSA-backed candidates have defeated incumbent or establishment-backed Democrats in primaries from Colorado and New York to Pennsylvania and Michigan.

There was also an appetite for more Mamdani-style candidates and eagerness to bring his agenda to their own hometowns.

Mamdani Claims Democratic Socialists Can Win 'Anywhere' As Democrats Feud Over Party's Future

"Yeah. I would definitely like that," Kassandra of Ann Arbor, Michigan, said when asked whether she would like to see her state move in the direction of Mamdani's New York.

Kassandra, a former volunteer for Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, pointed to universal health care, unions and removing money from politics as priorities.

Bernie Sanders, Dsa Reveal Demands For Dem Party After Socialists Sweep New York Elections

"I definitely do think we should probably get on board with some universal health care. Like I said, my biggest thing money out of politics," Kassandra said. "I feel like [El-Sayed] is very, like, [pro] union. He wants to get everyone together and, like, support all different religions all different races and I really value human rights as a therapist."

Kassandra said there have been policies that are aligned with socialism that have come from previous presidents that were beneficial. Asked to identify specific examples, she declined to answer.

Mamdani Clashes With Democratic Socialists' Push To Abolish Police And Prisons

Esteban, a New Jersey resident who works in New York City, said he has seen a "huge shift" since Mamdani took office.

"I feel like someone who's lived through a lot of mayoral terms in many different cities, this is probably the most change I've seen so quickly," he said. "So far what I'm seeing is good change."

title: O'Neill would rather Celtic had no fans at Ibrox than 300
description: Martin O'Neill says Celtic "might as well not get any" tickets after Rangers offered 300 for the sides' League Cup quarter-final at Ibrox next month.
fullText:
Martin O'Neill says Celtic "might as well not get any" tickets after Rangers offered 300 for the sides' League Cup quarter-final at Ibrox next month.

Rangers confirmed the allocation on Friday hours after the Scottish FA announced both clubs would have to play their next Scottish Cup home games behind closed doors.

The sanctions followed crowd disorder after Celtic's win on penalties in last season's Scottish Cup quarter-final win on penalties at Ibrox, when around 8,000 visiting supporters had been present.

That figure was about four times as many away fans that had attended recent Premiership meetings of Celtic and Rangers, with the ticketing rules different for Scottish Cup games.

"We might as well not get any, if that's the case," said O'Neill after Celtic's 2-1 Premiership win over Falkirk.

"Just looking at it from a personal viewpoint, it's one of the great fixtures. Even if the teams are not of the standard of, let's say, Paris St-Germain or Real Madrid, it is still a fantastic fixture.

"And you honestly don't realise how big it is in European games and in the world. People talk about it as a great game. And the best atmosphere is when the away fans have their allocation.

"So, that's a shame. But very obviously, if they're going to give us 300 tickets, I would rather say, 'no'. And we'll give them one."

Celtic salve Euro wounds with narrow win over Falkirk

Fan discontent over Celtic's calamitous Champions League play-off exit to LASK was writ large at Parkhead on Saturday in a banner bearing the message 'World Class Embarrassment', yet the overall mood was more supportive than sour. Much to O'Neill's surprise.

Celtic got the job done with a Camilo Duran double against Falkirk, although Colby Donovan's own goal ensured a nervy final 20 minutes. It wasn't the prettiest of victories, but it was crucial.

"As we got off the bus, the crowd actually cheered us, which was unexpected and something that we probably didn't deserve. I was really pleased," said O'Neill.

Midfielder Luke McCowan, a whipping boy on social media over his performance in Linz, was welcomed off the bench against Falkirk with an ovation.

"I thought the fans were good today," former Celtic captain Scott Brown told BBC Scotland.

"I liked what they did when McCowan came on. They are the real fans, going to games, not sitting behind keyboards.

"It's disrespectful, that. Luke has had to delete his Instagram or Twitter and he shouldn't need to do that. It's part and parcel of football, having a good game and a bad game.

"I know he will be hurting, but it takes a strong character to come back and get on with what he does. Luke did well when he came on. He's a huge Celtic fan and always wants to do his best for Celtic."

The Champions League exit exposed squad deficiencies O'Neill is eager to address before the transfer deadline on Thursday (17:00 BST)

"I'm still really hopeful we can do something [in the transfer market]," he told BBC Scotland post-match.

"If we want to defend our title and get something in the Europa League we need a bit more strength in depth. I think that's pretty obvious."

There's been long-held concern at left-back. Kieran Tierney is influential but struggles to complete games and there is no obvious alternative after Marcelo Saracchi's exit.

O'Neill confirmed Tierney picked up another injury issue against Falkirk with the extent of that unclear.

Former skipper Brown believes Celtic will "bring in another left-back and maybe another centre-half" and says Arne Engels' departure to West Ham has left a sizeable gap.

"I think they need a powerhouse in the middle of the park, especially in Europe," Brown added.

"Someone like Engels with his energy and legs. They need that physicality, they missed that against LASK and got bullied all over the park.

"They will be out there looking to do their best in the market and will have a few pounds to spend. Martin will be pushing the board as much as he possibly can."

title: Henshaw wins world gold 11 days after being in hospital
description: Britain's Charlotte Henshaw has won her 12th Para-canoe World Championship title - less than two weeks after being in hospital with cellulitis.
fullText:
Britain's Charlotte Henshaw has won her 12th Para-canoe World Championship title - less than two weeks after being in hospital with cellulitis.

The 39-year-old contracted the condition - usually a bacterial infection which makes the skin painful, hot and swollen - in her leg and, after leaving hospital, was unable to train on the water in the lead up to the championships in Poznan, Poland.

But in Saturday's KL2 200m final she crossed the finish line more than three seconds ahead of the rest of the field for her eighth world title in the event, adding to the four she has won in the VL3 equivalent.

"Of all the titles I've managed to win, that probably means the most because I did not know I was going to be here a week ago," she said.

"There's maybe something to be said for taking the pressure off and going out and trusting my body and my experience.

"I've been competing at the highest level for an awfully long time and in moments where things aren't going well and the preparation gets swept out from underneath you, you have to draw on every single bit of experience.

"Eleven days ago, I didn't think I would be on the plane so to come here and compete and then retain my title, I couldn't be happier and it means a lot this one."

A double leg amputee, Henshaw is a three-time Paralympic champion in Para-canoeing since switching from swimming in 2017.

Writing on Instagram, external after her heat on Friday, Henshaw said: "The last week or so has definitely put things into perspective.

"It's so easy to get caught up in results, rankings, times and expectations, but when your long-term limb health becomes the priority, those things seem a lot less important."

Elsewhere in Poznan on Saturday, Henshaw's team-mate Hope Gordon won gold in the KL3 200m while Stuart Wood won bronze in the men's VL3 event.

For Gordon, who last month represented Scotland in Para-powerlifting at the Commonwealth Games, it is a first KL3 world title - having previously won two in the VL3.

title: Maguire fires superb 63 as Alexander lead cut at Irish Open
description: Ireland's Leona Maguire fires a superb nine-under-par 63 at the Women's Irish Open at the K Club in County Kildare as Casandra Alexander leads by three going into Sunday's final round.
fullText:
Women's Irish Open - third round

-18 C Alexander (SA); -15 S Kouskova (Cze); -13 K Arwefjaell (Swe); -12 C Viden (Swe), L Rydqvist (Swe); -11 N Komulainen (Fin), L Maguire (Ire); -10 B Navarossa (USA), L Pettersson (Swe), A Foersterling (Ger), A Fanali (Ita), D Forbrigd (Nor)

Selected others: -8 A Dawson (IoM); -7 A Foster (Ire); -5 A Donegan (Ire), L M Humphreys (Eng), H Screen (Eng), L Walsh (Ire); Level A Wilson (NI)

Ireland's Leona Maguire delighted the home crowd by shooting a superb nine-under-par 63 on day three of the Women's Irish Open at the K Club to sit seven shots behind leader Casandra Alexander.

Maguire birdied nine of the first 15 holes in a bogey-free round to lie in a tie for sixth position on 11 under.

Her birdie putt on the 18th for a 62 lipped out but the Cavan native will be happy to have returned to her best form after two opening rounds of 71.

Maguire picked up shots on successive holes between the second and the fourth, with further back-to-back birdies coming on the seventh and eighth as she posted 31 shots for her outward nine.

Further birdies followed for the Europe Solheim Cup player on the 10th, 12th, 14th and 15th holes.

Heavy rain led to a suspension of play during the afternoon as puddles formed around the County Kildare course but - in terms of occupying top spot in the leaderboard - it was business as usual for South African Alexander, who has led the tournament from day one.

Alexander fired a 69 to hold a three-shot lead over Czech player Sara Kouskova, whose 67 cut her deficit to the pacesetter by two shots to three - in comparison to her arrears at the end of day two.

Kajsa Arwefjaell matched Maguire's round of the day by carding a 63 to move to third place on 13 under with two fellow Swedes, Corinne Viden and Louise Rydqvist, one shot further back after posting third rounds of 69.

Finn Noora Komulainen shot a 66 to join Maguire on 11 under.

Anna Foster is next best of the Irish players on seven under, following an impressive 66, while Lily May Humphreys and Hannah Screen lead the English challenge on five under.

title: Durham taken to final day despite needing only four runs to win
description: Division Two leaders Durham will need four runs on the final day to beat Gloucestershire.
fullText:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, Chester-le-Street (day three)

Gloucestershire 137: Aldridge 5-16 & 250: Hammond 58; Aldridge 4-47

Durham 384: Bedingham 122; Langridge 3-89

Durham (6 pts) need four runs to beat Gloucs (3 pts)

Bad light prevented Kasey Aldridge's superb nine-wicket match haul from delivering league leaders Durham a three-day County Championship win over bottom side Gloucestershire.

A devastating burst of 4-47 from the seam-bowling all-rounder backed up his first innings five-for, but the hosts' victory charge will roll into day four with only four to win as the weather meant their chase could not begin before close.

At the start of the day, Durham's tail boosted their first-innings total to 384 - a lead of 247 - thanks to cameos from Aldridge, Brydon Carse and Matthew Potts, before the latter pair reduced Gloucestershire to 7-2 second time around. They were later bowled out for 250.

Cameron Bancroft and Miles Hammond were able to guide the visitors to 50-2 at lunch.

A century stand for the fourth wicket halted Durham's progress before Aldridge produced a superb three-wicket spell on the brink of tea to reaffirm the home side's dominance in the match and the Division Two table.

Light dictated that Durham's Test-quality pace attack step aside with two wickets required, and an explosive 10th-wicket partnership of 39 between Sai Kishore (29 not out) and JT Langridge forced the league leaders to bat again.

With that target of four set, the players did not emerge from their dressing rooms, with Gloucestershire refusing to bowl spin, leaving as little as one ball of action in prospect for day four.

In the only fixture in the country to start on time, Durham resumed on 331-8 and swiftly accelerated beyond 350.

Carse took James Hayes for 16 in an over before he was bowled by the Nottinghamshire loanee for 20. Potts, who added 15, fell to Langridge, the seamer finishing with three wickets.

The England duo then produced a relentless opening burst which saw Gloucestershire stagger to 15-2 in 10 overs.

Joe Phillips was removed by Carse for the second time in the match for a duck, before Potts had Ollie Price caught behind. Bancroft and Hammond counter-attacked against the change bowlers to reach lunch with no further damage.

Both sides battled manfully after the break, with the left-handed Hammond negotiating a testing nine-over Ben Stokes spell to reach 50 off 80 balls.

He batted comfortably in partnership with captain Bancroft, but a rising delivery from Aldridge squared Hammond up and induced the edge for 58.

Aldridge continued his fine performance by having Bancroft caught at second slip for 46 in his next over, and new man Tommy Boorman followed shortly after.

Gloucestershire finished the session five down and still 115 in arrears, leaving five wickets left for Durham to complete the job.

As the gloom set in after tea, Aldridge uprooted Daz Ahmed's middle stump for a 14-ball duck to register nine wickets in a match for the first time in his career.

With a light reading taken, it seemed only the elements could save Gloucestershire, as first innings half-centurion James Bracey dug in alongside Mitch Killeen.

Carse removed Bracey with a vicious in-swinger - 173-7.

In the 61st over of the innings, light forced Colin Ackermann into the attack, and he struck with his second ball, ending a spirited hand from Killeen to leave his side two wickets away.

Ackermann bowled in partnership with Will Rhodes, while Kishore shone with two sixes in 29.

Ackermann accounted for Hayes, who chipped to mid-wicket and left his side nine down, still trailing by 36.

Kishore and Langdrige had fun against Durham's part-timers, eking out a slender lead with a succession of maximums which ended when Langridge holed out for 36.

Although the umpires returned to the middle, they soon trudged off, and play was called off just after 18:20 BST.

Durham are all but there for a seventh win in 10 games.

title: 'Supporters aren't always wrong' - Moyes on Everton fans' anger
description: David Moyes says "supporters aren't always wrong" after Everton fans voice their opposition to the potential sale of teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong during the 1-1 draw at Bournemouth.
fullText:
"Supporters aren't always wrong" was David Moyes' reaction to Everton fans voicing their opposition to the potential sale of teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong during the 1-1 draw at Bournemouth.

BBC Sport reported earlier on Saturday that Nottingham Forest had put in a £40m bid for the England Under-19 international, who is regarded as one of the brightest prospects to emerge from Finch Farm in recent years.

The 19-year-old started at Vitality Stadium as the Toffees rescued a late draw and their travelling supporters repeatedly chanted that there would be "a riot" if Armstrong was sold.

"I think you always have to consider supporters; supporters aren't always wrong," said Everton manager Moyes.

"But then there are also times where I've had people at clubs who are really powerful and make difficult decisions.

"I'd bring into that Bryan Gray, who was at Preston North End, and Sir Philip Carter, who was at Everton when I first came in. Not all decisions are popular, and sometimes they have to do it for different reasons.

"Managers have to make decisions on players sometimes and they feel like huge decisions. But there are sometimes bigger decisions to be made and the club will, I'm sure, make what they think is the right one.

"If I'd say something to them (the fans), I'd say their manager's an Evertonian."

Armstrong has made 24 appearances for Everton and played 87 minutes against the Cherries before he was replaced by Charly Alcaraz.

Are Moyes and Everton's owners on same page?

How to follow Transfer Deadline Day on the BBC

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?

Moyes has been frustrated by the club's lack of signings and he made it clear he wanted reinforcements after the Carabao Cup second-round win against Preston on Wednesday.

The Toffees have been searching for a replacement for right-back Seamus Coleman for more than a year.

Moyes stressed any decision about Armstrong's future would ultimately rest with Everton, owned by The Friedkin Group.

"It's not really a question for just now. It will be a club decision," he said.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Scot also questioned whether the summer transfer window should remain open once the season has started.

"For all the years I've been in the Premier League this is probably the first time I've thought it was really a nonsense we're still playing games when the window is still open," said Moyes, who is in the final year of his Everton contract.

"It feels like we'd have been better off just getting it shut.

"Maybe it's just the way I am at the moment, I might feel better on Tuesday, but just at the moment it just leaves too much open, too much talk, mainly from the media.

"If I look back over the years, back to Wayne Rooney, Mikel Arteta, Joleon Lescott, players at Everton I didn't want to lose, more recently Declan Rice at West Ham, sometimes it's part of the journey and you have to rebuild."

The window for the Premier League and EFL clubs to make new signings is to close on Tuesday, 1 September at 23:00 BST.

The Friedkin Group (TFG), Everton's American owners, will be risking the fury of their own fanbase should they agree to the sale of Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.

The notion that Everton could even consider parting with Armstrong sparked an instant reaction of disbelief and anger among supporters, with the teenager regarded as their brightest home-grown prospect for years and a big hope for the future.

As yet, there are no indications that Everton will accept an offer, but Forest's interest is real, although it would be a real coup should they pull it off.

It would also send out worrying signals about the scale of TFG's ambitions.

Manager Moyes has been frustrated by the club's lack of incoming transfer activity this summer.

Moyes made it abundantly clear after Wednesday's 4-0 win at Championship side Preston in the Carabao Cup that he wanted reinforcements.

His hope was that TFG would provide backing for further arrivals.

Since then, however, Everton's main creator Iliman Ndiaye has been heavily linked with Manchester City, and now Forest are ready to test their resolve over Armstrong.

How Moyes would view, or indeed explain, such a sale, would be intriguing. It would appear totally at odds with his stated intention of building a better squad.

And while Everton and their support may have to accept their prize assets being spirited away by clubs such as Manchester City, the idea that their most promising young player could be taken away by Nottingham Forest – a club they would be expecting to challenge or even surpass – may be harder to stomach.

That is why the manner in which Everton handle Forest's approach for Armstrong, who has already excelled this season, may be a defining moment for TFG and Moyes.

title: Lawrence impresses as weather delays England
description: Dan Lawrence impresses in devilishly difficult batting conditions to advance England’s push for a series win over Pakistan on a weather-hit third day of the second Test.
fullText:
Second Rothesay Test, Lord's (day three of five)

England 290 (Smith 61, Cox 55; Abbas 4-73) & 177-7 (Lawrence 50*; Abbas 3-48)

Pakistan 110 (Awais 46; Robinson 4-11, Archer 3-26)

Dan Lawrence impressed in devilishly difficult batting conditions to advance England's push for a series win over Pakistan on a weather-hit third day of the second Test.

Lawrence is one of the players looking to cement a place in the new-look England team and he enhanced his credentials with an unbeaten 50, his second half-century in as many Tests.

Only 24.5 overs were possible at Lord's on Saturday because of persistent rain. The action did not begin until 14:40 BST then was regularly interrupted until the players left the field for the final time at 17:08.

In farcical scenes, play was eventually abandoned at 18:30 in the best weather of the day to boos from the remaining spectators. There was potential for another hour to be used.

Lawrence lifted England to 177-7 in their second innings, with a lead of 357 looking colossal given the assistance on offer for bowlers and Pakistan's weak batting.

On the juicy surface, under the leaden sky and floodlights, Pakistan's trio of seamers made life incredibly hard for England's batters after they resumed on 81-3.

With the ball darting around in the air and off the seam, the last thing Emilio Gay needed was uneven bounce. Gay got one from Muhammad Abbas that shot along the ground to be lbw for 31, missing another chance to make the opener's spot indisputably his own.

Harry Brook and Lawrence battled to add 45 for the fifth wicket, a significant achievement given the task they faced. Brook adjusted his game to the situation before he was out for 34, superbly caught up to the stumps by wicketkeeper Muhammad Rizwan.

Lawrence eventually decided attack was the best form of defence, accelerating towards his fifth half-century in Test cricket.

Sunday's weather forecast is much better and should provide ample opportunity for England to seal victory in this match and their first series win since 2024.

Vaughan backs Lawrence for extended run in England team

Lawrence hits half-century but rain disrupts England's progress again - as it happened

In their rebuild following the retirement of Ben Stokes, England have stumbled upon a promising four-pronged pace attack.

If the post-Stokes bowling has settled, the batting line-up is in a state of flux, especially with Jacob Bethell eventually due to return from a knee injury.

The situation on Saturday - the conditions and broken play – meant extra value could be placed on any contribution with the bat. Gay will feel desperately unlucky that his opportunity was cut short, while Lawrence's half-century was worth much more.

Gay showed tenacity to reach 30 overnight. From the fifth ball he faced on Saturday, he was left helpless by the Abbas shooter that left him palpably lbw, a delivery to once again ignite debate about the Lord's pitch.

The opener was crestfallen, while captain Joe Root shook his head on the England balcony. In his first summer as a Test opener, Gay has been presented with taxing circumstances, still, an average of 23 is far from enough to guarantee a long-term place.

It could be that Gay and Lawrence are vying for one place when Bethell returns. While Gay was undone by the grubber, Lawrence came through multiple deliveries that spat and hit him on the body to further his case for long-term retention in the team.

Even if the weather does improve, batting is likely to remain a huge challenge for the remainder of this match.

For that reason, as well as the form of the England bowlers and possible absence of the injured Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq, the home side's lead is probably already enough.

Pakistan will need at least 358 runs to win, having managed only 416 in three completed innings so far in the series.

The failed experiment of asking Lawrence to open for three Tests in 2024 was one of the most criticised decisions in Stokes' four years as captain.

It could have been the end of Lawrence's Test career, but he has got a recall in the absence of Stokes, partly because he can offer some off-spin bowling. He has only been required to bowl one over, so has instead taken his chance with the bat.

This latest half-century was much more impressive than a scratchy innings in Leeds. At Lord's, following a swipe to get off the mark with a boundary edged over the slips, Lawrence showed bravery, determination and invention.

Time and again both he and Brook were beaten by the movement generated by the Pakistan seamers.

After scrapping to 19 from 39 balls, Lawrence changed approach. He danced to slice Mohammad Ali for four, then, next ball, shimmied to hit the same bowler over the covers for a magnificent six.

Brook's dismissal was the signal for England to lose regular wickets amid the breaks. Lawrence continued to attack and receive the blows.

Immediately after tea he clobbered the spin of Ali Usman over the leg side for six, then reached his half-century from 64 balls in the following over.

The weather permitted only two more balls to be bowled, leaving Lawrence primed for a further assault on Sunday morning.

title: South Africa hold off All Blacks fightback to level series
description: World champions South Africa deliver a powerful first-half performance as they edge past New Zealand and level 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series at 1-1.
fullText:
'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series - second Test

Tries: Kriel, De Allende, Kolisi Cons: Kolbe 3 Pens: Kolbe 4

Tries: Roigard, McKenzie, Carter, Savea Cons: Love 3

World champions South Africa delivered a powerful first-half performance as they edged past New Zealand and levelled 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series at 1-1 with two Tests to play.

The All Blacks travelled to Cape Town knowing a win would write them into the history books as the first New Zealand team to win back-to-back Tests in South Africa since the 'Incomparables' of 1996.

But South Africa dominated the basics and showed a more clinical edge this week, even though the lively All Blacks again outscored them on the try count by four to three.

New Zealand's fightback ultimately came too late, captain Ardie Savea barging over on 77 minutes to get the game within a score, but on the All Blacks' final attack Boks replacement Cameron Hanekom won a superb turnover that settled the nervy closing stages.

As he did last week, Springboks wing Cheslin Kolbe took on the kicking duties over fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, notching up 18 points in a player-of-the-match performance.

The first series in 30 years between these two mighty rugby nations is shaping into an epic, with the third Test back at altitude in Soweto, Johannesburg next Saturday.

The Springbok team that took the field at the Cape Town Stadium was markedly different to the one originally named by head coach Rassie Erasmus on Monday.

Fly-half Handre Pollard was fit and then injured and withdrawn in the week, while Kolbe was injured and then fit and eventually named on the wing.

On top of that, Erasmus switched around his whole front row in the hours before kick-off, with the starting trio dropping to the bench and vice-versa.

It meant there were five changes in all from the matchday squad announced on Monday and surely would have had the New Zealand management thumbing through the regulations of the tour agreement.

Despite producing a famous rearguard effort in the first-Test victory at Ellis Park, New Zealand boss Dave Rennie warned in the week his side would need to "go deeper" to cope with the inevitable Springbok backlash.

That South African onslaught came from the off.

Hooker Deon Fourie, at nearly 40 the oldest Springbok in history, found his target in the line-out, the South African maul powered into the 22, and lightning fast ball led to centre Jesse Kriel crashing over.

Kolbe added the extras as the world champions made the dream start.

But despite the fast start from the hosts, New Zealand grew into the contest, with referee Angus Gardner, himself a late call-up in place of Nika Amashukeli, presiding over a fast and fluent game.

Damian McKenzie made a clean break which almost put in Will Jordan, and while the Boks killed the ball from the ensuing breakdown, Eben Etzebeth got up to spoil New Zealand's five-metre line-out.

Despite their set-piece issues, the All Blacks came again. Intricate handling freed Jordan, who used his pace and strength to escape down the right and link with the outstanding Cam Roigard. Ruben Love levelled the scores from bang in front.

That score lit a fire in the Springboks, with Kolbe kicking a penalty and Damian de Allende barrelling over after another imposing maul as South Africa showed far more ruthlessness compared to a week ago.

With the Springboks dominating in the basics, the crowd in Cape Town smelt blood as the lead stretched to 17-7.

But with ball in hand, Rennie's crop are reminiscent of the great All Blacks side of old. Savea burst forward from a line-out, and perfect passing gave McKenzie a walk-in.

At 17-14 edging towards half-time the contest was in the balance, before a match-defining sequence just before the interval.

Kolbe forced a five-metre scrum, before which Erasmus brought on two of his strongest scrummagers in Malcolm Marx and Ox Nche, who immediately won a penalty.

From there, another scrum, another penalty advantage, and with the All Blacks back-pedalling captain Siya Kolisi crashed over for South Africa's third try and a 10-point lead after a pulsating first 40.

New Zealand needed to score first in the second half, and they didn't, losing the ball when in Bok territory and then giving away a soft penalty which Kolbe kicked.

The All Blacks were on the ropes, Marx won a breakdown penalty, and Kolbe stretched the lead to 16 points with half an hour to go.

With the second half lacking the fireworks of the first, the All Blacks backs – led by Roigard - desperately tried to drag New Zealand back into the match.

After another McKenzie break led to nothing, some more beautiful handling resulted in Leroy Carter scampering into the left corner, a fabulous finish.

More excellent attacking play released Jordan down the right, and the recycled ball found skipper Savea, who crashed over to cut the gap to seven points with two minutes remaining.

But the Springboks held on, despite lock Lood de Jager being sent to the sin-bin for a high tackle.

Fittingly, it was a breakdown penalty that settled the game, with Hanekom winning the crucial turnover in an area South Africa dominated.

The All Blacks' impressive win in the first Test had temporarily shot them above South Africa in the world rankings, something Erasmus urged his side to rectify.

That they did, and with normal service resumed in the eyes of the Springboks supporters, South Africa travel back to the Highveld with the momentum.

But the All Blacks have played some wonderful rugby in the first two Tests, and will still believe they can join the legends of 1996.

The eyes of the rugby world now turn to Soweto.

title: 'That trust isn't there' - how does Iraola get best out of Isak?
description: Alexander Isak scored his first goal of the season in the 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest - but how do Liverpool get the best out of him?
fullText:
During Liverpool's negotiations with Paris St-Germain for Bradley Barcola, the Anfield hierarchy were determined not to pay more than the club-record £125m they spent on Alexander Isak last summer.

When the £123m deal for Barcola is completed over the coming days, the France winger will become the 10th £100m player in Premier League history.

None have cost more than Isak, so the expectation on the former Newcastle striker is understandable, to say the least.

Isak scored 44 Premier League goals in his last two seasons at Newcastle, but in an injury-plagued first campaign at Anfield the 26-year-old found the back of the net just three times in 14 top-flight appearances.

For Andoni Iraola, who has drawn his first two games as Liverpool manager, a major part of success at Anfield will be the ability to get the best out of Isak, who - despite scoring - was largely ineffective in their 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest on Saturday.

Unlike last summer, Isak has looked sharp in pre-season after some impressive displays for Sweden at the World Cup, but struggled on his return to Tyneside last weekend.

For 45 minutes against Forest on Saturday, those struggles continued with just six touches, one accurate pass and zero shots.

"It is clear that Liverpool haven't worked out how to play with Alexander Isak yet," said ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart, who is a pundit on Saturday's Match of the Day.

"At Newcastle everything flowed through him. That was down to a trust thing that they had built up over time - their midfield knew exactly where he was and they didn't even need to look up as he'd be there waiting.

"At Liverpool that trust just isn't there at the moment - no-one is feeling it and he isn't that central point, which is leading to him looking lost and isolated."

Man City open talks with Liverpool over Gakpo

Munoz rescues point for Liverpool at home to Forest

Gibbs-White shines - player ratings for Liverpool v Nottm Forest

Iraola angry as official's board delays subs before goal

It would have been intriguing to be a fly on the wall in the directors' box at Anfield.

Iraola's first home Premier League game was watched by incoming Liverpool vice-chairman Amit Bhatia, principal owner John Henry, and sporting director Richard Hughes, who was integral in getting the deal for Isak done last summer.

Thankfully for them - and Iraola - Isak got Liverpool on level terms after the break. He managed just seven more touches in the second half but centre-forwards deal in goals and the Swede timed his run perfectly to meet Cody Gakpo's delivery for his first goal of the season. His smile after told a story in itself.

"That's the job ultimately as a striker [to score goals]. I am very happy to score the first one and hopefully it just keeps coming," Isak told TNT Sports.

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard described the goal as "big" - for both the striker's confidence and the team's.

But, in Hart's opinion, Iraola still has a major conundrum.

"Andoni Iraola has some big decisions to make," said Hart. "Does he base his team round him [Isak] or does he try to find a different solution within his squad? In my opinion he's got to commit to what the club have done by investing so heavily in Isak.

"There's no point signing these players if you aren't going to use them properly and play to their strengths. There's no doubting Isak's quality - they are just at a bit of a crossroads at the moment."

During Isak's struggles last season, the belief inside the club was that he was a long-term signing and judgement would be reserved for once he was fully fit.

Only Erling Haaland, Mohamed Salah and Ollie Watkins have scored more Premier League goals since Isak's first season in England and, with Salah now out of the picture, the onus is on Isak to deliver - particularly with Hugo Ekitike out injured.

Liverpool's first two games of the season have finished 2-2 despite Iraola's side enjoying 60% of possession against Newcastle last week and 70% against Forest.

In both games, they have found themselves trailing and are yet to be ahead in the Premier League this season.

That has inevitably made things trickier for Isak, who was such a force in a counter-attacking Newcastle side. Against low blocks, the proposition is different.

It is also symptomatic of a wider issue Iraola faces.

Last season, his Bournemouth side won just four of the 19 Premier League games in which they had the majority of possession. They won nine of the other 19.

The Cherries, who were known for their counter-pressing style and effectiveness in transition, also failed to win a game in which they had more than 58.8% possession.

In essence, his side were more successful when they had less of the ball - something that will rarely happen now he is at Anfield.

"As an attacking force it isn't flowing for Liverpool," said Hart. "With the physical nature of the Premier League and with them not 100% sure on what they are doing at the moment, teams are stomping all over them.

"It's going to take a whole lot of work from Iraola and his staff on the training pitch, but he is a top coach and they have top players."

Asked about whether he sets targets for the season, Isak said: "Not really. I think every striker wants to score [in] every game he plays. Obviously that's difficult but [we take] each game at a time."

That is one way to look at it, and this was certainly an improvement on his showing against Newcastle, but deep down Isak will know he can - and must - do better.

title: Man City open talks with Liverpool over Gakpo
description: Manchester City open talks with Liverpool about signing Netherlands winger Cody Gakpo.
fullText:
Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool about signing attacker Cody Gakpo.

The Netherlands forward's future is set to become one of the key storylines heading into the final three days of the transfer window.

The 27-year-old has attracted concrete interest from City and Tottenham Hotspur, but sources indicate that City is Gakpo's preferred destination if he leaves Anfield before Tuesday's deadline.

City made formal contact with Liverpool over a move on Saturday evening.

Gakpo's potential exit comes after Liverpool agreed to sign Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola in a deal worth up to £123m.

However, it is understood that Liverpool would prefer to sign another forward before sanctioning Gakpo's exit this summer.

The Reds have an interest in Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.

Gakpo joined Liverpool from boyhood club PSV Eindhoven in January 2023 and has scored 33 goals in 91 Premier League appearances.

On Saturday, he provided the assist for Alexander Isak's goal as Andoni Iraola's side drew 2-2 with Nottingham Forest at Anfield, having scored in last week's draw at Newcastle.

title: Tonali struggles but Gonzalez impresses - player ratings for Tottenham v Newcastle
description: How Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United's players rated following Saturday's 2-0 win for the visitors in their Premier League match.
fullText:
Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa fired Newcastle United to a 2-0 victory against Tottenham Hotspur.

Here's how I rated the players at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and you can see how you scored them below.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Antonin Kinsky: Unlike his countryman, Lukas Hornicek, the Spurs goalkeeper had nothing to do in the first half but could only watch on as Elanga's shot went in off the post after the break before Wissa's improvised effort made it 2-0. 5

Archie Gray: Can never fault his effort but is he at his very best at right-back? 5

Micky van de Ven: The captain's first start of the season. Picked up a needless early booking, but went on to make a crucial sliding challenge to deny Wissa inside the box. 6

Jan Paul van Hecke: Got back to make a block to deny Willock. Comfort in possession allowed Spurs to bypass Newcastle press. Went close with header. 6

Andy Robertson: Carried a threat going forward in the first half but could not prevent Dedic winning a header to set up Elanga's goal. 5

Rodrigo Bentancur: Work often goes unseen. Broke up play and won ball back on a number of occasions. 5

Sandro Tonali: A shaky start as he came up against his former club for the first time. Clearly still building up fitness. At fault in build up to both goals. Ironically cheered by away fans as he came off. 4

Mateus Fernandes: First Premier League start for club. Always looked to be positive and deliveries from corners caused one or two problems in first half. 5

Pedro Porro: The World Cup winner played further forward on the right wing and had a couple of openings, seeing a shot blocked by Hall and a dipping volley go just over. 5

Omar Marmoush: Debutant was quickly parachuted into starting line-up, having tormented Newcastle so many times before with Manchester City. Hit side netting on volley. Smart reverse pass created opening for Robertson. 6

Mathys Tel: Saw one stinging effort well-saved, but also frustrated the crowd by giving the ball away. 4

Kudus (on 68, Tel): Welcome return after being sidelined since January with a serious quad injury 5

Dominic Solanke (on 75, Tonali): 5

Subs not used: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Bergvall, Davies

Lukas Hornicek: Made saves to keep out Tel, Robertson and van Hecke's efforts when Newcastle were under pressure in the first half. His save from van Hecke's header left head coach Matthias Jaissle clenching his fists on the touchline. 7

Amar Dedic: Another impressive all-round performance from the summer signing little more than a week-and-a-half into his Newcastle career. Great knock-down header to set up first goal. Tino Livramento faces a real battle to win back his place. 7

Malick Thiaw: Captain again in Dan Burn's absence. A proper old-fashioned tussle with Marmoush at times, who kept him on his toes. 6

Sven Botman: Had a shaky pre-season but looking more assured. Appears to be benefitting from a run of games with the same back four. 6

Lewis Hall: Made a huge last-ditch block inside the box to prevent Porro from getting a shot away in first half. Defensively solid and no penalty fears this time. 7

Nico Gonzalez: An impressive debut. Kept composure even after booking. A stunning cross-field ball in the build up to Elanga's goal. 8

Lewis Miley: Goes about his work quietly but keeps the ball so well. 7

Anthony Elanga: Looks a reborn player full of confidence under Jaissle. Scored his second goal in two games with a smart turn and finish in off the post. His was the name repeatedly sung by the away supporters. 7.

Joe Willock: Made an instant impact after coming off the bench against Liverpool, but not as effective as a starter on Saturday. Got one of biggest cheers from Newcastle fans for a meaty challenge on Tonali. 5

Harvey Barnes: Fresh from scoring two goals in the midweek win over West Brom in the Carabao Cup, but did not offer same threat this time. Fired one effort way over and failed to pick out a team-mate on one promising breakaway after his cutback went straight into traffic. 5

Yoane Wissa: Led the line in injured William Osula's absence and repeatedly dropped deep to help his side. Clever overhead kick sealed the win. 7

Sean Steur (on 71, Gonzalez): Sent in teasing deliver with corner in build up to Wissa's goal. 7

Nick Woltemade (on 71, Willock): Header set up Newcastle's second from Steur's corner. 7

title: Vaughan backs Lawrence for extended run in England team
description: Former captain Michael Vaughan backs batter Dan Lawrence for a run in England's Test side. How would you solve impending selection headache?
fullText:
Former captain Michael Vaughan believes Dan Lawrence has shown enough to remain in the England Test side when Jacob Bethell returns from injury.

Lawrence, a batter who bowls part-time off-spin, was a surprise choice when he was picked to fill the role created by the retirement of all-rounder Ben Stokes earlier this summer.

But after making 51 in the first Test at Headingley, Lawrence impressed with 50 not out from 66 balls in tricky conditions on day three of the second Test against Pakistan.

"I think it is a really good selection," Vaughan told BBC Test Match Special. "He will have a period in the England side that we will enjoy watching him bat.

"I think in time his off-spin will come in very handy indeed."

Lawrence impresses as weather delays England

Lawrence hits half-century but rain disrupts England's progress again - as it happened

Lawrence, 29, was recalled after an international absence of almost two years, having averaged 26.84 across 14 previous Tests including a stint as a makeshift opener.

On Saturday Lawrence made his mark by coming to the crease at 83-4 and steering England to 177-7 in their second innings when rain brought an early close.

The right-hander, whose best Test score remains 91, countered excessive seam movement and uneven bounce by showing attacking intent, hitting six fours and two sixes.

"He seems to read the game," Vaughan said. "It was the right way to play at that moment.

"He has a quirky technique that has worked for him and is very confident. He knows his scoring areas.

"He is clearly a better player than when he played for England last time."

England's current balance - with Lawrence picked over a frontline spinner - appears suited to home conditions, and could also work in South Africa and Australia where England play this winter.

While stronger spin options would likely be needed for the tour of Bangladesh in the new year, the success of England's pace quartet of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue has lessened the need for a spinner in home conditions and, in turn, helped Lawrence's cause.

Key selection decisions are still looming, however, with Jacob Bethell currently out of the series because of a knee injury.

Bethell, who also bowls part-time spin, could replace Lawrence, or regain his place from Jordan Cox, who has impressed with two fifties while filling in for Bethell at number three.

Other options include pushing Cox or Bethell up to open in place of Emilio Gay - Cox opened early in his career in county cricket and Bethell is England's current 50-over opener - and moving Cox down the order to replace Jamie Smith as wicketkeeper.

Smith scored an impressive 61 in England's first innings and has improved his glovework after a poor showing in the Ashes.

"It's pointless looking to the future because it hasn't happened yet," Lawrence said. "I'm just trying to contribute every Test I can and give a good showing of myself.

"Thankfully, so far, I think I have done.

"Obviously thoughts creep into your head and I'm desperate, along with all the other boys, to establish myself in an England shirt, which is something I haven't quite done in my career so far.

"It's just about trying to take every opportunity you get and really enjoy the occasion instead of feeling nervous about the occasion. Just have fun, play the cricket that's got me here this summer."

title: Will the Seahawks win the NFC West in 2026?
description: The Seahawks were forecasted by Bleacher Report to finish second in the NFC West in 2026 with a worse record than the one they had last season.
fullText:
Where will the Seattle Seahawks finish in the NFC West standings in 2026?

A last place finish seems to be the only near impossibility that will take shape for the defending NFC West champion Seahawks next season. However, playing in arguably the toughest division in the entire NFL, which also includes the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will be challenging as ever to win, especially when having to deal with both of those teams a total of four times next season.

Bleacher Report's Moe Moton forecasted the Seahawks to go 11-6 next season, good for second place in the NFC West division.

"The reigning Super Bowl champions should make it back to the playoffs with resurgent starter Sam Darnold at the helm," Moton said. "However, Darnold lost offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, and the team's 10th-ranked rushing attack from the previous season lost lead running back Kenneth Walker and may be without running back Zach Charbonnet (torn ACL) for multiple weeks. The Seahawks defense is equipped to win games, and it may need to do so early with question marks on offense."

The Seahawks have it all. Despite the Rams (13-4) being forecasted to win the division, experience as Super Bowl champions, elite veterans on defense, a high-powered offense and great coaching from defensive signal caller Mike Macdonald give Seattle a great chance to win the division, even with the juggernaut Rams looking like the toughest matchup on the schedule for every team that will face them next season.

title: Updated Quinshon Judkins’ Fantasy Outlook 2026: Why the Browns RB Is Priced Too High
description: Quinshon Judkins enters his second professional season recovering from a brutal dislocated ankle and fractured fibula suffered on December 21 (Week 16) of his rookie campaign. While the late-season injury understandably gives fantasy football managers pause, his collegiate resume proves he is built for the long haul.
fullText:
Quinshon Judkins enters his second professional season recovering from a brutal dislocated ankle and fractured fibula suffered on December 21 (Week 16) of his rookie campaign. While the late-season injury understandably gives fantasy football managers pause, his collegiate resume proves he is built for the long haul. Having logged two collegiate seasons with over 280 touches, there is absolutely no doubt that his frame can confidently handle a massive, traditional workhorse role, something that is very much his to lose entering 2026.

However, translating that volume into reliable fantasy production is where the major concerns lie. Last season, Judkins struggled with efficiency, posting an ugly 3.6 yards per carry. Of course, only so much of that was his fault, but he has to play the hand he is dealt and I'm not sold that he's got significantly more help for Year 2.

In college, he was an absolute touchdown machine, scoring 16 or more touchdowns in all three of his collegiate seasons. Unfortunately, that kind of elite scoring ceiling simply isn't happening here in Cleveland. The structural roadblocks in this offense make it incredibly difficult for any running back to find the end zone with that sort of consistency., even with a plus role that saw him touch the ball 18.3 times per game in 2025.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

Judkins should theoretically sustain his high-end volume, making him a relatively safe compiler of touches that can be slotted into fantasy lineups, even without a ceiling of note. But unless this Browns offense as a whole takes a massive step forward and produces well above expectations, his weekly potential remains tightly capped.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

The narrow range of outcomes isn't a terrible thing if you get him at the right cost, but right now, he's priced a bit above that. Without much in the way of scoring equity, I am simply not sure he will consistently finish among the 20 most productive running backs on a week-to-week basis.

He is a volume-based flex option, but you should temper your expectations and look for spike weeks elsewhere.

title: NFL waiver wire explained and the Eagles’ position in the claiming order
description: The preseason is almost over and NFL teams have until Sunday, August 30 at 6:00 PM Eastern to get their roster down to just 53 players. 37 players from each team will end up waived or released (if not traded or injury designated), and teams then have an opportunity to put a claim on any […]
fullText:
The preseason is almost over and NFL teams have until Sunday, August 30 at 6:00 PM Eastern to get their roster down to just 53 players.

37 players from each team will end up waived or released (if not traded or injury designated), and teams then have an opportunity to put a claim on any player subject to the waiver wire — and they have until Monday, August 31 at 1:00 to make those decisions. Players claimed will head off to their new teams, and those that pass through unclaimed, will become unrestricted free agents. From there, teams will fill their 16-man practice squads and finalize things heading into Week 1 of the regular season.

Not all players are subject to the waiver wire, however, vested veterans — players who have four years of accrued NFL service time — are outright released. Those players become free agents right away. Teams who are concerned about losing a young player on the waiver wire, might consider releasing a vested veteran on the bubble instead, whom they can bring back immediately on the practice squad, or to the active roster after moving someone else to the scout team.

The Eagles currently sit at the No. 23 spot on the waiver wire, which mirrors the 2026 NFL Draft order. Last year, Howie Roseman claimed center Willie Lampkin, who was waived by the Los Angeles Rams. And Lampkin has been a training camp standout this summer.

The NFL waiver order during the preseason and the first three weeks of the regular season reflects the 2026 NFL Draft order, and then after four games, the order resets to the current league standings. So, right now, the Raiders currently have first pick at every player on waivers. The wire order is also fixed, so the Raiders will get first rights to every single player available regardless of whether they pick one (or many).

title: Florida native Ross Chastain calls Daytona Cup pole a "life achievement"
description: Chastain grew up less than two hours away from Daytona International Speedway
fullText:
Ross Chastain has never been known for his qualifying performances. In fact, he became the only driver to ever win the Coca-Cola 600 from last place on the grid in 2025.

But Friday at Daytona, he rocketed to the top of the charts, taking pole position by half-a-tenth over Chris Buescher.

It's just Chastain's third career pole in the NASCAR Cup Series, with his other two P1s coming at Watkins Glen in 2024 and Nashville in 2023 (a race he won).

"Yeah, it's almost indescribable," Chastain said of the pole in a post-qualifying press conference. "I think I should probably start with, like, I grasp that it doesn't have much bearing on knowing what tomorrow is going to bring, but for tonight and today for a new package, for Trackhouse to go and pick the right things for car build to come here and to execute through two rounds, it's incredible. We've been good in one round before, but not the second. So, yeah, it's very important to note that we chose the right things as a team to come here and execute through qualifying.

"I'll start this with -- I do not know what that means for tomorrow. I'm being honest, I have no idea what it means for tomorrow."

Of course, as Chastain notes, qualifying means very little a superspeedway. Last year, Ryan Blaney won the race from P1, but qualifying was rained out. The last true Daytona pole-sitter to win the race was Dale Earnhardt Jr. in the summer of 2015.

But besides that, it's still a very special moment for the Florida driver.

"Life achievement," said Chastain. "I was a kid sitting in the grandstands. We camped outside of turn one, gate 40. For those that remember back in, I don't know, late 90s, 2000s, early 2000s, it was not the nice, beautiful gate 40 with dry grass that you see now. It was a mud pit. We camped over there, rode our bikes around and had other families that were family and some that were more than family that were such close friends and my buddies that I grew up with.

"So, yeah, I mean, from the race pools, like getting the race day paper and drawing names out that they would cut up and hoping you got the pole-sitter, that was a big deal. And as I got older, I realized how much little or just less it means, as far as how the car is going to draft. But, still, it's a big deal. It's a life achievement that I will never forget. This is a moment I'll never forget."

It was also a great day for Trackhouse as an organization, with Chastain's teammates Shane van Gisbergen and Connor Zilisch qualifying sixth and seventh, respectively.

SVG is trying to hold onto the 16th and final spot inside the Chase field, and Chastain is fully aware of the role he may play in that battle.

"When there's an opportunity of two cars in front of me, I think everybody in the field knows that I'll push the 97 [SVG]," said Chastain. "I am OEM loyal and specifically 97 loyal. So when there's opportunity, any momentum I have, any push I have, will go to the 97. The crew chiefs will be talking. You know, there's little differences, and if we find something air pressure wise or something, the 97 will be the first to know."

However, Chastain surely wants to win too, as he is facing a winless streak that dates back to Memorial Day Weekend, 2025. Daytona will mark 49 races since his last trip to Cup Series Victory Lane, and the driver of the No. 1 has also managed to win at least one race in every year of the Next Gen era (since 2022).

title: Updated Breece Hall Fantasy Outlook 2026: Jets RB Is a Safe Option
description: It is difficult to feel much conviction regarding Breece Hall this season. Offensive limitations have hindered his production throughout his entire career, and that trend projects to continue in 2026.
fullText:
It is difficult to feel much conviction regarding Breece Hall this season. Offensive limitations have hindered his production throughout his entire career, and that trend projects to continue in 2026.

Despite his undeniable talent and a featured role in the backfield, Hall has yet to rush for more than five touchdowns in a single season. He also has not surpassed 1,100 rushing yards in a campaign. He functions as the running back version of Garrett Wilson: both players serve as a stark reminder that raw talent and fantasy points are not directly correlated, no matter how much we want them to be.

However, Hall does provide stable floor elements for fantasy managers:

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

Availability: He has registered only two absences over the past three seasons.

Receiving Volume: He has recorded two separate seasons with more than 55 receptions.

Explosiveness: Since 2022, among running backs with at least 500 carries, Hall ranks 10th in the percentage of rushes gaining 10 or more yards. He trails names like De'Von Achane, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jaylen Warren, James Cook, Bijan Robinson, James Conner, Nick Chubb, Kenneth Walker III, and Christian McCaffrey.

The New York Jets offense remains a significant hurdle. Geno Smith now leads the unit, and the front office just invested heavy draft capital into a pair of pass catchers. This specific offensive environment restricts Hall's scoring upside and makes a true statistical breakout highly unlikely.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

You can safely draft Hall in the third round as your RB2. He will likely provide a baseline of production through his receiving work and breakaway runs, much like what we've seen to date. However, expecting a massive breakthrough campaign in an offense led by Smith is not a wise strategy.

He's not winning you your league, but he's probably not costing you a chance to compete either.

title: Elversberg stun Leverkusen on Bundesliga debut, Leipzig glisten
description: Elversberg enjoyed a dream Bundesliga debut as one of the smallest clubs ever to grace the German top flight humbled 2024 champions Bayer Leverkusen 3-2 at home on Saturday. Saarland-based Elversberg, from a district of just 13,000 people and a village of only 7,000, made an early mockery of pundits who said they would struggle badly in their first season after promotion.
fullText:
Elversberg enjoyed a dream Bundesliga debut as one of the smallest clubs ever to grace the German top flight humbled 2024 champions Bayer Leverkusen 3-2 at home on Saturday.

Saarland-based Elversberg, from a district of just 13,000 people and a village of only 7,000, made an early mockery of pundits who said they would struggle badly in their first season after promotion.

In front of 10,000 fans at the URSAPHARM Arena with just three sides and a slew of temporary structures, Lukas Petkov struck on 8 minutes and ex-Borussia Dortmund youth prospect Cole Campbell netted straight after.

David Mokwa made it 3-0 right at the start of the second half. Patrik Schick's flick for Leverkusen was their first shot on goal and Christian Kofane's second in injury time set up a nervous finish, but the home side hung on.

It was an abject Bundesliga start for new Leverkusen coach Carles Martínez, especially as new captain Edmund Tapsoba was at fault for the first two goals, presenting US forward Campbell with the ball for the swift second.

New RB Leipzig boss Martín Demichelis had a winning start on his return to the Bundesliga as a coach, Ridle Baku, Antonio Nusa and Rocco Reitz netting in a 3-0 home win over Reitz's ex-side Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Former Bayern Munich defender Demichelis was appointed at Leipzig in the close season after Ole Werner was sacked despite finishing in third.

Younes Ebnoutalib scored a hat-trick but Eintracht Frankfurt's returning coach Adi Hütter, previously in charge 2018-21, had to make do with a 3-3 draw at Union Berlin.

The hosts, under new boss Mauro Lustrinelli, showed off their dead-ball expertise as Emmanuel Latte Lath headed in an early corner past new Eagles keeper Noah Atubolu.

But Ebnoutalib soon hit a quick double, including a second which was confirmed by goal-line technology, before completing his treble in the second period. Leopold Querfeld made up for a mistake for a Frankfurt goal with another header from a corner for Union, and Tim Skarke netted a leveller in stoppage time.

Cologne hit back three times to beat Hoffenheim 3-2 in the cathedral city and newcomers Paderborn drew 0-0 at Mainz.

title: Caitlin Clark Gives Encouraging Health Update After Fever Win
description: It was truly a dominating night for the Indiana Fever, as they picked up an 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday.The story of the game was the combination of Fever guards Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, each scoring 34 points in the win. Clark had a double-double as well with 12 assists, 5 […] The post Caitlin Clark Gives Encouraging Health Update After Fever Win appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
It was truly a dominating night for the Indiana Fever, as they picked up an 111-91 win over the Connecticut Sun on Friday.

The story of the game was the combination of Fever guards Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell, each scoring 34 points in the win. Clark had a double-double as well with 12 assists, 5 rebounds, and 3 steals. She made history as the first WNBA player to ever have consecutive games with 30+ points and 10+ assists double-doubles.

One concern about Clark was her back injury, which has lingered for the last two months. With the World Cup around the corner and Clark about to play for Team USA, many wonder how her health is.

Clark had a chance to speak with the media after the Fever beat the Sun. She was asked about her health, and it was the kind of update that Fever fans needed to hear.

"I feel probably the best I've ever felt in my career," Clark said. "It was battle for like the first 20 games for me to really find my confidence again, mostly in my body. Now, I feel like I'm just playing. I'm not thinking."

#Fever star Caitlin Clark on her back/overall health:

“I feel probably the best I’ve ever felt in my career …”

“It was battle for like the first 20 games for me to really find my confidence again, mostly in my body. Now, I feel like I’m just playing. I’m not thinking.” pic.twitter.com/i3c0jC15GV

— James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 29, 2026

In 36 games this season, Clark is averaging 22.5 points, 8.4 assists, 3.9 rebounds, and 1 steal per contest. She leads the WNBA in assists per game and is third in scoring.

The Fever enter the World Cup break with a 26-14 overall record and sit in fourth in the standings. They are 2.5 games behind the Golden State Valkyries for second in the playoff hunt.

Clark is about to take off to play in the World Cup for Team USA. The hope is that she can stay healthy with fewer minutes. Team USA will play as many of its players as possible. Clark could be looking at 15 to 20 minutes per game at most.

As for the rest of the Fever, they will use this time to rest and prepare for the last four games of the regular season. They won't be back in action until September 18 when they face the Toronto Tempo.

After that game, though, the Fever have the Washington Mystics and close with a two-game series against the Minnesota Lynx. Those will be games where Clark needs to be 100% healthy. The Fever are going to be in for a demanding playoff run.
