title: Tadej Pogacar abandons Vuelta a Espana after nasty crash on stage eight
description: Tadej Pogacar was riding the Vuelta for the first time since 2019 and was the heavy favourite to clinch a seventh grand tour crown
fullText:
Six-time grand tour champion and Vuelta a Espana leader Tadej Pogacar has abandoned the race after a nasty crash on stage eight.

The two-time world champion was the overwhelming favourite to win the Vuelta, the only grand tour he has yet to win, and won three stages in its opening week. He led the race by nearly four minutes from Movistar's Enric Mas before his shock crash and abandon with around 33km to go on stage eight.

The race leader appeared to swerve suddenly while travelling in the midst of the peloton along a wide road and crashed hard, with riders falling around and behind him.

He sustained a nasty wound to his left shoulder and the left side of his face, with blood pouring from above his eye and his shoulder, and was immediately attended to by medical staff.

The Slovenian got up unassisted and appeared ready to get back on his bike before shaking his head and sitting down again, before he was helped into a waiting ambulance by staff and taken immediately to hospital.

This is the first time Pogacar has abandoned a grand tour in 10 attempts, the first time he has ever not finished on the podium, and his first withdrawal from a race since breaking his wrist in a crash at Liege-Bastogne-Liege in 2023.

The 27-year-old won this year's Tour de France in dominant fashion and carried that form into an electric first week at the Vuelta, winning stages one, four and six on his way to establishing a seemingly unassailable lead.

But his crash on an innocuous-seeming stretch of road on the way to Xeraco - reminiscent of his rival Jonas Vingegaard's unexpected crash on stage 15 of this year's Tour - blows the race wide open.

Spain's Mas now leads the overall standings by one minute from Slovenia's four-time champion Primoz Roglic, with Giro d'Italia runner-up Felix Gall third at 1'11". Britain's Oscar Onley leads the best young rider classification and now sits fifth, 2'16" off the pace.

Pogacar's withdrawal also entirely changes the dynamic of the race. His UAE Team Emirates-XRG squad are now likely to target stage wins through the likes of Joao Almeida and Jay Vine, while Visma-Lease a Bike, who had largely been expected to aim for stages through Wout van Aert and two-time stage winner Matthew Brennan, may now prioritise the general classification hopes of Sepp Kuss. The American won this race in 2023 and now sits fourth overall.

title: Tyler Loop dismisses any concern after two more missed field goals
description: Tyler Loop says he isn't worried about his preseason struggles, but the Ravens and their fans have every right to be.
fullText:
The Baltimore Ravens couldn't have asked for a more impressive preseason. A final tune-up was scheduled for Friday night, and they responded by beating their opponent soundly. The Washington Commanders have a lot to talk about. It's like the guys they fielded had concluded there was no real reason to fight anymore and that their futures had already been settled. 41-3 would be the final score in this one, with the Ravens ending up on the right side of the scoring tally.

But alas, there's more to discuss. Most of the conversation afterward centered on a dominant team performance, young players making cases for roster spots, and a preseason that largely went according to plan. Yet one storyline continues to follow the Ravens into Week 1. Tyler Loop's struggles aren't going away.

The second-year kicker missed two of four field-goal attempts in the preseason finale, finishing the preseason 5-for-8 on field goals. While he remained perfect on extra points, the inconsistency has fueled questions about whether Baltimore can trust him when a game is hanging in the balance.

Asked after the game whether his preseason struggles were cause for concern, Loop didn't hesitate.

That's the answer Ravens fans probably expected. It seems as expected he'd express confidence, but it's also the answer that Baltimore's fans likely didn't want to hear. Loop explained that this past week was one of his best stretches of practice and said things are beginning to click. At the same time, he acknowledged that progress in practice has to translate to game situations and admitted his performance against Washington wasn't good enough.

Ravens K Tyler Loop finished the preseason 5-of-8 on field goal attempts.

He said after Friday's win over the Commanders that his issues are not cause for concern. pic.twitter.com/vaAdL53vEI

That honesty matters. So does confidence. A kicker who publicly questions himself isn't helping anyone. Loop wasn't about to stand in front of reporters and declare he can't handle the job. Still, it's understandable why his response may leave some Ravens fans uneasy.

Baltimore's season ended last year with a missed kick in a critical moment. Fair or not, every miss this summer has reopened that wound. The Ravens don't appear ready to make any rash decisions, but they also aren't blindly ignoring the situation. Head Coach Jesse Minter discussed this postgame.

"I think you want to see makes in games, and so it's something we'll continue to look at. "He has had a good camp overall, but again, it comes down to making the kicks in the pressure situations in the games."I think you want to see makes in games, and so it's something we'll continue to look at. We'll continue to look at what the best situation is there. He has had a good camp overall, but again, it coms down to making the kicks in the pressure situations in the games. That's something that we'll always be looking at to make sure we're doing what's best for the team"

When asked whether Baltimore could bring in competition, Minter left every option on the table.

"I think there's a million scenarios there to try to make sure we have the best situation headed into Indianapolis."

That's probably where things stand. Loop isn't worried. The Ravens aren't publicly sounding alarms, either. The problem is that confidence and results haven't matched often enough this summer. Loop believes things are beginning to click. Baltimore's coaching staff is still evaluating every option. Until those two realities meet somewhere in the middle, the conversation surrounding the Ravens' kicking situation isn't likely to fade anytime soon.

Loop believes the breakthrough is coming. The Ravens are betting that he's right, but they might want to invest in some insurance just in case theories are in error.

title: Detroit Lions may face one obstacle in any Christian Gonzalez trade pursuit
description: Detroit’s defense intercepted 13 passes last season, tied for 11th in the NFL. Four of those came from cornerbacks, and D.J. Reed accounted for two of them. Carter Bahns and Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports named the Lions on Thursday among five potential landing spots for New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, alongside the Dallas […] The post Detroit Lions may face one obstacle in any Christian Gonzalez trade pursuit appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Detroit's defense intercepted 13 passes last season, tied for 11th in the NFL. Four of those came from cornerbacks, and D.J. Reed accounted for two of them.

Carter Bahns and Zachary Pereles of CBS Sports named the Lions on Thursday among five potential landing spots for New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, alongside the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders, New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Terrion Arnold, the 24th pick of the 2024 draft, was released by Detroit in June while facing felony charges he has denied, and he agreed to terms with Seattle this month. Reed inherited the No. 1 job, and the group behind him has been shuffled and interrupted by injuries throughout camp.

Tim Twentyman wrote in the club's own training camp position preview in last month that "the Arnold release hurts Detroit's depth at the position," adding it would not surprise him if general manager Brad Holmes added to the spot before the regular season. That went up five weeks before Gonzalez's name entered the conversation, written by someone the team employs.

Detroit ranked 28th in opponent passer rating in the red zone last season at 104.3, allowing 19 passing touchdowns inside its own 20-yard line without intercepting a throw there. Reed's year split around a hamstring strain that cost him six games, and he turns 30 in November.

Gonzalez turned 24 this summer and has two seasons left on his contract. He closed 2025 with three pass breakups and four solo tackles in New England's Super Bowl LX loss to the Seahawks.

The #Lions are listed as a top landing spot for #Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez if he were to be traded Per CBS Sports pic.twitter.com/shw9ae09nF

— NFL Rumors (@nflrums) August 29, 2026

Gonzalez is playing on a rookie deal worth $4.8 million this season that runs through 2027 after New England exercised his fifth-year option in April. Detroit would inherit two years of control and an immediate negotiation, and that negotiation now starts from a number set this month in Seattle, where Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year extension averaging $33 million a season with $101 million in total guarantees and just over $59 million locked in at signing.

The draft compensation would be the cheaper half of the transaction. Bahns and Pereles made that point about the Lions specifically, writing that a long-term deal for Gonzalez would limit Detroit's flexibility at other positions and that the club can carry it only because the money would not take effect until next year.

Robert Kraft said at the start of training camp that New England had offered Gonzalez a deal that would make him the highest-paid cornerback in league history and the highest-paid player in franchise history.

"We love Christian Gonzalez," Kraft said. "We love him as a player, as a person. That's why we've made an offer to him that makes him the highest-paid player ever to play that position in the NFL, and coincidentally, it's the highest contract in the Patriots franchise history,"

Adam Schefter said on The Pat McAfee Show during the week that the sides are "obviously not in the same neighborhood right now and haven't been."

Eliot Wolf, the club's executive vice president of player personnel, answered yes this week when asked if New England still intends to reach that figure.

Gonzalez reported to camp on time and practiced in pads, passing up a holdout that would have cost him $45,000 for every day he missed. He returned to full participation this week after a hard fall on Aug. 10 kept him out of both of the Patriots' first two preseason games. Asked about the standoff, he told reporters it was "frustrating, but I'm focused on the season."

His trainer posted, then deleted, a message on Thursday saying New England should trade him. That remains the loudest anyone in Gonzalez's circle has been all summer.

The Patriots reached Super Bowl LX in February and open this season with a quarterback still on a rookie contract, which places them inside the window where a cornerback of Gonzalez's standing is worth more to them than to anyone else.

title: Kyle Larson Wants to See More NextGen Car Changes: ‘Same Thing’
description: Kyle Larson is hopeful to see more changes to the NextGen car.
fullText:
Kyle Larson would like to see more changes to the NextGen car moving forward. The defending NASCAR Cup Series champion expressed enthusiasm about this Saturday's Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona, which will see a new rules package.

Larson believes the new rules package could be a game-changer in the type of racing seen at "The World Center of Racing." However, the driver of the No. 5 also is not sure it will make a difference.

Regardless, "Yung Money" supports the change and hopes to see more adjustments to the NextGen car in the future.

During a media session on Friday at Daytona, Larson said he is looking forward to trying something new in Saturday's Coke Zero Sugar 400.

Because of the NextGen car, Larson said, things have gotten repetitive in NASCAR. In the weeks following Daytona, the Hendrick Motorsports star would not mind seeing different rules packages for other tracks in an effort to "spice things up."

"I'm just excited to try something new. I feel like so long in the NextGen era it's just every track we go to, it's just the same thing. I'm happy for a change. I would be open to changing packages at other tracks just to spice things up, because it gets kind of repetitive each year," Larson said.

Larson pointed to the lack of parity of competition as to why he would encourage NASCAR to make changes to the NextGen car. The two-time Cup Series champion pointed to Ryan Blaney's victory at New Hampshire last week as an example.

"You see Ryan Blaney win Loudon. He won Loudon last year. It's like the same guys run up front every week that did the year previous," Larson said.

Ironically, Larson is excited about a potentially chaotic Coke Zero Sugar 400. Because everything in the NextGen era has been similar in Larson's opinion, a package change that creates chaos is something that the California native is anticipating.

"It's weird because a lot of us complain that Daytona and Talladega and tracks are too chaotic and there's crashing and all this stuff. Then, it's like it got so boring, we want the chaos, so that's why we're at this point of changing the package," Larson said.

When speaking to his No. 5 team earlier in the week, Larson was led to believe the attempt to reduce downforce might not make a difference. Yet, the 32-time Cup Series winner remains unclear on what to expect.

"I was like, 'Tell me how crazy it's going to be this week.' They're like, 'Yeah, it's less downforce, but then you just raise the front of your car and you get all that downforce back, or a lot of it back. I'm not sure. I hope it's a lot different," Larson said.

title: Iraola angry as official's board delays subs before goal
description: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he was angry about being prevented from making a triple substitution sooner during his side's draw against Nottingham Forest.
fullText:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says he was angry about being prevented from making a triple substitution sooner during Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw against Nottingham Forest.

With the game level at 1-1 during the second half at Anfield, the Basque wanted to bring on Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha.

However, despite the ball going out of play three times, the players were left waiting on the sideline as fourth official Tim Robinson had problems with the board.

To add to Liverpool's frustrations, the third time the ball went out, instead of play stopping for the changes, Forest took a quick throw-in from which they won a penalty to retake the lead.

Forest wing-back Neco Williams darted in behind the Liverpool backline and was caught by goalkeeper Alisson as he lifted a shot goalwards.

When it drifted wide, referee Samuel Barrott blew his whistle and pointed to the spot.

"With the penalty, the situation has already finished when the contact appears. And it's not an aggressive contact," Iraola told BBC Match of the Day.

"But more than this we complained about the subs. We had to wait about three minutes.

"He was having an issue with the board, I don't know if it was not working, but we definitely wanted to do the subs the last two or three stoppages before the goal.

"It wasn't just that reason but everything helps."

Speaking to TNT Sports, he added: "A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes. We'd already given him the subs two or three minutes before.

"I was already angry because in the previous stoppage we couldn't make the subs and then before throw-in I thought we could do it.

"I don't know, they will have to explain it. But it has taken ages."

Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard believed they could have no complaints over the award of the penalty itself but empathised with Iraola's anger over the substitutes.

"You can understand the frustration - in this day and age, with all the technology, it can't be taking three minutes to make a triple substitution," he told TNT Sports.

"But I think it's a small problem in the overall problem because it's a goal that can be avoided."

Ex-Liverpool and England full-back Stephen Warnock agreed with his old team-mate.

"Andoni Iraola wanted to make a triple change and the assistant referee hasn't got the thing done," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"It would've completely stopped the play. It's appalling from the fourth official."

Liverpool were able to salvage a point from the game as Victor Munoz scored his first goal for the club with eight minutes remaining.

title: How would you split the 49ers’ RB workload in 2026?
description: Christian McCaffrey and now Kaelon Black—how do you divide the snaps with this promising rookie entering the fold?
fullText:
There are two good things: Christian McCaffrey will be available in Week 1 of 2026, and the 49ers have a nice rookie to try out in Kaelon Black. Brian Robinson Jr., the running back behind McCaffrey last year, was a significant upgrade, and Black might be even better.

Behind those two, well, whoever doesn't get cut. Probably Jordan James, maybe Sincere McCormick.

Black has been impressive in the preseason. So much you could overreact that he might be an heir apparent to McCaffrey—because McCaffrey isn't going to play forever. That said, he has a lot of football left in him, but maybe, just once, the 49ers have an option that isn't 80 percent of McCaffrey's snaps.

If anything, Black should quickly give Kyle Shanahan confidence that pulling McCaffrey for a play or two isn't a hindrance. Something he said he finally was able to do last year when I asked this same question:

"[When] Christian goes out," Shanahan said during his segment on KNBR's Dirty Work, "Whether it's a run play or pass play, it's tough. Because you know he's such a good runner and such a good receiver. But now, when you have a really, really good back behind him, and we take Christian out and things like that, you're not so upset on all these plays because you know you've got a guy coming in there who you shouldn't miss a beat on."

Of course, McCaffrey played nearly 83 percent of the offensive snaps during the 2025 season. So apparently those plays off came few and far between.

Black is a rookie; Robinson wasn't. So the first order of business is Black getting Shanahan's trust and holding onto it. That means holding onto the ball when he gets it.

Unlike last year, snaps for a third running back might not be as necessary—if they are, something has gone horribly wrong. I remain convinced McCaffrey should get 65 percent of the snaps. Give 30 percent to Black, provided all that optimism he's shown in the preseason doesn't go "poof" in Weeks 1 and 2, and the remaining five to Jordan James. I'm basically saying Black should get a larger role so McCaffrey can rest, and it's not like the 49ers offense is down a player when he takes the field. They might not miss a beat.

That's obviously asking a lot since Shanahan tends to run McCaffrey way more than many armchair GMs think he should. More likely than not, McCaffrey will be going 90 percent of the time this year simply because he's CMC and he's that good. That said, if we're being logical about it, what is your pitch count between what most likely will be the 49ers' running back room?

title: NEW UFC Bantamweight Rankings After Song Shockingly Smashes Nurmagomedov at UFC Shanghai
description: In the early morning hours in the United States, the MMA world leader returned to Paramount+ for UFC Shanghai. The […]
fullText:
In the early morning hours in the United States, the MMA world leader returned to Paramount+ for UFC Shanghai. The card in China was headlined by a major matchup at bantamweight when rankings regular and native son, Yadong Song, took on top-five fighter Umar Nurmagomedov.

Despite the former title challenger being a solid favorite heading into the bout, the "Kung Fu Kid" scored a huge knockout victory in Round 2. Following the win, let's take a look at the updated UFC bantamweight rankings and where Song lands.

Marlon Vera has been one of the division's most entertaining fighters over the last six years. However, while he did eventually get himself a title opportunity, he has gone into a steep decline since trying to take the top spot at the mountaintop.

The fan-favorite Ecuadorian has lost four straight, with his latest coming in February as he came up just short in a clash with David Martinez in Mexico City. "Chito's" days as a top-10 fighter seem to be numbered.

After a pair of losses, Aiemann Zahabi was probably one more loss away from having to look for a job elsewhere. However, over the last five years, he has won seven straight, including a huge UFC 315 win over living legend Jose Aldo, then in his native Canada over Marlon Vera.

He got the biggest opportunity of his career at UFC Freedom 250 when he took on former champion Sean O'Malley. Unfortunately for him, he was outclassed and knocked out in Round 2. The loss probably ends the 38-year-old's hopes of ever fighting for UFC gold.

Cory Sandhagen has been many fight fans' favorite bantamweight for several years. He is gutsy, highly skilled, and rarely in a boring fight. In October 2025, he finally got an elusive title opportunity at UFC 320. Unfortunately, despite his best efforts, he was just another victim of former bantamweight king Merab Dvalishvili.

Sandhagen was back in the Octagon at UFC 329 but was outworked by rising star Mario Bautista. He has now lost three of his last four and is as far outside the title picture as he has ever been.

Umar Nurmagomedov has been one of the best bantamweights in the world for quite some time. In 2025, he had the chance to be the second Nurmagomedov to win gold in the UFC, but came up just short in a highly competitive clash with champion Merab Dvalishvili.

Following the defeat, he scored a pair of important decision wins over ranked fighters, Mario Bautista and Deiveson Figueiredo. However, with a possible title opportunity on the line, the Russian was shockingly KO'd by top-10 stalwart Song Yadong at UFC Shanghai in August. Ending any hope of a championship fight in 2026.

Yadong Song has long been seen as a fighter with the potential to fight for gold in the UFC one day. However, after putting a few wins together, he always seems to be halted by a key loss to one or two of the division's elites. That happened over the last couple of years when he lost matchups against former champions Sean O'Malley and Petr Yan.

However, following his loss to the American earlier this year, the Chinese star has rebounded with big wins. First, a submission victory over former flyweight champ Deiveson Figueiredo in May. Then at UFC Shanghai a few months later, he scored a nasty KO win over former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov. Thrusting him back into the contender conversation.

After an outstanding run in Combate Global, where he went 10-1, David Martinez has emerged as a top 10 bantamweight in the No. 1 company in the world, the UFC. After earning a contract on Dana White's Contender Series in 2024, he has reeled off three straight wins in the Octagon. Including a big victory over Marlon Vera in February. He has fairly earned his spot in our rankings after winning 10 straight overall.

Since his UFC debut seven years ago, Mario Bautista has steadily climbed the rankings. Scoring wins over top 15 talent like Jose Aldo and Ricky Simon. However, the biggest win of his career came at UFC 329 when he got a chance at revenge against Cory Sandhagen. The man who beat him in his UFC debut.

After three hard-fought rounds, the MMA Lab product earned a decision win and is right on the cusp of a title opportunity in the next year.

Former champ Sean O'Malley is one of the UFC's most popular fighters. He has the unique look, charisma, and most importantly, the knockout striking that turns fighters into stars. However, his back-to-back losses to the division's former champ have pushed "Suga" to the back of the contender line. But he has found new momentum in recent fights.

He was in a must-win situation at UFC 324 if he ever wanted to fight for gold again. In a hard-fought bout, he got a big W against top-10 fighter Yadong Song. O'Malley then followed it up with a TKO win over a surging Aiemann Zahabi at UFC Freedom 250. The win may have earned him a title shot in his next bout.

Merab Dvalishvili truly is "The Machine." His relentlessness and wrestling have turned him into one of the greatest bantamweights of all time. If there were any doubters after his 2024 win over Sean O'Malley, he silenced them with a decisive rematch victory, as well as two other title defenses.

However, staying at the top is always tough, and his title reign came to a definitive end at UFC 323 at the hands of Petr Yan. While he is no longer the champ, his place in division history is set.

Three straight losses had many wondering if Petr Yan's days as a top-five bantamweight were over. However, his recent wins over Yadon Song, Deiveson Figueiredo, and Marcus McGhee helped rebuild his title contender status. Earning a title shot at UFC 323.

In a rematch with a man who defeated him two years ago, the Russian was the greatest version of himself as he decisively defeated Merab Dvalishvili to become a two-time bantamweight champion. "No Mercy" proved he is completely back to being an elite fighter in the world.

title: Bills cut receiver Mecole Hardman, punter Mitch Wishnowsky
description: As the Bills pare down their roster from 90 to 53 players, they're getting rid of a well-known veteran wide receiver and picking a winner in their punter competition.
fullText:
As the Bills pare down their roster from 90 to 53 players, they're getting rid of a well-known veteran wide receiver and picking a winner in their punter competition.

Wide receiver Mecole Hardman is being released, according to Jeremy Fowler. Hardman, best known for scoring the game-winning touchdown for the Chiefs in overtime of Super Bowl LVIII, signed with the Bills late last season and caught a touchdown pass for them in their playoff loss to the Broncos. He will now be a free agent.

The Bills have also decided to cut veteran punter Mitch Wishnowsky, according to Tom Pelissero. Wishnowsky was in a training camp competition with seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman, and it appears that Doman has won.

The Bills and all other teams must be down to 53 players on the active roster by 6 p.m. ET tomorrow.

title: ‘Did nothing wrong’ – Caitlin Clark fans livid over sideline spat with Fever assistant Briann January
description: Caitlin Clark made headlines for her performance on the court against the Connecticut Sun, but there was one moment in particular that piqued fans’ interest. Caitlin Clark tore up the record books again during Friday’s 111-91 blowout against the Connecticut Sun, dropping 34 points and 12 assists.
fullText:
Caitlin Clark made headlines for her performance on the court against the Connecticut Sun, but there was one moment in particular that piqued fans' interest.

Caitlin Clark tore up the record books again during Friday's 111-91 blowout against the Connecticut Sun, dropping 34 points and 12 assists. Late in the fourth quarter, with Indiana holding a 13-point lead, a defensive miscommunication opened the door for a Connecticut bucket after Mercedes Russell was slow to rotate over.

Head coach Stephanie White immediately called a timeout, leading to a heated exchange where assistant Briann January appeared to single out Caitlin Clark for the breakdown.

Clark's reaction spoke volumes, as she threw her hands up and animatedly argued her case.

Fans on X took Clark's side too, as they aimed criticism at the Fever assistant coach.

One fan claimed it was Mercedes' fault: "Big lost her man and then went over the screen. 100% not CC's fault."

"January has a problem. I don't like her doing this with CC." Another said.

This supporter suggested January is jealous: "Everyone wants to get a credit for her success."

title: Joel Barlow grad TJ Baer named FCBL Defensive Player of the Year
description: Former Joel Barlow standout TJ Baer has been named FCBL Defensive Player of the Year for his efforts in the outfield.
fullText:
Former Joel Barlow baseball standout TJ Baer earned postseason recognition from the Futures Collegiate Baseball League of New England.

The former GametimeCT All-State first team selection was named FCBL Defensive Player of the Year, according to a Thursday morning release. Baer was all over the outfield for the Norwich Sea Unicorns, who reached the FCBL semifinals.

Baer played in 43 games, starting 42 of them. He recorded seven assists and made just two errors in 93 chances between right field, center field and left field. Baer started 20 games in right, 19 in center and three in left. He didn't make an error in his first 21 games with Norwich this summer.

Baer recorded two assists in a 3-1 win over the Nashua Silver Knights on July 24. In the top of the sixth inning, Nashua led, 1-0, and was looking for more when Mike Villani singled to right field. Baer came up firing, however, and threw a strike to catcher Bryce Miller to nail Hudson Story at the plate. Baer threw out a runner trying to go to second base on a fielder's choice in the top of the ninth.

At the plate, Baer batted .318, posted a 4.21 on-base percentage, and stole 19 bases in 20 attempts. The Easton native is heading into his sophomore year at Marist College.

title: Buccaneers roster cuts tracker: Live updates as Bucs trim roster to 53
description: Follow every Buccaneers roster cut as Tampa Bay trims its roster to 53 players ahead of Sunday's deadline.
fullText:
The preseason is officially in the books for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, which means the focus now shifts toward building the roster that will open the 2026 regular season.

Tampa Bay must reduce its roster to 53 players by Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline, and the first wave of moves is already underway. The Bucs have decisions to make throughout the depth chart after three preseason games gave the coaching staff one final opportunity to evaluate the roster.

Some players who don't survive the initial cut could still return on the practice squad, while others will hit the waiver wire and potentially get an opportunity elsewhere.

Bucs Wire will keep track of every reported and confirmed roster move as Tampa Bay works its way toward the initial 53-man roster.

Linebacker John Bullock is among the first players waived as the Buccaneers begin trimming their roster.

Bullock returned to Tampa Bay during the offseason after initially joining the organization as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He faced a crowded competition at inside linebacker this summer, with Alex Anzalone, Josiah Trotter, Christian Rozeboom, SirVocea Dennis and others battling for spots and roles.

Undrafted rookie running back Barika Kpeenu has also been waived.

Kpeenu joined the Buccaneers during the preseason and was competing for a spot in a backfield led by Bucky Irving. With veterans Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker also in the mix, there were limited roster spots available behind Tampa Bay's starter.

Second-year quarterback Connor Bazelak is also being waived as Tampa Bay begins sorting out its quarterback depth chart.

Bazelak spent time with the Buccaneers as a rookie in 2025 but entered this preseason facing a much different quarterback room. Baker Mayfield remains entrenched as the starter, while veteran Jake Browning and rookie Jalon Daniels have been competing for the backup roles.

This tracker will continue to be updated as additional Buccaneers roster moves are reported ahead of Sunday's deadline.

title: Real Madrid complete final training session ahead of Málaga clash
description: Mourinho’s side wrapped up preparations at Valdebebas, with seven players continuing individual recovery work
fullText:
Real Madrid completed their final training session on Saturday ahead of Sunday's La Liga meeting with Málaga at the Santiago Bernabéu.

José Mourinho's team returns home looking to maintain its perfect start to the league campaign after victories over Espanyol and Real Sociedad. The Málaga game, which kicks off at 5 p.m. local time, is Real Madrid's third match of the new La Liga season.

Saturday's session at Real Madrid City began with warm-up exercises on the pitch before Mourinho and his staff moved the squad into tactical work. The players then went through pressing and possession drills, with the session concluding with a series of small-sided games.

The injury situation remains unchanged heading into the weekend. Aurélien Tchouaméni, Raúl Asencio, Ferland Mendy, Éder Militão, Rodrygo, Endrick, and Thiago Pitarch all continued with individual recovery programs rather than taking part in the full session.

Militão and Endrick were able to work separately on an adjacent pitch as they continue progressing from their respective physical issues, while the other unavailable players primarily carried out their recovery work indoors.

With none of the injured players expected to return against Málaga, Mourinho is likely to have a similar group available to the one he called upon for the opening two league fixtures. Academy players Fran González Mestre, Mario Rivas, Jorge Cestero, and Alexis Ciria could therefore remain involved with the first-team squad.

There was also a familiar face at Valdebebas on Saturday morning. Former Real Madrid captain Sergio Ramos visited Real Madrid City ahead of the Málaga game. Ramos, who is currently without a club following the end of his spell in Mexico, returned to the training complex where he spent so many years during his legendary Real Madrid career.

Real Madrid will now turn their attention entirely to Sunday's match as they look to enter the first break in the congested early-season schedule with maximum points from their opening three La Liga games.

title: Skarke rescues point for Union in six-goal thriller with Frankfurt
description: 1. FC Union Berlin opened its 2026/27 Bundesliga campaign on a sunny, 25-degree afternoon in the nation’s capital, hosting Eintracht Frankfurt at Stadion An der Alten Försterei.Union’s 2024/25 ca...
fullText:
1. FC Union Berlin opened its 2026/27 Bundesliga campaign on a sunny, 25-degree afternoon in the nation's capital, hosting Eintracht Frankfurt at Stadion An der Alten Försterei.

Union's 2024/25 campaign saw them under the leadership of Steffen Baumgart and history-making Marie-Louise Eta, moving up two places compared to their 2023/24 season from thirteenth to eleventh - with a 10-9-15 record and 35 points. Their Hessian opponents finished four places above them but could not balance Champions League football with their Bundesliga season, ultimately finishing one spot out of Europe in eighth with an 11-11-12 record and 44 points.

Union are undefeated in their last five matches against Frankfurt going into this meeting (3-2-0), having won their head-to-head matchup at home (4-3) and drawing away (1-1) last season. The last time Frankfurt won was in Berlin on 4. November 2023, a 3-0 result on goals from now-Manchester City FC forward Omar Marmoush (2', 14') and now-Feyenoord SC striker Nacho Ferri (82').

Union Berlin would see the first chance of the match in the second minute, as a cross into the right side of the box from Robin Koch was deflected away by the right leg of Marin Ljubičić for a corner. On the ensuing set piece, Josip Juranović's delivery into the centre of the box was met by a towering header from Ivorian international and new loan signing Emmanuel Latte Lath, above a leaping Noah Atubolu and top-centre to give the hosts the lead.

Ebnoutalib's brace, just 11 minutes into the match, became the third-fastest from a player on the first matchweek of the Bundesliga season - both Frank Mill (Borussia Mönchengladbach - FC Schalke 04, 1984/85) and Kevin Behrens (1. FC Union Berlin - 1. FSV Mainz 05) were able to do so in the first 9 minutes. At 50 seconds between goals, it was also one of the fastest braces in Bundesliga history since this data was counted, with FC Schalke 04's Edu having recorded a 47-second brace against 1. FC Nürnberg during the 2001/02 season.

Five minutes later, Eintracht Frankfurt would win a free kick on the left side of the ground, swung in by Keita Kosugi but cleared away by Rani Khedira. The ensuing corner would ultimately land in front of Younes Ebnoutalib, amidst a scramble at the goalmouth - and he smashed the ball past Matheo Raab and into the bottom-left corner to draw Die Adler level.

Ljubičić would restart play just seconds later, playing the ball back to Leopold Querfeld. The 22-year-old Austrian centre-back took a few seconds to evaluate his passing options, but it was a bit too much time - as Ebnoutalib came charging towards him and ultimately stripped him of possession. It led to a 1-on-1 between Ebnoutalib and Raab, with the former lifting the ball above the 27-year-old German goalkeeper. By the time that Zeno van den Bosch could run in to sweep the ball away, it already crossed the line - and the visitors jumped in front just seconds after finding their equaliser.

Frankfurt would continue to press in the minutes that followed, with Ebnoutalib searching for one of the fastest first half hat-tricks in Bundesliga history. In the eighteenth minute, Koch lobbed the ball into the centre of the box; Ebnoutalib and Can Uzun were both there, but the latter reached out to meet the ball, volleying it just above Raab and out of play for a goal kick to the hosts.

In the twenty-fourth minute, Kosugi would progress the ball for Frankfurt on the left side of the ground. Michel Aebischer lunged in for a harsh tackle and was almost instantly shown the first yellow card of the day by head official Bastian Dankert. The ensuing free kick was whipped in by Uzun, but landed right into the hands of Raab. Union would counter in the minutes that followed, as a pass from Latte Lath on the left side of the Frankfurt third ultimately landed in front of Ljubičić. His sliding chance to tap the ball bottom-right missed by a few metres, going out of play for a goal kick to the visitors.

Four minutes later, the match saw a rare delay, as while Frankfurt were passing the ball around in the centre of the ground, assistant referee René Rohde appeared to have picked up an injury on the sidelines. He abruptly went down the tunnel, with the other assistant official, Mitja Stegemann, relaying information to Dankert. After a six-minute delay, it was ultimately determined that fourth official Konrad Oldhafer would manage the offside flag on the right side of the ground, and that the match would continue with a drop ball.

Just before halftime, Ayoube Amaimouni would get a chance from distance to put Frankfurt into a two-goal advantage. It deflected off the arm of Querfeld - but not enough for Dankert to call a penalty to the visitors, given that the arm of the Austrian defender was close to his body at that moment. That would be the last notable play of the opening term, as the two sides would go into the locker rooms with Eintracht Frankfurt leading by two goals to one.

Shots in the first half finished 5-5, but the three goals were the only shots on target. Eintracht held 59% possession and had a 16% better pass accuracy - 78% on 175 completions, compared to 62% on 96 for Union.

Ljubičić kicked off the second half for the hosts - but after both sides consistently stopped each other in the midfield, it would be the visitors that would get the first chance of the term, albeit from distance. In the fifty-sixth minute, Farès Chaïbi would take a pass from Amaimouni to the centre of the Union half and then smashed a right-footed shot towards the bottom-right corner, not missing by much as it went past a standing Raab but off the side netting.

In the sixty-fifth minute, a long throw from Tim Rothe on the left side of the Eintracht half bounced off the ground, in front of substitute Tim Skarke, who came into the match for Latte Lath just four minutes earlier. The 29-year-old German attacking midfielder tried to half-volley the ball into the top-right corner, but mistimed his kick and the ball went off the back of his boot - directly into the hands of Atubolu.

Two minutes later, Eintracht would make sure that Union could not get .  Elias Baum took possession of the ball on the right side of the hosts' third after a failed clearance from Livan Burcu; his initial pass into the centre of the box, towards Ebnoutalib, was blocked by Burcu, and the rebound appeared to have gone off his arm, which was close to his body. The second attempt, a lob into the box, was successful, and within seconds, Ebnoutalib thundered it into the bottom-right corner to complete the hat-trick. The Union players were adamant that Baum touched it with his arm in an illegal manner, but it was quickly determined by the VAR officials that the contact was incidental - thus, under revised Bundesliga rules implemented in recent years, the goal stood.

Union would get a series of chances to pull the match back within one, none more notable than a cross into the box from Ljubičić that was met by a free header from Skarke in the seventy-fifth minute. Atubolu had a split-second to react to the ball heading towards the top-right corner, but leapt in time to glove it down with both hands.

Two minutes after that, Atubolu made a fine double save, denying a shot from distance towards the bottom-left corner from Rani Khedira, and then leaping to punch away a Josip Juranović shot towards the top-right corner with his left hand. Union would win a corner, cleared by Atubolu for another set piece; that one was quickly taken by Juranović and headed by Querfeld into the bottom-left corner to make the score 2-3.

Despite their best efforts, the hosts were unable to find an equaliser in the remaining ten minutes of the 90. Four minutes of stoppage time were added, Union quickly won a corner, and Juranović's cross was headed towards the bottom-left corner by Querfeld. Atubolu was ready to leap to deny it with both hands, but a deflection from Skarke with the right leg quickly caught him off-guard, tapped into the centre of the goal to send the Alte Försterei into delirium.

Neither side could get a late decider, but for Union, they remained unbeaten in their last six meetings against Frankfurt, with a 3-3 draw in an absolute thriller to open their 2026/27 Bundesliga campaign. Shots in the second half finished 14-7 to Union, 9-1 on target with 56% possession and a 74% accuracy on 151 passes to 72% on 123. Overall, shots finished 19-12 to Union, 10-3 on target with Frankfurt holding 52% possession; pass accuracy finished 75% on 298 passes for Frankfurt, 69% on 245 for Union.

1. FC Union Berlin will make a trip to Nordrhein-Westfalen to take on Bayer 04 Leverkusen in the second matchweek of the new season; that match is set for Saturday, 15.30 (CET). As for Eintracht Frankfurt, they will go back to the familiar Deutsche Bank Park to face FC Augsburg for the Sunday primetime match, with kickoff at 17.30 (CET).

title: ESPN analyst says Bill Belichick is running out of time
description: Bill Belichick isn't getting the benefit of the doubt in his second season at North Carolina.
fullText:
Bill Belichick and the North Carolina Tar Heels kicked off their season in Dublin, Ireland against the TCU Horned Frogs in Week 1. Last season, in Belichick's first game as head coach at North Carolina, TCU beat the Tar Heels, 48-14. North Carolina went on to have a 4-8 season and things aren't much better off the field.

North Carolina football general manager Mike Lombardi was placed on administrative leave in July. Stephen Belichick, the team's defensive coordinator, went on medical leave earlier this month and did not make the trip to Ireland.

On ESPN's College Football Countdown, Booger McFarland made the case that Belichick is running out of time in Chapel Hill and doing a better job coaching may not be enough to save him.

MORE: Dan Orlovsky offers rare defense of Bill Belichick, UNC football

"They may be better, but to your point, the name of the game is winning games," said McFarland. "If they don't win games, what you said earlier could come true which is he may not make it to the end of the season. It's been a drastic shift in philosophy. Last year, 40 transfers. This year they signed 40 freshman. So you know what happens with young guys? You gotta teach them how to play. It takes time to develop a young guy. You know who doesn't have time? Bill Belichick does not have time because they want to win now. It's amazing. They go from up on TCU seven-nothing in the first game. Michael Jordan and Mia Hamm are going crazy in the stands. It's gone downhill ever since."

title: George Russell Pokes Fun at Alex Albon During Mercedes F1 Karting Day
description: George Russell took selected people from the Mercedes F1 bases at Brackley and Brixworth at Kart Silverstone, with some jokes and competition. To unwind after grueling F1 race weekend, Russell took the Mercedes employees from Brackley and Brixworth for a…
fullText:
George Russell took selected people from the Mercedes F1 bases at Brackley and Brixworth at Kart Silverstone, with some jokes and competition.

To unwind after grueling F1 race weekend, Russell took the Mercedes employees from Brackley and Brixworth for a day of fun to go with a karting competition at Silverstone. Due to the limit, only 170 people could be allowed to compete from the 1000 who applied.

The Brit would race them as well. "We're here at Silverstone, doing a team karting day," said Russell. "A thousand people applied from Brackley and Brixworth. We can only fit 170 people. Yeah, really looking forward to it. And I'm going to be racing with them.

It was a fun day which involved some banter from Russell, even recalling his friend Alexander Albon from Williams, spotting the #23 – the Grill the Grid episode working. "He's not very quick. It's a slow stop that one. That's Albon, number 23," joked the Mercedes F1 driver.

The F1 drivers do get the team trackside to such kart events, even dinners. But Russell went ahead and took the team at Brackley and Brixworth, who travel less to races. These sessions with a race winner is always good from unity perspective for mechanics, engineers, marketing, HR, sales, finance etc.

"Yeah, it was good," continued Russell. "It was good fun. Look how greasy it is almost sort of oil coming out of the tarmac. Oh, look at the drift (pointing the camera to the race). Real good, oh, what a move. What a move. Ohhh… no. He's off. Oh, they're off as well. Oh my God. This is carnage.

"We've actually got a steward's enquiry ongoing about the win at the moment. Then the winners: Car 20, CLS63. And we've got some pretty spectacular big trophies here as well. Everyone had a really great time and yeah, great turnout. And we'll definitely have to do it again because it was, it was mega," summed up Russell.

The Brit is coming off from a good weekend in F1 Dutch GP where he secured pole in sprint race and took the win, followed by a Top 3 in main qualifying and a third place finish in the race. Russell has had a difficult run so far, but felt much better in the car after going back to doing basics.

title: SEC backs down in battle over professional player eligibility
description: Though it looked like we were gearing up for a legal battle, the SEC is reportedly going to comply with court orders allowing pro players to return.
fullText:
The SEC has seemingly caved in its quest to prevent former professional players from suiting up this fall.

Prompted by LSU's attempt to add three players who were waived from NFL training camps — including two who played for Ole Miss last season — the SEC passed a rule to bar teams from adding players who had signed pro contracts.

Punishments for violating that rule include a suspension of the coach for 50% of the season, a fine of 50% of the sport in question's operating budget and the loss of voting privileges on matters of conference business.

It looked like the conference was gearing up for a legal battle, but on Saturday, NIL attorney Darren Heitner revealed that the SEC will comply with the court orders from those players who received injunctions allowing them to play this fall.

My understanding is that the SEC and Greg Sankey will comply with all applicable court orders, including those in Louisiana. This portion of a newly issued order should be sufficient to give schools comfort with rostering athletes despite threatened penalties. SEC is a Defendant. pic.twitter.com/u0dmQPsV5P

This was looking like a major potential controversy on the eve of the 2026 campaign, but in a fairly surprising move, the SEC has relented. Now, LSU's additions and any other players in similar positions will be permitted to play in the league this season.

title: Phillies World Series Champion Larry Christenson Dies at 72 During Family Fishing Trip
description: “The club and its fans are forever grateful for his contributions and the legacy he leaves behind in Philadelphia,” the Phillies wrote on social media
fullText:
Larry Christenson has died at age 72

The baseball star died while on a fishing trip with his family and friends in Washington state

Christenson was selected by the Phillies in the third round of the 1972 MLB Draft, after which he became a member of the 1980 World Series championship team and the National League pennant-winning club in 1983

Larry Christenson, a World Series champion with the Philadelphia Phillies, has died. He was 72.

The Philadelphia Phillies announced in an X post that the former pitcher died unexpectedly during a fishing trip with family and friends in Washington state on Friday, Aug. 28. No additional details about the circumstances of his death were immediately shared.

After being selected by the Philadelphia team in the third round of the 1972 MLB Draft, the Washington native made his big league debut on April 13, 1973, against the New York Mets at the age of 19. During his debut, Christenson earned the win in a complete game effort.

According to the MLB, Christenson remains the last pitcher to ever earn a complete game victory as a teenager in his MLB debut.

Throughout his 11 years with the Phillies, the pitcher became a member of the 1980 World Series championship team and the National League pennant-winning club in 1983. The Phillies also reached the playoffs six times in his 11 seasons.

"In addition to his legacy as a Phillies player, 'LC' was an active supporter of Phillies Charities and other local non-profits," the Phillies wrote on X. "The club and its fans are forever grateful for his contributions and the legacy he leaves behind in Philadelphia."

"We extend our heartfelt condolences to Larry's beloved daughters, Claire and Libby, his extended family and friends, and former teammates at this difficult time," the team added.

Christenson ranks ninth among all Phillies pitchers in career starts, per MLB. His 11 career home runs are also tied with Rick Wise for the most by a pitcher in franchise history.

Following the athlete's death, Larry Bowa, who played with Christenson from 1973 to 1981, shared an emotional tribute on social media.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — 

"My heart is heavy today," he wrote. "LC was a tremendous teammate, an outstanding pitcher and a true friend."

"He was always the life of the clubhouse," he continued. "He will be deeply missed. My thoughts and prayers are with his family."

Former Phillies infielder Mike Schmidt also told ESPN that Christenson would be remembered as someone who was "very special, the guy that kept in touch with all of us."

"He always had a smile on his face, he never forgot a moment he spent with you," he said. "His passing will leave a hole in all of our hearts. May he rest in peace."

title: San Antonio native Jordan Clarkson meets tennis star Alex Eala at U.S. Open
description: San Antonio native and Knicks champion Jordan Clarkson met tennis star Alex Eala at the U.S. Open, where the Filipino athletes bonded over their heritage in an interaction shared by ESPN.
fullText:
San Antonio native Jordan Clarkson crossed paths with rising tennis star Alex Eala at the U.S. Open on Thursday, bringing together two prominent Filipino athletes from different corners of the sports world.

ESPN shared video of the meeting on social media, showing the New York Knicks guard and Eala congratulating each other and bonding over their shared Filipino heritage.

Wembanyama shines in return to FIBA stage

Clarkson is coming off a championship season with the Knicks, who defeated the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the 2026 NBA Finals. The San Antonio native attended Wagner High School.

"I wear my culture on my sleeve," Eala told Clarkson. "It brings so many people together. It's crazy how people can connect through culture and just nostalgia. I think it's a really powerful thing."

Clarkson, who has represented the Philippines in international basketball, agreed.

"When you got Filipino blood, [you] take the whole country with you, the whole pride," Clarkson said.

The two also discussed representing Filipino culture through their respective sports.

"We're doing a lot for the country and the culture," Clarkson said.

Eala called 2026 "a big year for the culture."

Their conversation eventually turned to sports. Eala noted the Philippines' passion for basketball, while Clarkson praised her impact on tennis.

"You're leading the way for tennis," Clarkson told her.

San Antonio native Jordan Clarkson honored for giving back to his Alamo City hometown

Clarkson also pointed to the Filipino support surrounding Eala at the U.S. Open, including Philippine flags visible in the stands.

"I'm proud of you," Clarkson told her.

The meeting brought together two athletes who have represented the Philippines on the international sports stage. For Clarkson, it came just months after the former Wagner standout returned to San Antonio for the NBA Finals and left his hometown as an NBA champion.

There's more to San Antonio with the Express-News.

title: Agent explains why Jonathan Kuminga rejected Warriors’ $75 million offer
description: Jonathan Kuminga rejected a huge extension to remain with the Warriors, resulting in him now being on the Timberwolves roster.
fullText:
Jonathan Kuminga has had an interesting trajectory in his NBA career, moving on from a chaotic stint with the Golden State Warriors last season. His agent went into detail about what the young forward declined to secure a big extension with Golden State.

Kuminga represented the Warriors for five seasons from 2021 to 2026, winning a title in 2022. However, his final years with the franchise saw him be in and out of the rotation, resulting in frustration over his role. Golden State eventually traded him to the Atlanta Hawks for Kristaps Porzingis.

Kuminga had an opportunity to obtain a three-year contract extension with Golden State for a total of $75 million. However, he declined to sign it as his agent Aaron Turner appeared on the Run It Back podcast to explain the decision.

"Money coming before basketball is not how you continue to make more and more money. … Next year is a way better free agency year for him…teams that have been trying to sign-and-trade for him, like Sacramento and Chicago, will have a lot of money," Turner said.

Mar 1, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Hawks forward Jonathan Kuminga (0) dunks against the Portland Trail Blazers in the fourth quarter at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Jonathan Kuminga doesn't have to worry about the Warriors anymore. After all, he is now an official member of the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Timberwolves, which includes a player option on the second season. He chose Minnesota over offers from the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers, via ESPN. Despite the small contract, it's clear that Kuminga wants to maximize his worth as a player in his career for his next deal.

Minnesota finished with a 49-33 record last season, securing the sixth seed in the Western Conference standings. They finished above the Portland Trail Blazers and the Phoenix Suns while trailing the Houston Rockets and the Los Angeles Lakers.

The Timberwolves made noise in the playoffs, stunning the Denver Nuggets in six games despite suffering significant injuries. However, their postseason journey ended after losing to the San Antonio Spurs in six games.

title: Jesse Bisiwu reveals the Barcelona star who has surprised him most

title: How overlooked Liverpool signing can pave the way forward in post-Salah era
description: Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest: Iraola and Glasner remain winless in the Premier League but the Reds came from behind twice to nick a point
fullText:
Wingers come in different guises and at different prices. On the day Liverpool agreed to pay up to £123m for Bradley Barcola, the man signed for rather less, and with rather less fanfare, again spared Andoni Iraola a first defeat of his reign. On Sunday at Newcastle, Victor Munoz won the penalty that produced Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th-minute equaliser. On his Anfield bow, the £34m Spaniard delivered a devastating equaliser.

That both contributions came from the right flank, though he had started on the left against Nottingham Forest, may be pertinent. The presumption is that Barcola will be used on the left. While Liverpool are yet to replace Mohamed Salah, they got two equalisers from the men stationed in his old spot here, with Cody Gakpo affording Alexander Isak a tap-in. The Dutchman is scarcely a right winger and faces an uncertain future at the end of the window. If Munoz had a fine introduction, this could prove Gakpo's goodbye, and his was a valiant effort.

An encouraging element for Liverpool is that Iraola has exerted an impact with his changes in each of his first two games. Munoz, who came on at St James' Park, swapped flanks at Anfield, took Florian Wirtz's pass, span and unleashed a vicious shot, even if a deflection off Murillo helped. It may not have been the first example of fine decision-making by Iraola: he pushed for Munoz's signing when Newcastle were closing in on his signature. "Victor has been very good both games," said Iraola. "Everything hasn't been perfect but he tries again and again and again and I like this from the wingers."

And so his tenure has begun with twin 2-2 draws. If it promises to be fun, at times his Liverpool can be both fast and flawed. Yet this underlined the size of his task if Iraola is to succeed his way. Liverpool had more defensive difficulties, with a susceptibility to the counter-attack again apparent, but with variations on a theme. Newcastle had scored twice by running straight through the heart of Iraola's team. Forest struck twice courtesy of balls in behind, the first punted 80 yards by goalkeeper Matz Sels; both involved throw-ins, too, the second a quick one by the debutant Liam Delap.

After the Forest striker added to the family tradition of Delap throw-ins, Alisson upended Neco Williams and Morgan Gibbs-White, an increasingly regular scourge of Liverpool, converted the resulting penalty. "It could and probably should have been a win," said Oliver Glasner. "Very proud of the performance but frustrated and disappointed about the result." So both new managers remain winless.

It looked a perfect storm for Liverpool; or maybe a Venn diagram of doom. Forest had won on their previous two trips to Anfield. Glasner had beaten Liverpool three times last season with Crystal Palace. Iraola tends to begin slowly in new jobs.

But they avoided the worst-case scenario and had a point to show for a rather mixed display. "The first half has been poor from our side," admitted Iraola, who drew more optimism from what followed.

Yet Liverpool again had a high defensive line and a susceptibility to counter-attacks. Glasner, despite his back-to-back losses to Leeds, seemed to be the new manager who had made the more immediate impact.

Liverpool were run ragged by Dan Ndoye and Igor Jesus. Gibbs-White showed there is life after Elliot Anderson for Forest. He played a part in both goals. For the opener, the Liverpool defence, attempting to push up, were caught out by Sels' long kick to Jesus, before Gibbs-White fed Ndoye to slot in. Alisson made a terrific save to deny Forest a second, tipping Jesus's shot on to the bar.

Wirtz had a goal disallowed when Jeremie Frimpong was offside. The German provided more promise than he had at Newcastle, drawing a fine save from Sels after a lovely Gakpo cross, finding the Dutchman in the build-up to the first equaliser and ending with an assist of his own. Isak, though, got his goal, just his second for Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

A subplot in a match where substitutions felt significant was that Iraola was readying a triple change, with Rio Ngumoha about to come on; the manager revealed that Gakpo would have been among those going off.

Instead, Glasner summoned Delap, fresh from his £45m club-record move from Chelsea. Iraola was aggrieved Liverpool were trying to make a triple change when the forward took the throw. "I wanted to make the subs about three minutes before," said Iraola. "I don't have an explanation." He suggested the fourth official's board was malfunctioning. So, though, was his defence.

They look in need of bolstering, though Liverpool are instead adding a winger for a nine-figure sum. Meanwhile, Glasner, set to sign Daniel Munoz and amid Forest interest in Harrison Armstrong, is eyeing more arrivals. "Definitely one, potentially two and probably three," he said. It could lead to departures. "Definitely one, potentially two and probably three," he grinned.

title: Houston Texans 53-man roster projection: With preseason complete, who will make the team?
description: The Texans have some tough decisions to make before Sunday evening's roster deadline. Beat writer Jonathan M. Alexander makes his final 53-man roster projection.
fullText:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. - The preseason is over, and by Sunday at 5 p.m., the Houston Texans roster will be cut down to 53 players.

Here's our final roster projection (* - practice squad candidate):

Projected starter: C.J. Stroud
Projected depth: Davis Mills
Projected cut: Brett Rypien*
IR:

Analysis: Rypien did nothing to help his case to make the roster. He may be a practice squad player for the Texans unless they look elsewhere.

Projected starter: David Montgomery
Projected depth: Woody Marks, Jawhar Jordan, British Brooks
Projected cuts: Noah Whittington*, Owen Wright*, Deuce Vaughn
IR: Joshua Pitsenberger

Analysis: The Texans have dealt with a ton of injuries at running back in recent weeks. But Montgomery, Marks, Jordan and Brooks seem like the logical locks, with Whittington returning for the practice squad.

Projected starters: Nico Collins, Kayshon Boutte, Jaylin Noel
Projected depth: Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, Lewis Bond
Projected cuts: Jared Wayne*, Josh Kelly*, Sterling Shepard, Justin Watson, Treyvhon Saunders, Daniel Sobkowicz, Zay Jones

Analysis: Coach DeMeco Ryans said it best. The Texans have too many receivers worthy of making the roster than they have space for. Having said that, the Texans could still cut someone and bring them back after they've made their IR selections.

Projected starters: Dalton Schultz
Projected depth: Marlin Klein, Foster Moreau, Cade Stover
Projected cuts: Brevin Jordan, Layne Pryor*, Louis Hansen

Analysis: Jordan was expected to give Stover a run for his money, but he hasn't been available in camp and that will hurt him.

Projected starters: Aireontae Ersery, Trent Brown
Projected depth: Braden Smith, Blake Fisher
Projected cuts: Jarrett Kingston*, Derrick Graham, Sam Hagen

Analysis: The Texans like their depth at tackle, and should keep four even if they think they can trade one down the line. Brown and Smith have often been injured throughout their careers.

Projected starters: Keylan Rutledge, Ed Ingram
Projected depth: Wyatt Teller, Febechi Nwaiwu
Projected cut: Jarrett Patterson*, James Neal III

Analysis: The Texans decided not to play Rutledge, Ingram or Teller on Friday, which means their spots are solidified. But Patterson played the entire final preseason game, which could mean his days as a Texans player are numbered. He could, however, be brought back for the practice squad if he doesn't decide to move on.

Projected starters: Evan Brown
Projected depth: N/A
Projected cut: Jake Andrews*, Eli Cox

Analysis: Brown solidified his spot as the starter over the past two weeks by putting up good film and being reliable. Rutledge can back him up at center, if needed, while Andrews, who played Friday, may return to the practice squad.

Projected starters: Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter
Projected depth: Jadeveon Clowney, Logan Hall
Projected cut: Sabastian Harsh*, Solomon Byrd*, Dominique Robinson
IR: Dylan Horton, Ali Gaye

Analysis: Byrd became the latest Texans edge rusher to suffer an injury, though it doesn't appear to be serious. Harsh made a phenomenal last impression, but was it good enough to sustain his spot on the roster? It's possible the Texans could bring him or Byrd back after the initial 53-man roster is set.

Projected starters: Sheldon Rankins, Tommy Togiai
Projected depth: Kayden McDonald, Mario Edwards, Naquan Jones
Projected cut: Dominic Bailey, Kyonte Hamilton*

title: LSU poised to sign former NFL players after SEC says it will comply with court order
description: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris are expected to sign with the Tigers.
fullText:
LSU may soon fire the loudest shot yet in a battle with its own conference.

The SEC has communicated to plaintiff attorneys that the league will comply with a Louisiana state court order permitting their clients — former professional football players — from a return to college. Yahoo Sports obtained a message from the conference legal counsel to attorneys signaling the news.

The message paves the way for a host of players to join SEC programs, most notably at LSU, where two players who signed pro contracts this summer are poised to now be on coach Lane Kiffin's roster.

Dae'Quan Wright, the former Ole Miss tight end who signed an undrafted free agent contract with the Cleveland Browns, and Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris, who signed with the Saints before being waived, plan to sign with the university. While the signing does not immediately constitute a violation of the SEC's new policy banning former professional players, their inclusion on LSU's final roster would. Rosters are not set until a day before Game 1 (Friday).

The impending signings continues to put at odds the SEC and LSU in an unprecedented legal collision over athlete eligibility that's been brewing for days. A Louisiana judge earlier this month granted Wright and other players an additional year of eligibility through a temporary restraining order by prohibiting the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility standards.

The move created a whirlwind of a week where all the power conferences adopted their own eligibility policy banning pro athletes from returning to college. And then, on Friday, a Baton Rouge judge granted a request from players' attorneys to also enjoin the SEC's new rule, amending the complaint to add the league and commissioner Greg Sankey as defendants.

It's not only football. RJ Luis, a basketball standout who played three games in the NBA and was part of two franchises, is a commitment to Will Wade's hoops team.

The addition of all three players violated two SEC policies: the ban on pro players and the prohibition on players moving from one conference member to another outside of the transfer portal window. Each violation comes with stiff sanctions, including a half-season suspension of the head coach, a 50% fine of a school's athletic budget and the forfeiture of voting privileges.

However, the Louisiana judge's order prohibits the league from enforcing sanctions against a school, coach or athlete. A preliminary injunction hearing - where the judge determines if the restraining order will be more permanent until a trial - is scheduled for Thursday in Baton Rouge.

Two days later, LSU hosts Clemson in a top-25 game in Tiger Stadium in coach Lane Kiffin's debut.

The Tigers aren't necessarily alone in intentionally leaving open roster spots for pro players and/or those transferring within the league outside of the portal window. Texas has a player, Cole Hutson, who participated in mini camp with two NFL teams, received a state injunction and is practicing with the Longhorns. Kentucky is expected to sign former Missouri players Mark Mitchell, who played games in the NBA summer league.

But the Tigers have been the most aggressive, with their brash coach and even the Louisiana governor leading the way.

In a news conference on Monday, Kiffin said the players suing the NCA were "wronged" because of the association's timing of the new eligibility policy, suggested that other programs are also recruiting the same athletes and said he's only trying to improve his roster through a "relentless pursuit of excellence."

"That's how I live," he said. "It's how I run the team. And that we're always going to look at every avenue to give you the best team, to give you the best players, so that you have the best chance to win."

The state's governor, Jeff Landry, released a statement to Front Office Sports earlier this week on the issue, blaming the system and not his state school: "Don't hate the player; hate the game."

More players are available outside of the Louisiana suit.

A Dallas judge on Thursday granted additional eligibility to more than two dozen athletes playing multiple sports - a complaint filed, like the Louisiana one, by attorney Ryan Downton and the Texas Trial Lawyers. Downton represented former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia in a case in 2024 that opened the floodgates for many eligibility lawsuits against the association.

But the latest wave of cases stems from the NCAA's new eligibility policy enacted this summer. The new rule grants athletes five seasons of eligibility, up from four under the previous bylaw. The association chose not to make an exception for players graduating this spring who exhausted their eligibility under the former policy.

That decision, made by the member schools themselves, sparked the current landscape: more than 300 athletes filing 60-plus lawsuits for an additional year, including those who this spring signed pro contracts without knowledge of the NCAA's rule change. Athletes have won a wide portion of those rulings, but inconsistent judicial decisions - the NCAA has, for now, won cases in Ohio, New York, Nevada and a federal suit in Colorado - has created an uneven competitive playing field.

"The 'chaos' of NFL players going back to college is a one-time occurrence specifically resulting from the NCAA arbitrarily denying Class of 2022 athletes from having a fifth year under its new rule, which the NCAA forecasted was coming for a long time," Florida based sports lawyer Darren Heitner, who's assisting with the lawsuit and represents some of the players involved, posted online earlier this week.

"They wouldn't have been NFL players at all if the NCAA would have rightfully given them an extra year. Alternatively, had the NCAA provided the option of a fifth year and the athlete still went to the NFL, the player wouldn't be allowed to go back to college. But that's not what happened."

Judges are not only granting athletes eligibility but creating temporary windows for them to transfer and permitting pro players to return to college - a long-honored college policy that is now under attack, in part because of the monetary incentive. Pro athletes cut from rosters are expected to receive big pay days at their colleges through NIL and revenue-share agreements.

The act of schools accepting professional players is emerging as a seminal moment in the industry, as college executives rally to halt the action. Within a matter of 48 hours, leaders of the Big Ten, SEC, Big 12 and ACC adopted their own pro-player bans in an effort to evade legal challenges by governing a smaller group of schools than the hundreds under the NCAA umbrella. But despite unanimous votes from school presidents to pass such rules, universities are leaving open roster spots and are, privately, supporting players in legal battles - most notably LSU, which played a role in the Louisiana filing.

The situation has sprung to life the industry and its legion of fans - many of whom do not publicly support the return of pro athletes.

College Football Playoff leaders may soon follow the power leagues, in fact. They plan next week to seriously discuss and possibly adopt a participation policy that disqualifies several categories of athletes, including those who have previously signed pro contracts, sources with knowledge of the talks told Yahoo Sports.

But plaintiff attorneys believe that these athletes belonging to the 2022 high school class should have been granted an additional year of eligibility. On the other side, NCAA and conference officials believe they are taking spots from other players on the eve of the start of the fall sports season.

"Courts across the country granting relief to ineligible athletes who already had every opportunity to compete in college - sometimes without even having a hearing - are failing to appreciate the destabilizing effect their rulings are having on college sports," the NCAA released in a statement earlier this month. "The lawyers bringing these cases seemingly won't be satisfied until every professional athlete can treat college sports as a fallback option, regardless of the opportunities it strips from both those who will never have a chance to begin their collegiate sports experience and those who are currently on campus working out with the team and attending classes."
