title: Scraper that probes a site before promising it works
description: Tiered config-driven scraper: probe-first site classifier (curl_cffi TLS impersonation), YAML configs, pagination certification. MIT. - vhsgreed/scrapeforge
fullText:
Tiered Python scraper that probes the target first, picks the right fetch
tier automatically, extracts with CSS selectors, and outputs CSV/JSON.
New sites are a YAML file, not code.

The probe (classify.py) fetches the target, scores the response, and
picks the tier. Tier 3 is never promised blindly; it is an escalation path
with honest caveats. If a site is out of reach, scrapeforge says so before
you commit.

Tier 3 (browser stealth) is optional:

1. Config-driven pagination (paginate.py) — the runner follows
next-page links from the YAML config. The paginate block is optional; if
absent, only the starting URL is fetched:

The loop fetches each page, extracts items, and follows the next link until
max_pages is reached or no next link exists. rate_limit_sec inserts a
pause between page fetches (recommended: keep it >= 1.0).

2. Pagination certification (pageprobe.py) — verifies that a target
actually paginates before you promise anything. For each URL it:

Verdicts: PAGINATED_OK / NO_NEXT_LINK / BLOCKED_AT_DEPTH /
NO_CONTENT_CHANGE / ERROR. Run it on the exact URLs a job needs (e.g.
category pages, not homepages: homepages usually have no next link).

results-stress-test-2026-08-29.csv contains reachability verdicts for 150
live e-commerce and indie-web sites (probed 2026-08-29): tier per site,
response size, and notes. 103 deliverable, 37 blocked, 10 unreachable.
pagination-matrix-homepages-2026-08-29.csv is the pagination-advance
matrix from the same set.

Reachability is IP- and time-dependent. Probe per job; never assume a
verdict carries over to another network or day.

Public data only. Respect robots.txt and rate limits. No login-gated
content, no credential abuse. If a site forbids scraping, scrapeforge flags
it and you decide with the site's terms in mind.

title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172k for Trump speech bets
description: The staffer was found to have used his prior knowledge of the president's speeches to place lucrative bets.
fullText:
A former White House teleprompter operator has been ordered to pay more than $172,000 (£127,000) for using inside information to bet on Donald Trump's speeches.

Gabriel Perez was found to have made trades concerning what the US president would say during addresses between December 2025 and February 2026 on Kalshi - a prediction markets platform where users can bet on real-world events.

Its regulator, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), said Perez would have to surrender profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil penalty of $65,000.

The White House has not yet commented. In July, then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Perez was on unpaid leave and would not return to his post.

Announcing the settlement on Friday, the CFTC said Perez had "misappropriated" his prior knowledge of Trump's speeches to place bets "in breach of his duty of trust and confidence".

It said his civil penalty had been reduced due to his "exemplary co-operation" with the investigation.

Perez has also been banned from trading for three years.

Kalshi's lead lawyer Bobby DeNault welcomed the decision, writing on X: "It doesn't matter who you are: violate our rules or federal law and you will face the consequences."

The company previously told the BBC that its analysts had noticed unusual betting on "mention markets" – contracts through which users predict whether a speaker will use common terms, such as specific countries, campaign slogans or words – in March.

It said it had used account data to find that the user had been a federal employee operating White House teleprompters, and reported the activity to the regulator.

"The words of political leaders like presidents and Fed chairs cause billions of dollars of movement in FX markets, oil futures [and] the stock market," it said in a statement in July.

The same month, the White House Management Office had sent a letter to aides telling them not to place bets on prediction markets, administration officials told the BBC's US media partner CBS News.

title: Manchester Airports breach exposes data on 8.7M customers
description: Manchester Airports Group says hackers stole contact, postcode and vehicle data from up to 8.7 million customers, while payment data stayed secure.
fullText:
Manchester Airports Group says hackers stole contact, postcode and vehicle data from up to 8.7 million customers, while payment data stayed secure.

Manchester Airports Group says hackers stole personal data tied to up to 8.7 million customers across Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports. The exposed information includes email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers and postcodes.

The affected records came from several airport services rather than flight operations: car-park bookings, lounge reservations, Fast Track bookings and airport Wi-Fi sign-ups. Together, those details could help attackers build credible messages for individual travelers, even though MAG says banking and other financial information was not exposed.

The company has not disclosed how the attackers got in, which systems they accessed, when the intrusion began or whether the stolen records have been published. Available reporting also does not establish whether all 8.7 million records were taken, only that the incident affects data belonging to up to that number of customers.

“We immediately contained the risk and have been working with specialist advisors and taking appropriate steps to protect our customers and systems. We have informed and are working with the relevant authorities. At no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised.”

MAG says the incident did not compromise passenger safety or aviation security. Airport services continued operating, with no reported flight cancellations or terminal queues attributed to the attack. The immediate operational impact is limited, but the customer data remains valuable to criminals.

Equifax automates half of its security tickets with AI

Sophia Reynolds • Aug 29, 2026 • 6 min read

An email address or phone number alone can support a generic phishing campaign. Combined with a postcode, vehicle registration and knowledge that someone booked airport parking or lounge access, those details can support a message that looks like a real airport notification: a parking refund, a payment problem, a Fast Track change or a warning about the breach itself.

That risk also applies to US travelers who used one of MAG’s UK airports. A message referencing a genuine trip through Manchester or Stansted may be more convincing than a broad airline scam, particularly when it includes a vehicle registration or other information the recipient recognizes.

“The absence of cancelled flights or queues at terminals does not make this a small cyber attack. The data reportedly taken can now be weaponised.”

Stewart said aviation companies should treat the incident as evidence of sustained pressure on the sector, not as a minor customer-database compromise. His warning focuses on the path attackers can take through suppliers and connected systems: a breach in a service such as parking or Wi-Fi can expose customers without touching aircraft-control or airport-security systems.

Vykintas Maknickas, CEO of Saily, made the same distinction from the traveler’s perspective:

“This breach shows that airport cybersecurity is no longer only protecting flight systems or operational infrastructure. The digital services travelers use every day, like airport WiFi, parking bookings, lounge access, and fast-track reservations, have become part of the security perimeter.”

The exposure may support targeted phishing and smishing, including fake airport emails, fraudulent parking-payment notices, bogus flight updates and calls offering compensation. Dr. Ilia Kolochenko, founder of ImmuniWeb, warned that travel details connected to lounge and Fast Track bookings could also be used in more coercive campaigns:

“A wave of personalized and AI-enhanced blackmailing and extortion campaigns may be launched shortly.”

That is an expert assessment, not a confirmed description of activity already linked to the breach. MAG has not said that extortion, cryptocurrency demands or publication of the data has occurred.

MAG advises customers to treat unexpected emails, text messages and phone calls about the airports or the incident with suspicion. Travelers should not click links or open attachments in unsolicited messages, and should instead visit an airport’s official website directly to verify a parking, booking or refund issue.

Anyone who receives a call claiming to be from an airport should end the call and contact the organization through an independently verified number. If a customer has already provided banking information after responding to a suspicious message, the source guidance recommends contacting the bank immediately. Anyone who disclosed a reused password should change it everywhere it was used and enable two-step verification.

Raghu Nandakumara, vice president of industry strategy at Illumio, said keeping terminals operating is only one part of containing a breach:

“Maintaining services during a cyberattack is critical, but organisations also need to minimise the amount of data and systems an attacker can reach before the threat is isolated.”

His recommendation points to segmentation as a technical control: separating customer-service databases and connected airport services can limit how far an attacker moves after an initial compromise. It cannot undo data already copied, but it can prevent a single exposed service from granting broad access to unrelated systems.

For US travelers, the practical concern is more convincing airport-themed scams. Customers who traveled through Manchester, Stansted or East Midlands should remain alert, while the underlying entry point, the full scope of the records and any law-enforcement findings remain undisclosed.

The exposed data includes email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers and postcodes linked to up to 8.7 million customers.

No. Manchester Airports Group said banking and financial information remained secure during the incident.

The group owns and oversees Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports. The affected records came from services including parking, lounges, Fast Track and airport Wi-Fi.

The available reporting does not establish how the attackers entered the systems or which specific database was compromised.

Sophia unpacks the invisible wars happening on our networks. Covering cybersecurity, privacy legislation, and cryptography, she exposes how our data is weaponized and defended. Before joining for(geeks), she spent years as a penetration tester. She's the reason the rest of the team uses physical security keys.

title: Thailand: Where does the planned cut in visafree stays from 60 to 30 days stand?
description: Announced in spring 2026 and further clarified in July, Thailand’s overhaul of its visa exemption rules has still not taken effect. Nationals of 93 countries and territories can currently continue to stay visa-free for up to 60 days, while the country is also moving ahead with the digital modernization of its entry procedures through the TDAC and the upcoming THIM app.
fullText:
Thailand has now clearly announced plans to reduce its visa-free stay from 60 to 30 days, but the change has not yet taken effect.

A series of announcements over the past several months may have created the impression that the visa-free stay has already been shortened. As of August 11, 2026, that is not the case.

Nationals of the 93 countries and territories currently eligible, including the US, Canada, the UK, France, Belgium, and Switzerland, continue to benefit from the scheme introduced in July 2024, allowing visa-free stays of up to 60 days.

That period can currently be extended for an additional 30 days, at the discretion of Thai immigration authorities.

Under the upcoming rules, the initial visa-free stay is expected to be reduced to 30 days for many of the nationalities concerned. Before the changes can take effect, however, the new regulations must still be published in the Royal Gazette, Thailand’s official government journal.

The plan has gradually taken shape since the beginning of 2026.

In February, the Thai government announced that it intended to review the 60-day visa exemption scheme, citing misuse of the program and repeated entries for purposes beyond those originally intended.

On March 20, 2026, Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow took the process a step further by announcing that a proposal to cut the visa exemption from 60 to 30 days would be submitted to the government.

He noted that most tourists stay in the country for less than 30 days and said travelers wishing to remain longer should continue to have access to an additional extension.

At that point, however, the reform had not yet received formal approval.

The process moved forward on May 19, 2026, when the Thai Cabinet formally approved a revision of the country’s visa exemption and visa-on-arrival schemes.

The government approved the principle of ending the general 60-day visa exemption covering 93 countries and territories and adopted a new structure based in part on the “one country, one regime” principle, designed to eliminate overlaps between general visa exemptions, bilateral agreements and visa-on-arrival arrangements.

Under the initial framework presented in May, authorities planned:

Authorities stressed, however, that the new measures would only take effect 15 days after their publication in the Royal Gazette.

That publication did not take place in the weeks that followed.

The Thai government has since made additional changes to the planned system.

On July 14, 2026, the Cabinet approved a revised version of the upcoming visa exemption policy, significantly changing the structure presented in May.

Under the latest announced framework, 59 countries and territories are expected to qualify for a 30-day visa exemption for tourism.

Six countries were added to this category: India, Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Malta and the Maldives.

Adding Croatia, Bulgaria, Cyprus and Malta will notably mean that nationals of all 27 European Union member states are covered by the same 30-day visa exemption scheme.

The future system is also expected to include:

Overall, 65 countries and territories are expected to be covered by these various arrangements, excluding certain provisions stemming from bilateral agreements.

The visa reform comes as Thailand continues to modernize its immigration procedures.

Since May 1, 2025, foreign travelers have been required to complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before entering the country.

As part of the reform approved in July, authorities also announced plans to strengthen the system, including through greater integration of government databases to improve risk assessment and the monitoring of foreign nationals entering and leaving Thailand.

This broader modernization effort also includes the development of THIM (Thailand Immigration Management), a new Thai immigration mobile app currently available on a pilot basis.

As of August 11, 2026, the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) still states that the app’s official launch is expected sometime in August, although no specific date has been announced.

For now, THIM remains optional and is not a new mandatory entry requirement for Thailand. It also does not replace the TDAC.

The app allows travelers to photograph their passports so certain details can be captured automatically, before entering information about their stay, accommodation and travel plans. Group registration for up to 10 travelers is also available.

Over time, THIM is expected to develop into a broader immigration services platform, with features such as digital document submission, appointment scheduling and certain procedures that can be completed remotely. These functions are still under development, however, and remain subject to confirmation by Thailand’s Immigration Bureau.

Despite the numerous announcements, no effective date has yet been set for the new visa exemption system.

The regulations required to implement the changes are still awaiting publication in the Royal Gazette. The new rules will take effect 15 days after that publication.

In practical terms, an eligible traveler entering Thailand today under the general visa exemption scheme can still be granted a stay of up to 60 days, not 30 days.

Thai authorities have also indicated that travelers who enter the country before the new system takes effect will retain the length of stay granted to them upon arrival.

A traveler admitted for 60 days before the rules change should therefore not see that authorized stay automatically reduced once the new provisions come into force.

The key next step remains the publication of the regulations in the Royal Gazette. That publication, rather than the government announcements made so far, will determine the exact date from which travelers will have to comply with the new visa-free stay periods.

For travelers, the situation remains unchanged as of August 11, 2026: the announced reduction of visa-free stays to 30 days does not mean the shorter period is already in effect. The current 60-day scheme will remain in place until the new regulations officially take effect. At the same time, Thailand is preparing a broader modernization of its digital entry procedures through an upgraded TDAC system and the development of THIM, although the new app remains optional and in its pilot phase for now.

title: I was getting tired of looking for my travel info so I built this
description: Your whole itinerary, remembered for you. Skaoot keeps it right when plans shift.
fullText:
Skaoot is a travel assistant that reads your booking confirmations and
 remembers every flight, train, rental, stay, and detail for you. You always
 know what’s next, and you hear about changes the moment they happen.

Free for your first few bookings. No credit card.

Reads booking emails from the providers travelers actually use

Built for travelers who live out of a suitcase, a backpack and a calendar that won’t sit still.

Three flight confirmations from one airline. Two Airbnb bookings with door
 codes buried somewhere in paragraph nine. A visa appointment, a transfer
 voucher, a rebooked outbound that arrived as a separate thread.

When the gate changes, you find out at the gate. When you land, you scour
 your inbox for the door code. When plans shift, your itinerary tool either
 misses the update or duplicates the booking.

Travel was supposed to feel like freedom.

Pass along a confirmation for a flight, hotel, train, or vehicle rental, and that’s the last you think about it. Old bookings, new ones, anything in between.

It reads each booking, links it to the others, and builds one timeline in the order things happen. Changes merge in on their own. No duplicates, nothing lost.

The door code when you arrive at your accommodation. Drive time when you land. The gate change the moment it happens. You stop searching. What you need just shows up.

Stop holding it all in your head. Every flight and stay laid out in the order it happens. Nothing to remember, nothing to dig for.

Hear about a gate change before you’re standing at the wrong one. Skaoot watches your flights and tells you the moment something matters, then stays quiet when it doesn’t.

Land at midnight and the address, the door code, the WiFi are already there, pulled from the listing and waiting for you. No scrolling, no scrambling.

Rebooked, rescheduled, cancelled and replaced: your itinerary just stays right, on its own. You never travel on information you cannot trust.

The door code ready the moment you arrive, tired, at midnight. A nudge to leave with time to spare, never a sprint for the gate. The detail you need, surfaced exactly when it matters.

Forward a rail booking and your seats, tickets, and stations take their place between your flights and stays. One journey, in order, nothing separate to check.

Car, campervan, or motorcycle: the fuel policy, the mileage cap, the deposit release, the return timed against your flight. Every step on your timeline, with your licence checked for the country you’re driving in.

Skaoot checks every trip against your passports, visas, and travel authorizations, and warns you while there’s still time to apply. The immigration math stops living in your head.

title: Listen in on the Sounds of a Jurassic Period Forest
description: Behold the call of the katydid
fullText:
Do you want to hear what the insects in a Jurassic forest in Mongolia sounded like?

Obviously, there were no recording devices, let alone humans, 165 million years ago, but there were katydids, insects in the order Orthoptera that are known for their sound-making abilities. And for a new study, paleontologists have recreated katydid melodies of the time by examining the katydid’s delicate file and plectrum structure via fossils.

The file consists of a serrated hard strip on the underside of the left forewing that gets scraped by a plectrum on the edge of the right forewing. A drum-like cell further resonates the vibrations from the scraping and amplifies the sound. There are also sets of teeth on the plectra spaced at different intervals (closely spaced teeth yield high frequencies, while wider spacing makes for lower frequencies). Amplitude can be varied by the amount of pressure exerted from the file on the plectrum.

In a Jurassic forest, katydids had no competition for airspace from squeaking bats, as bats didn’t evolve for another million years. Not that it would have mattered anyway; even early on, katydids had specialized ears to pick up each other’s calls—located on their front legs just below the knees, but similar in three-part structure to those of mammals. Sound travels into the outer ears, through the middle ears, and to the inner ears where a tiny sensory organ detects the sound vibrations.

The study authors also hypothesize that “the ability to produce sound by wing stridulation could have appeared before hearing as a defensive tool to deter terrestrial predators.” Although there were no bats, there were plenty of insectivorous mammals and reptiles, such as tree-climbing theropods and flying pterosaurs, in the Jurassic forests of China, which perhaps would be repelled by the squeaky-blackboard sounds.

If nothing else, katydids of the era certainly knew how to make sure that their voices were heard.

title: New York City sends 11,000 more pied-à-terre tax letters as it apologizes to the 1,200 wrongly targeted because it didn’t check 2025 tax returns
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani admitted the city lacked 2025 tax data before sending 17,000 warning letters.
fullText:
New York City's Department of Finance is sending a second wave of pied-à-terre tax letters to roughly 10,800 property owners, even as it mails a very different kind of letter to other owners from the first round, telling them, in effect, never mind.

Roughly 17,000 owners received a notice this summer warning they might owe the surcharge, which applies only to non-primary residences amounts, with a rate of 0.8%–1.3% on homes over $5 million and 4%-6.5% on condos and co-ops over $1 million. But 1,210 are now being cleared outright, according to new court filings disclosed this week.

The reason has nothing to do with a change in the law and everything to do with timing: New York State sent the city's DOF preliminary 2025 income-tax records on Aug. 12, several months earlier than the agency would normally begin receiving them. Of that group, 630 owners were cleared because their 2025 tax returns listed the property as their primary home address; another 580 were cleared using a mix of 2025 extension filings and 2024 returns.

"So by my last count, I think we sent out less than 20,000, 'you may be subject to' letters, I think it was about 17,000 or 18,000. And at the time that we sent those out, we did not have access to the 2025 income tax filings," said Mayor Zohran Mamdani at a Wednesday press conference. He noted the timing wasn't unusual on the state's end: 2025 filings are "typically released in February of the next calendar year," and the state simply gave DOF early access this time.

Randy Mastro, the attorney suing the city over the rollout (and a longtime suer of the city in general), made his thoughts known in the court filing. "There are many thousands fewer property owners subject to this surcharge than this administration originally boasted when it flooded the landscape with 17,000 threatening Mailed Notices."

"The City has now effectively admitted" that some people who received the letters, Mastro said, "do not actually owe this surcharge." He also argued the timing undercuts the city's excuse: "The City admits that, after this lawsuit was filed on August 7, it obtained 2025 tax information within five days," which is evidence, he claimed, that DOF could have gotten the same data before mailing anything, not just after being sued.

Mamdani laid out three categories of properties the city is targeting. One is properties owned by a corporate entity like an LLC or a trust, about 6,400 households, where DOF doesn't have enough information on primary residence holder. The 1,210 owners who were being cleared make up the second category. The third category, about 4,400 households, consists of properties where DOF doesn't have 2025 tax returns that would indicate whether they are primary residences. The first and third categories make up the 10,800 letters going out to people.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who stood alongside Mamdani when the tax was first announced in April, said this week she "wasn't a fan of the rollout" and that City Hall was working to correct the problems. Mamdani, at the same press conference, held firm on the tax's revenue target: "We continue to be confident in that assessment of what the annual revenue will look like."

Ryan Lavis, a DOF spokesperson, said: "From the beginning, we have been committed to ensuring that New Yorkers have the time and information they need. Property owners have until October 6th to file an exemption application. We have received the tax information from the state for 2025 and want to give New Yorkers more time to apply for an exemption, if applicable.

Mamdani noted Oct. 6 isn't necessarily the final word for owners who miss it. "If New Yorkers still want to appeal an assessment, they can still appeal to the tax commission until early next year."

New York City's pied-à-terre tax initially began as a Tax Day pitch. Mamdani and Hochul announced it in April, with Mamdani unveiling the plan in a video filmed outside Citadel billionaire Ken Griffin's $238 million penthouse. The state legislature passed it May 27, and Hochul signed it the next day.

The rollout is what actually caused the uproar. DOF's supplemental roll, meant to flag properties that might owe the surcharge, ballooned into an unfiltered list of nearly a million properties, instantly branded a "rich hit list" online, and united the ultrawealthy and merely well-off alike in opposition once thousands of legitimate primary residences got needlessly swept into DOF's notices. That confusion is now the subject of Mastro's active lawsuit.

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

title: SpaceX recovers Starship from the Indian Ocean a month after launch and is shipping it back to Texas
description: SpaceX has pulled off its biggest salvage operation yet, recovering its most recently launched Starship from the Indian Ocean.  Elon Musk’s company is now in the process of shipping Starship back to i...
fullText:
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — SpaceX has pulled off its biggest salvage operation yet, recovering its most recently launched Starship from the Indian Ocean.

Elon Musk's company is now in the process of shipping Starship back to its home base in Texas, a trip expected to take several months. SpaceX shared pictures of the recovery effort near Christmas Island late this week.

Starship — the biggest and most powerful rocket in the world — blasted off July 24 from Starbase, Texas. It was the 13th test flight of a full-up Starship, but unlike all the others, it survived the hourlong space-skimming flight and remained floating and intact.

"Congratulations to the entire SpaceX Recovery team for battling through challenging conditions to give our engineers access to a wealth of data to continue rapidly developing Starship," the company said via X.

Starship is how Musk intends to get people and equipment to Mars, where he hopes to build a city. First up, though, is the moon. NASA is counting on Starship as well as Jeff Bezos' Blue Moon lander to return astronauts to the lunar surface as early as 2028.

President Donald Trump endorsed both destinations during a visit to NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston on Friday. He presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to each of the four Artemis II astronauts who flew around the moon in April.

title: Soros-backed DA accused of going easy on illegal immigrants gets squeezed by House GOP
description: Chairman Jim Jordan warns subpoenas are on the table for sanctuary jurisdiction prosecutors his committee accuses of going easy on illegal immigrants.
fullText:
House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, is warning that subpoenas are on the table if county prosecutors accused of going easy on illegal immigrants who commit crimes do not cooperate.

Jordan's committee is investigating district attorneys for so-called "sanctuary jurisdictions" who have been accused of taking immigration status into account when pursuing criminal complaints, even when the alleged crime has nothing to do with the suspect's legal status.

"If we have to, we'll use subpoenas to get the documents that we think they may not be giving us. There's a process we always go through. We ask for things, we ask again, we explain why, we work with their office — in some cases their counsel — and back and forth," Jordan explained in an interview with Fox News Digital. "And then if we have to use subpoenas, we certainly will do that ... but we want to know the facts."

Doj Opens Investigation Into Soros-backed Da Accused Of Shielding Illegal Immigrants From Consequences

Of particular concern, Jordan said, is Fairfax County, Virginia, DA Steve Descano. Descano was recently thrust under scrutiny after the stabbing death of 41-year-old U.S. citizen Stephanie Minter, whose accused killer came to the U.S. illegally from Sierra Leone in 2012.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said the man had been arrested over 30 times before Minter's killing.

Soros Prosecutor In Danger Of Being Removed After Grieving Mom's Desperate Alarm: 'Can't Believe This'

Descano, who has led the Fairfax County District Attorney's Office since January 2020, issued plea bargaining guidance that year saying prosecutors should "consider immigration consequences where possible" and consider "the collateral immigration consequences of the specific crime(s) the defendant is charged with," according to local outlet WTOP News.

Fairfax County is known as a sanctuary jurisdiction, meaning local law enforcement is not bound to cooperate with federal immigration authorities.

Sanctuary County Refused 615 Ice Transfer Requests, Turned Over Just 11 Illegal Immigrants, Records Show

"This is one of the dumbest policies I've ever heard of. You're going to tell local law enforcement not to work with federal law enforcement when it comes to enforcing federal law?" Jordan said. "And then you have people like Mr. Descano, who are releasing bad guys, and they have a stated policy saying, you know, 'We will look at their immigration status before we make a decision on charging,' and in certain clear agreements and they're releasing guys. You have then you have bad things happen."

He noted Minter's case as an example.

Soros-backed Prosecutor Set For Capitol Hill Grilling As Sanctuary Policies Face Reckoning

Descano's 2019 campaign for DA notably received hundreds of thousands of dollars from Justice and Public Safety PAC, which boasts billionaire George Soros among its backers.

Fairfax County happens to be a major suburb of Washington, D.C. Jordan argued its proximity to the country's national security epicenter made its sanctuary policies even more dangerous.

"That's definitely a concern that I think probably any American with common sense would have," he said.

But there are other sanctuary jurisdictions his committee would probe as well, Jordan suggested.

Doj Accuses Maryland Of 'Active And Deliberate Effort' To Prevent Deportations Of Illegal Immigrants: Lawsuit

"You've got not just Descano, but it looks like Alvin Bragg up in New York, [Larry Krasner] in Philadelphia, so many of these DAs who are doing the same darn thing," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Descano's office for comment.

title: Risk of lake burst near China-Nepal border disaster site wanes
description: The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where a devastating flood occurred earlier this week has decreased, Chinese
fullText:
BEIJING, Aug 29 (Reuters) - The threat of a lake formed after a glacier collapse bursting near the China-Nepal border where a devastating flood occurred earlier this week has decreased, Chinese authorities said ‌on Saturday, as its size appears to have shrunk.

Satellite images from Thursday to Saturday morning suggest that ‌water in the lake – straddling the China-Nepal border at the confluence of two rivers – has been slowly flowing through, decreasing the reservoir gradually, ​state broadcaster CCTV reported citing the Water Resources Ministry.

The ministry said satellite imagery of the surface area of the lake at Purepu Tsangpo river showed it was 99,000 sqm in size on early Saturday morning – around the size of 14 football fields combined – having shrunk by 21,000 sqm compared with images from Thursday.

A glacier collapse on Wednesday sending a powerful torrent of rock, ‌ice, mud and debris through Himalayan ⁠mountain river systems swept away a border port complex linking China's Tibet to Nepal, killing hundreds and leaving thousands missing.

Experts and authorities have warned of the extremely high risk of ⁠secondary disasters in the valley, especially from the lake that was formed by glacier debris, potentially endangering rescue operations downstream.

State-owned engineering and rescue enterprise China Anneng, which has been monitoring the lake since Thursday, dispatched a 15-member team on Friday with reconnaissance ​drones, ​portable satellite stations and mobile surveillance cameras to gather more ​data about the lake.

An overflow from the lake ‌on Friday temporarily halted rescue work before further assessment deemed the risks manageable.

Authorities have also flagged another larger body of water at the bottom of the glacier collapse.

"We estimate its area to be over 120,000 square meters, but its depth is currently unknown," said Chen Hongqi, a senior engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources' Geological Disaster Technical Guidance Center.

Flood risks will remain until the two lakes have fully drained, an official with Nepal's Disaster Management Authority ‌has said.

In bleak rainy weather on Saturday morning, more than 50 ​rescue workers combed through the grey rubble of boulders and mud ​looking for signs of life and calling out ​to any survivors, according to CCTV.

The first team of rescuers and a search-and-rescue dog had ‌made their way to the location of the Gyirong ​border crossing complex on Friday ​afternoon, which they described as having nothing left but ruins.

Dangerous conditions at the main disaster zone, made more complex as roads and communication were cut off, continue to pose challenges to the Chinese relief ​efforts, state news agency Xinhua said.

China's death ‌count from the disaster rose to seven early Saturday, with 554 still missing.

Nearly 500 villagers and ​construction workers, as well as all 555 tourists from the area have been evacuated, Xinhua said.

(Reporting ​by Liz Lee and Yukun Zhang; Editing by Stephen Coates)

title: A Jewish scholar chosen to lead the Catholic Biblical Association is hit by antisemitic backlash
description: When Amy-Jill Levine was a child in Massachusetts, a schoolmate in her predominantly Catholic hometown told her she was guilty of killing Christ because she was Jewish.  Levine has worked to improve h...
fullText:
When Amy-Jill Levine was a child in Massachusetts, a schoolmate in her predominantly Catholic hometown told her she was guilty of killing Christ because she was Jewish.

Her mother reassured her that wasn't the case — and instead of being embittered by the encounter, the young Levine began attending a Catholic catechism class to learn more about her Christian neighbors and their beliefs.

That blossomed into a decades-long academic career in an unusual role — a Jewish scholar of Christian Scriptures. Levine has worked to improve how Christians and her fellow Jews understand each other. She's spoken at many churches and taught students about the ancient Jewish context of Jesus' life and teachings. She's written numerous books, some in tandem with Christian scholars; she and a co-author even presented one book personally to Pope Francis.

But after the Catholic Biblical Association of America announced earlier this month that Levine was elected its first-ever Jewish president, an antisemitic backlash began.

Denunciations appeared in the posts and replies on social media accounts with tens of thousands of followers. Critics called her "anti-Christian," claimed she's trying to hijack Catholicism, denounced Jews for not accepting Jesus, and tacked on anti-Zionist comments.

While some questioned why the association would appoint anyone who wasn't a Catholic, much of the criticism was infused with anti-Jewish statements. They come at a time of rising antisemitism in the country.

Her supporters and longtime Christian collaborators are appalled by the backlash.

"Unfortunately, some neither understand the role of the president nor the nature of a professional society," said a joint statement by the association's executive board chair, Gregory E. Sterling, and executive director, Archie Wright. "She was not elected because she is Jewish, but because she is an exceptional scholar and has played a very important role in Catholic-Jewish dialogue."

The association is made up of Catholic and non-Catholic scholars with the stated purpose of improving the study of the Bible within the context of faith. Levine has been active in the association for decades, though she said when someone from its nominating committee asked her to consider being president, she wasn't sure at first if it was serious. It was — with supporters citing her long history of working with Christian scholars.

The criticisms underscore the need to address antisemitism, the association statement said: "We need to live and practice the values of our faith, values that are not evident in the criticisms." Numerous past presidents of the association signed a similar statement.

The chairman of the committee overseeing interreligious relations for the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops wrote to Levine to congratulate her.

"Your election is a fitting celebration of the genuinely interfaith character of biblical scholarship and of the many years of faithful Jewish-Catholic collaboration in the study of Scripture," said Bishop Joseph Bambera of Scranton, Pennsylvania, adding that it reflects the Vatican's call for Catholics to pursue "deeper understanding and mutual respect with the Jewish people."

Levine, an adherent of Orthodox Judaism, said that although she doesn't accept the Christian belief that Jesus is divine, she admires him as an early rabbinic teacher and believes Christians and Jews can learn much from each other.

"Hate and demonizing, name calling and slandering, are not good forms of evangelism," Levine said on her Facebook page. "And now, ironically again, I have to explain that these nasty posts are not indicative of the best of the Church."

She noted that she often defends the Catholic Church from bigoted statements against it.

"My historical work shows that we do not need to make Judaism look bad in order to make Jesus look good," she said.

She noted, for example, that there are common stereotypes that Jesus was introducing grace and acceptance against a rigid Jewish notion of law and purity. In fact, Levine told The Associated Press, the Bible shows that Jesus affirms Jewish law and "restores people to states of purity."

Levine said the gospel stories would have resonated strongly with ancient Jewish readers. For example, the stories of Jesus' miracles echo those of ancient Israelite prophets. His escape from a murderous tyrant as an infant is similar to that of Moses. When Jesus said the greatest commandments are to love God and neighbor, he was quoting from the Torah rather than inventing something new, she said.

People embrace antisemitic views for various reasons, Levine said: "what they heard from their parents or friends, what they read on the internet, the conflating of certain Israeli policies with the views of all Jews, and what they hear in churches, whether problematic readings from the New Testament or sermons that introduce or reinforce, often because of ignorance and tone-deafness, antisemitic messages."

While Catholicism has had a historic legacy of antisemitism, the Vatican has repeatedly denounced it in the post-Holocaust decades. The reformist Second Vatican Council of the 1960s affirmed the shared "patrimony" of Christians and Jews. It said the death of Jesus cannot be blamed on "all the Jews, without distinction."

St. John Paul II, the longtime pope, prioritized reconciliation with Jews, saying antisemitism "has no justification and is absolutely reprehensible."

Levine is a professor emerita in New Testament and Jewish studies at Vanderbilt University in Nashville, Tennessee. She now teaches part-time at the Hartford International University for Religion and Peace in Connecticut.

She said her role as Catholic Biblical Association president will include promoting excellence in biblical studies and supporting scholars and their research and publications.

She wants to continue speaking in parishes and to work with Catholic bishops "to help ensure that textbooks used in parochial schools, catechesis, and preaching do not promote antisemitic messages, to promote better Jewish-Catholic relations, and to promote the work of the CBA."

Levine's admirers include Protestant as well as Catholic scholars.

Professor Ben Witherington III, a New Testament expert at Asbury Theological Seminary in Kentucky, co-wrote a commentary on the Gospel of Luke with Levine, believed to be the only Gospel commentary jointly written by evangelical and Jewish authors.

"She is profoundly loved by all kinds of Protestant and Catholic folks," he said.

He said Levine regularly put her faith into action, including teaching Bible classes at a Nashville prison.

"She loves Christian people and she loves the Bible," Witherington said. "What she doesn't love is people using the Bible to beat other people over the head, including Jews. I agree with her on that."

title: 3 students stabbed at high school, 14-year-old suspect in custody: Authorities
description: The victims are in stable condition, authorities said.
fullText:
Three 14-year-old students were injured in a stabbing at a Texas high school on Friday, authorities said.

A 14-year-old suspect is in custody in connection with the incident at Americas High School in El Paso, according to the El Paso County Sheriff's Office, calling it an "isolated attack."

Quintuple homicide suspect gunned down his girlfriend and her family, friends: Officials

Authorities received a report of an individual with a knife by the high school's baseball field around 8:30 a.m., according to El Paso County Sheriff's Office Commander Jerome Washington.

Two of the victims were injured while trying to intervene and help the third, he said.

The victims -- two 14-year-old boys and a 14-year-old girl -- were transported to local hospitals with stab wounds and are all in stable condition, authorities said. Two have since been released, Washington said.

"All other students and staff are safe under the supervision of faculty and staff," the Socorro Independent School District said in a statement.

District police took the suspect into custody near the school without incident, officials said. He faces at least three charges for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, according to Washington.

The sheriff's office said it is investigating the incident with assistance from the Texas Rangers and Socorro Independent School District Police Department.

"Our investigators are actively working to determine the circumstances that led to the incident," Washington said at a press briefing on Friday.

The commander said he was unable to confirm if the suspect is a student at the high school.

7th graders tackle knife-wielding student who attacked teacher, sheriff says

The school was placed on lockdown as a precaution while law enforcement secured the area.

Counseling and support services will be made available, school officials said.

"Nothing is more important to us than the safety and well-being of our students and employees," Socorro Independent School District Board President Michael Najera said at the press briefing. "We will continue working closely with law enforcement as the investigation moves forward, while our focus remains on supporting our students, staff, and families."

Texas State Sen. Cesar Blanco said his office is in "close contact" with local and state officials following the incident.

"I am deeply saddened by the senseless violence at Americas High School today," Blanco said in a statement. "I am praying for the students, families, faculty, and staff affected by this incident."

ABC News' Tristan Maglunog contributed to this report.

description: Jose Mourinho says the three-week international break is a “concern” for Real Madrid, with several key players facing a demanding schedule after the World Cup.
fullText:
Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has raised concerns about the impact of September's three-week international break, highlighting the amount of time his players will be away from their club.

"The international break does concern me," Mourinho said. "It's a lot of time."

Speaking before Sunday's home La Liga match against Malaga (16:00 BST), Mourinho said he was mostly troubled by players linking up with their nations who then do not get game time.

"Players who will join their national teams to play don't worry me as much. It's the ones who join the national teams and are not really involved that concern me," he said.

"We'll see how we can go about this and work with the rest of the players. But not having players at my disposal for three weeks is a difficult situation."

The first international break of the 2026-27 men's football season next month will last a week longer than usual, with the traditional October break now scrapped.

In recent years, Fifa has used five primary international breaks during the season, in March, June, September, October and November.

But instead of separate breaks in September and October, there will now be a three-week gap for international fixtures across late September and early October, when countries will play four international matches instead of two. The existing international breaks in November, March and June will remain.

A number of reasons are behind the change, including the 2026 World Cup final being played on 19 July, the latest date for a summer World Cup since 1966. Player welfare and travel considerations were also taken into account when the changes were made.

"I totally respect the players' decisions and I don't want to dramatise too much, but very often they pick up injuries during those breaks and right after returning from an international break," Mourinho explained.

"So it does worry me, but this is the way these things are and we can't do much about it."

The Portuguese has already spoken at length about the World Cup players in his Real Madrid squad, including Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Kylian Mbappe, who have had a demanding summer.

He said the club are working to manage their workload to reduce the risk of injury.

In his pre-match media conference, Mourinho was also full of praise for Bellingham, highlighting his importance to the team beyond his attacking contributions.

"He is a unique kind of player, extremely important for the team," said Mourinho.

"His mental strength, tactical ability, the way he recovers the ball, the way he pressures, the way he plays up front.

"We like talking about Kylian, Vini [Vinicius Jr] and Jude, but I'm really happy with all the players.

"We have great, great players here."

Mourinho also gave his perspective on the Ballon d'Or debate, arguing that winning the Champions League or World Cup should not automatically make a player the favourite for the individual award.

"It's a very beautiful thing individually and that enters into the individual history of a certain player," Mourinho said.

"I think it's normal that there are a dozen players of a very high level, of which we have three or four. It is normal that it exists as an ambition."

Mourinho suggested the prize should be ultimately measured by a player's lasting impact on the game.

"For me, the Ballon d'Or has to be one of those players that when he finishes playing, we miss for eternity," Mourinho said.

"I miss Maradona, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo, Cristiano, Messi, Zizou, Lothar Matthaus - I miss these people.

"You can't give the Ballon d'Or to a player because he won the Champions League or because he won the World Cup. It doesn't have to be from Paris St-Germain or the Spanish national team."

title: Forest in advanced talks to sign Munoz from Palace
description: Nottingham Forest are in advanced talks over a deal worth up to £25m to sign Crystal Palace defender Daniel Munoz.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest are in advanced talks over a deal worth up to £25m to sign Crystal Palace defender Daniel Munoz.

Colombia international Munoz has emerged as late transfer target for Forest boss Oliver Glasner, who worked with the full-back during his time in charge at Selhurst Park.

Talks over the proposed deal have been ongoing for a number of days and have accelerated since Palace's 4-1 defeat by Manchester City on Friday.

An agreement between the two clubs is now understood to be close as Tuesday's transfer deadline nears.

Munoz joined Palace from Belgian side Genk in 2024 and has been a key player for the Eagles in recent seasons, playing a crucial part in the club's historic FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs under Glasner.

The 30-year-old has just under two years left on his current deal and Palace are prepared to sell this summer.

Palace signed Anan Khalaili from Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise earlier this summer and the Israel international is expected to take Munoz's place in Pierre Sage's team.

title: Gibbs-White shines - player ratings for Liverpool v Nottm Forest

fullText:
Liverpool drew 2-2 with Nottingham Forest in Andoni Iraola's first home Premier League game as their new head coach.

Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

Munoz rescues point for Liverpool at home to Forest

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Alisson: Well beaten for Dan Ndoye's goal but made a superb save to deny Igor Jesus on the brink of half-time and keep Liverpool in the game. Poor penalty to give away for Gibbs-White's goal. 5

Jeremie Frimpong: Struggled defensively but got into some good positions going forward. Did really well in the build-up to Florian Wirtz's disallowed goal but was just offside. Has to improve consistency with his end delivery. 6

Jeremy Jacquet: Made a goal-saving challenge to deny Igor Jesus an early goal and was impressive but still had a few moments where he was slack and lacked discipline. 6

Virgil van Dijk: Will be furious with how easily the Liverpool backline was cut open for Ndoye's opener and the ease with which Forest won their penalty. 6

Dominik Szoboszlai: Solid as usual and was much more alert defensively, compared to his display at Newcastle. 6

Alexis Mac Allister: Back in the starting XI and played a lovely reverse ball for Cody Gakpo early on. Couldn't cope physically with Igor Jesus in the build up to Ndoye's goal. 6

Murillo: Unafraid to drive with the ball and put in a solid shift but was well beaten by Munoz for the goal that made it 2-2. Still crucial that Forest keep him. 6

Ola Aina: Relentless all game. Was very involved, as always, and constantly asked questions of Liverpool. Nearly created a goal for Forest. 7

James McAtee: Getting his chance after Elliot Anderson's move to Manchester City and was very tidy on the ball in an impressive performance. Made some really good deliveries in the first half and battled well all afternoon. 7

title: Football fans pay tribute to crash death officers
description: PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision on the A66 near Middlesbrough.
fullText:
Football fans and players have paid tribute to two Cleveland Police officers who were killed in a crash on Teesside.

PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

There was a minute's applause in their memory ahead of Middlesbrough and West Bromwich Albion's Championship match at Riverside Stadium, as pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

On Friday evening Hartlepool United also held a two-minute silence before their home National League game against Eastleigh.

Middlesbrough FC said in a statement prior to the match: "We are also showing our appreciation for the dedication and hard work of both men, and to Cleveland Police force in protecting and supporting our local community.

"The commitment shown by officers and staff, often in challenging and demanding circumstances, plays a vital role in keeping residents safe and helping people feel secure in their homes, neighbourhoods and local areas."

Earlier this week 17 people were arrested in connection with the investigation into the crash bringing the total number of arrests to 24.

The occupants of the other vehicle, a Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17, also died.

Speaking earlier on Radio 4's Today programme, Middlesbrough mayor Chris Cooke said Cleveland Police was doing "extremely well" despite a lack of funding that "they absolutely need".

"They are a police force that has been the hardest hit.

"They've had over 10 per cent reduction in FTE (full-time equivalent) of police officers, while other places have seen over 20 per cent increase, and that isn't fair," he said.

Cooke added police funding should "follow need".

"It cannot just be based on population sizes as it currently is, because that serves no one well," he said.

title: Leader Pogacar abandons Vuelta after crash
description: Race leader Tadej Pogacar pulls out of the Vuelta a Espana after crashing during stage eight of the three-week race.
fullText:
Race leader Tadej Pogacar has abandoned the Vuelta a Espana after crashing during stage eight.

The world champion, who was looking to complete a full set of Grand Tour victories, crashed with about 33km to go.

Pogacar, 27, was riding in the midst of the peloton when he came off his bike, hurting his left shoulder and cutting the left side of his face.

The Slovenian appeared to try and get back on his bike before sitting back down again.

He then walked unaided into an ambulance to mark the first time he has abandoned a Grand Tour.

The six-time Grand Tour winner was on course to win all three of the sport's biggest stage races, having already won five Tours de France and a Giro d'Italia.

The overwhelming favourite to win the three-week long race had started the stage three minutes and 50 seconds clear of the rider in second place.

title: ‘I’m Not Drinking The Kool-Aid Anymore’ — 2-Time Super Bowl Champion WR Completely Turns on Colorado HC Deion Sanders in Fiery Rant
description: Deion Sanders is healthy and focused on helping Colorado rebound from its three-win campaign in 2025. Coach Prime made several roster changes during the offseason in an effort to turn things around, but two-time Super Bowl champion Brandon Stokley remains skeptical about the Buffaloes’ potential.
fullText:
Deion Sanders is healthy and focused on helping Colorado rebound from its three-win campaign in 2025.

Coach Prime made several roster changes during the offseason in an effort to turn things around, but two-time Super Bowl champion Brandon Stokley remains skeptical about the Buffaloes' potential.

Sanders inherited a Colorado program that had gone 1-11 in 2022 and immediately sparked plenty of excitement in his first season. The Buffaloes opened 2023 with a 3-0 record but ultimately finished 4-8, losing eight of their final nine games.

The Buffaloes bounced back in 2024, posting a 9-4 record and becoming one of the most-watched teams in college football. More than 54 million viewers watched Colorado games throughout the 2024 season.

However, Colorado took a major step back in 2025, finishing 3-9 after losing Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter to the NFL.

While quarterback Julian Lewis seems to be showing promise heading into the 2026 season, and footage from the Colorado locker room has fueled optimism about the team's potential, Stokley remains skeptical.

"I'm not drinking the Kool-Aid anymore," Stokley said. "I'm not. Sorry, I was hook, line, and sinker. I loved it when Deion was here when they hired him… That was awesome. The energy, the buzz, the excitement-that was fun… You know what wasn't fun? Last year.

There's been noise around the Sanders family for varying reasons this year.

A federal bankruptcy judge ruled on Aug. 27 that the Colorado head coach must be available to testify remotely in Shilo's upcoming bankruptcy trial at 1:30 p.m. MT on Sept. 4, one day after Colorado begins its season against Georgia Tech.

The judge clarified that Sanders would only need to appear if rebuttal testimony becomes necessary. However, Stokley also questioned the way the situation has been portrayed publicly.

Shilo filed for bankruptcy in October 2023 in an effort to discharge more than $11 million in debt. Almost all of that amount is owed to John Darjean, a former security guard at his school in Dallas, who is the plaintiff in the bankruptcy case.

title: Jürgen Klopp says he didn’t talk to Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala, he sent him a voice memo
description: The Germany boss wants FC Bayern’s Jamal Musiala to get healthy.
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp has offered Jamal Musiala a strong message of support as the Bayern Munich star continues to deal with his latest setback, making it clear that his place in the Germany national team will not be affected by his rehabilitation.

Speaking about his communication with Musiala, Klopp explained that he did not actually call the 23-year-old directly, instead choosing to send him a voice message.

"We didn't speak on the phone. I sent him a voice message. He doesn't know me at all and doesn't have my number. I think if I had called him, he wouldn't have answered for three days because he wouldn't have recognized my number. He responded to the message. He's in a situation that you wouldn't wish on anyone, especially not a young guy like him. But everything should turn out fine, everyone agrees on that. I reassured him that this wouldn't have any impact on the national team," Klopp told Sky Germany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia)."That's all I can do for him. Vincent Kompany confirmed to me that he was in incredible shape. After the metal plate and screws were removed, he was back to his old self, or even better. Now this has happened for the reasons we know.

"What's important now is that he is given the necessary time, and that he gives himself that time as well. Young players normally don't have any problems, apart from becoming impatient, and of course you can't afford to be impatient during a phase like this. He's at the perfect club, in the perfect environment for that, and we also want to do our part. And we're telling him: 'Son, first get healthy, and then the door is open for you.'"

For Bayern Munich, Klopp's comments should provide plenty of encouragement. Musiala's priority remains getting healthy and allowing himself the necessary time to recover rather than rushing his return.

The fact that Klopp has already reassured him that Germany's door remains open is another important message for the Bayern Munich star.

Musiala has already established himself as one of Germany's most important players, and Klopp clearly intends to make him a central part of his plans once he is ready to return.

For now, however, the message from Klopp is exactly what Musiala needs to hear — get healthy first, and everything else can wait.

title: Former Braves Pitcher Punches, Pins Knife-Wielding Man To Protect Players, Per Report
description: “I don’t think I’m a hero,” the former Atlanta Braves right-hander said, shortly after subduing an intoxicated man in a hotel, according to police.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves have employed countless players throughout their long history, from Hall of Fame stars to short-term contributors whose careers in Atlanta were measured in only a handful of appearances.

Kevin Lomon belongs in the latter category, pitching briefly for the Braves in 1996 during a major league career that ultimately lasted just 12 games. Lomon made six relief appearances for Atlanta that season, working seven-and-one-third innings with a 4.91 ERA. He allowed seven hits and three walks while striking out one batter, with his final major league appearance coming on Sept. 28, 1996.

Overall, Lomon pitched 16 2/3 innings, surrendering 24 hits and eight walks while recording seven strikeouts in his career. But nearly three decades later, he has made headlines for a heroic reaction to a violent threat.

Cubs' 2-Year Veteran, Former ROTY And All-Star, Cuts Ties With New Team After Just 3 Games

Lomon is now the head baseball coach at Cameron High School in southeastern Oklahoma. Earlier this month, he was traveling with 13 players for a baseball game in Shawnee when an alarming situation unfolded at the team's hotel.

"An Oklahoma high school baseball coach says he didn't have much time to think when one of his players called from a hotel room saying a man had pulled a knife," Taylor Howard reported for 5 CBS News.

Lomon said that one of his players called him around 9 p.m. after encountering a man in the hotel hallway. The player reported that the man had opened a knife and moved toward him before retreating into his room.

Lomon instructed his players to get inside their rooms and called 911. He then went into the hallway himself.

The police report indicated that Lomon encountered the man near the elevators with an open knife. The man allegedly moved toward Lomon, who punched him several times before holding him on the ground until police arrived.

Yankees' Survivor 51 Contestant Sends Brian Cashman Message In Debut Video

The confrontation ended without physical injuries being reported among Lomon or his players. Police reportedly recovered two knives, while Stevens was arrested on complaints of assault with a deadly weapon and public intoxication, according to Howard.

For Lomon, the decision was less about bravery than responsibility.

"I don't think I'm a hero," Lomon said, per Howard. "I just think I would do it again."

That mindset reflects the role he has embraced long after his brief MLB career ended. As a coach responsible for 13 young players on the road, Lomon viewed protecting them as part of his job.

His former life as a Braves pitcher may have lasted only part of one season, but nearly 30 years later, Lomon found himself facing another high-pressure situation — this time with his young team depending on him to keep them safe.

title: Chiefs Finish Winless Preseason With 9-9 Tie vs. Seahawks
description: The Kansas City Chiefs once again featured field goals in their final preseason game against Seattle.
fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs finished their uninspiring preseason with a 9-9 tie against the Seattle Seahawks, as Seattle kicker Jason Myers missed a 52-yard field goal that would have won the game as time expired.

The tie meant the Chiefs went winless during the preseason with an 0-2-1, which wasn't surprsing given that they scored just a single touchdown in three games.

Both teams sat their starting quarterbacks, as per usual in the third preseason game, with Seattle keeping Sam Darnold on the sidelines and the Chiefs playing without Patrick Mahomes as he continues to shoot for Week 1 while rehabiliting his knee after offseason surgery.

Just two quarterbacks played in this one, with Garrett Nussmeier going 22-for-34 for 198 yards for Kansas City and Jalen Milroe going 16-for-26 for Seattle.

The first half was a battle of field goals with the Chiefs getting a pair of Harrison Butker chip shots from less than 30 yards, while Myers had one from 46 yards out to make it 6-3 at halftime.

Seattle scored the lone touchdown of the game in the third quarter on a four-yard pass from Milroe to Nick Vanett, but Myers missed the extra point to make it 9-6. Kansas City then tied the game at 9-9 on another short field goal from Butker to make it 9-9, and Seattle's final drive stalled to force the missed field goal that left it a tie.

Chiefs linebacker R Mason Thomas had a strip sack and a fumble recover, and he probably expressed the thoughts about the possibility of bonus preseason football.

"I thought we were going to overtime," he said in an ESPN/AP report, "but it was nice to get a tie."

Thomas was more excited about the Chiefs opener against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead on Sept. 14, as it will be the first game of the season featured on Monday Night Football.

"It's going to be packed out, at night in the loudest stadium in the in the whole NFL," Thomas added. "I'm excited."

The Chiefs did get several noteworthy performance despite their overall sluggish offense. Andrew Armstrong caught five passes for 52 yards in his bid to make roster, and rookie running back had a nice game with 39 yards on seven carries for a 5.6 yards per carry average.

Brashard Smith had 72 yards on 16 carries as running back Kenneth Walker III sat out this one after sustaining a foot injury in practice during the week.

title: Scottie Scheffler comments on what Ludvig Aberg is really like as a playing partner
description: Scottie Scheffler played alongside Ludvig Aberg during the second round of the Tour Championship on Friday. Scheffler posted a solid second-round 67, while Aberg carded a 68 at East Lake.
fullText:
Scottie Scheffler played alongside Ludvig Aberg during the second round of the Tour Championship on Friday.

Scheffler posted a solid second-round 67, while Aberg carded a 68 at East Lake.

The 30-year-old world number one is just two strokes adrift of the lead heading into the weekend, with the Swede a further shot back.

While Scottie Scheffler and Ludvig Aberg would both prefer to be leading, they will be happy with their positions after two rounds of the Tour Championship.

Aberg enjoyed playing with Scheffler on day two at the Tour Championship, with both players moving at a good pace around East Lake.

Now Scheffler has opened up on what Aberg is like to play alongside.

Scheffler spoke to the media at East Lake late on Friday night after a practice session alongside his coach Randy Smith.

The world number one was asked what Ludvig Aberg was like to play with on day two of the Tour Championship.

"He's an easy guy to get paired with," Scheffler replied.

"He's a really nice guy. He's a great competitor, good player as well. He's always very easy to be on the golf course with.

"It's pretty simple to be paired with him."

Scheffler is paired with Cam Young for the third round of the Tour Championship, while Aberg will play alongside Adam Scott.

Scheffler has missed both tee shots out to the right on the opening hole this week, and has been forced to lay up both times on the long par-four.

During the final round of the Tour Championship in 2025, Scheffler actually hit his opening drive out of bounds to the left.

And he was asked after his second round yesterday if the right miss is now in his head.

"I mean, there's an out-of-bounds fence on the left," he said.

"Didn't really hit too bad of a shot there. Then you get a lie there that you can't advance more than 80 yards.

"No, I wouldn't say anything is in my head out there. Thank you, though."

title: Jose Mourinho sees only one position for Real Madrid captain
description: As Real Madrid’s captain, Federico Valverde has been one of the first names on the team sheet for several years now. Yet, he has barely ever stayed fixated on a single position.Despite being one of ...
fullText:
As Real Madrid's captain, Federico Valverde has been one of the first names on the team sheet for several years now. Yet, he has barely ever stayed fixated on a single position.

Despite being one of the team's most important players over the years, the Uruguayan star has been used as a Swiss-knife by manager after manager who have all praised him for his versatility.

As a result, he has played as a full-back, a defensive midfielder, an attacking midfielder and even a winger based on the requirement of the team.

As reported by MARCA, the new Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho is not a fan of Valverde being used all over the field. He sees the player as a midfielder and a midfielder only, specifically a deep-lying midfielder at that.

Valverde has started the season well. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

The player, after all, has started off the team's games so far this season and has played as part of the double pivot on both nights alongside Bernardo Silva. He has enjoyed a strong start to the season, and his numbers speak volumes.

Against Real Sociedad, the player made three defensive actions, two recoveries and one interception.

He was not dribbled past in the entire game, won two duels and completed 93% of his passes. Beyond his defensive numbers, he assisted Kylian Mbappe and had two shots on goal.

It is clear at this point that Mourinho sees Valverde only as a midfielder, especially since he now has convincing options at full-back and on the right wing.

How will Mourinho incorporate Tchouameni? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The central midfield is where the manager sees the player's output to be the highest.

Part of the reason why Valverde has had a non-turbulent start to the season, however, is the injury Aurelien Tchouameni is suffering from.

The Frenchman has been the club's de facto pivot player for a long time now and was expected to be the manager's preferred option to partner Silva in the double pivot.

His absence helped the Uruguayan earn Mourinho's favour and move up the pecking order. Tchouameni's return, however, is not far off and it remains to be seen how the selection changes after he is back in action.

title: Updated De’Zhaun Stribling Fantasy Outlook 2026: Is the 49ers Rookie a Diamond in the Rough?
description: De’Zhaun Stribling enters the 2026 season with a clear path to targets following extensive roster turnover and injuries in the 49ers’ offense. While he is not a plug-and-play fantasy starter for Week 1, his impressive preseason performance makes him a high-upside depth piece with midseason breakout potential as a rookie.
fullText:
De'Zhaun Stribling enters the 2026 season with a clear path to targets following extensive roster turnover and injuries in the 49ers' offense. While he is not a plug-and-play fantasy starter for Week 1, his impressive preseason performance makes him a high-upside depth piece with midseason breakout potential as a rookie.

Stribling turned heads during the summer, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 109 yards through the first two weeks of the preseason after generating plenty of buzz at camp. That strong summer performance has been a sight for sore eyes in San Francisco, a team battling the injury bug before a single live bullet is fired.

Ricky Pearsall (PCL) is out for the season, creating a vacancy in the receiving rotation from the jump. Meanwhile, veteran Mike Evans has his best football behind him, and Deebo Samuel enters the year after the NFL essentially told us that his time as a viable asset is nearly over after no team showed interest until August.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

Christian Kirk is coming off an inefficient season and has struggled to remain on the field, though I'm not sold he was destined to be a real piece of this offense anyway. While George Kittle continues to make great strides, his playing style and age is a tough combination to feel great about over the four-plus month grid that is the NFL regular season.

This leaves the offense in a last-man-standing situation. Christian McCaffrey and Kittle will certainly absorb a significant share of the targets, but they can't carry the entire passing attack on their own. When the front office drafted Stribling, the move was widely viewed by most as a reach. That selection proved the organization was significantly higher on his prospect profile than the general scouting public, and his summer has only reinforced those internal beliefs.

Playing in a Kyle Shanahan system led by Brock Purdy provides Stribling with upside in the efficiency department, as that tandem ranks among the most consistent in football.

For me, he represents a smart process buy in drafts. You should not rely on him as a weekly fantasy starter right away, but once your starting lineup is filled, he serves as a viable depth target who could realistically transition into a weekly lineup staple by the middle of the season.

The price is on the rise, so be careful, but there seems to be some fire at the bottom of this preseason smoke.

title: Broncos kicker Wil Lutz close to hitting impressive PAT streak
description: Denver Broncos kicker Wil Lutz is one extra point away from 100 consecutive converted PATs.
fullText:
There isn't anything flashy about Denver Broncos placekicker Wil Lutz. He doesn't have the strongest leg in the NFL and his name won't come up when fantasy football players want the league's top kicker. But one thing he has proven to be is consistent.

Consistency is exactly what coach Sean Payton was looking for when he traded for Lutz, his former kicker in New Orleans. That consistency also helped Lutz get a three-year contract extension from the team last year.

Lutz has currently made 99 consecutive PATs for the team, something that is no longer a given in today's game. Several teams have cycled through multiple kickers over the last several years, while the Broncos have had just one guy, whose job security is not threatened.

"[I have] a lot of pride, and I don't mind talking about it," Lutz said of his streak. "I think it's a cool feature. This game is decided by, if you look at the stats, it's like something like 75 percent of games are decided by three points. So I take just as much pride in the extra point as I do a 55-yarder in the third quarter. It's important.

"I think you saw in the Giants game, one point changes the entire approach of the game. So that comes from preparation and not having a lazy swing in those moments. It's the kick you're going to hit the most in the season. So it's making sure you're locked in for all 70, 60 extra points you're going to have. Hopefully we can keep that going."

Lutz referenced the wild comeback the Broncos had against the New York Giants last season, in which Giants kicker Jude McAtamney missed two extra-point kicks in that game, which the Broncos won 33-32.

Lutz's streak of 99 straight makes is the top active streak in the league. Tyler Bass of the Buffalo Bills made 104 straight from 2020 to 2022. Justin Tucker made 112 straight for the Baltimore Ravens from 2015 to 2018.

The all-time NFL record, which will likely never be touched, is 523 in a row, held by Stephen Gostkowski of the New England Patriots between 2006 and 2016. However, most of those kicks were made from the old 20-yard range, where you rarely ever saw a miss. The league changed it to a 33-yard kick in 2015, which changed the success rate quite a bit.

If he makes his first PAT attempt this season, Lutz will hit 100 makes in a row, which is certainly an impressive achievement.
